item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 1 (Sep. 2013)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Adam Christianson from the Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Steve Stanger from the Mac Roundtable Podcast - @tmasteve

This first episode focuses on the Apple eBook price-fixing case, the release of the iPhone 5C & 5S, and the release of iOS 7, but it also touches on other stories including the terrible month Blackberry have had, the announcement of the Surface 2 by Microsoft, and Martha Stewart's suit against Lodsys.

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP1-Sep2013.mp3"]

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 2 (Oct. 2013)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots

Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots

  • Peter Upfold - @PeterUpfold
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner

This episode starts with some updates on the Apple eBook case and Black Berry's launch of BBM for iOS and Android. The main focus for this episode is on so-called Patent Trolls, some dirty tricks by Samsung and others, the October Apple event, and OS X Mavericks.

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP2-Oct2013.mp3"]

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 3 (Nov. 2013)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Allison Sheridan from the NosillaCast Podcast - @podfeet

This episode starts with some updates on iWork, Mavericks Mail, and Backberry. The main topics for this episode are the Rockstar consortium suing Google, the Apple -v- Samsung damages retrial, Apple & Google's transparency reports, Tim Cook's WSJ op-ed in favour of gay rights, and the end of the Stack Rank at Microsoft. The show finishes with a lightning run through some other stories of note for the month that didn't quite make the grade to become a full segment.

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 4 (Dec. 2013)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Allister Jenks - @zkarj
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
  • Guy Serle from the My Mac Podcast - @Macparrot

This episode starts with some updates to stories from last month including news about the Supreme Court of the US taking up a potentially important patent case, and Google starting the fight back against the Rockstar Consortium. The main topics for this episode are the battle of wills between court-appointed-monitor Michael Bromwich and Apple, some developments in legal war between Apple & Samsung damages retrial, a raft of good numbers for Apple over the holiday season, Apple's deal with China Mobile, some NSA-related Apple stories, and Tim Cook's on-going campaigning for equality. The show finishes with a quick run through some other stories from the month that might have important ramifications in future, including a possible change of direction within Microsoft, and our first glimpse at the direction USB 4 is heading.

Segment Start Times:

  • 00:03:43 - Followup from LTA3
  • 00:06:50 - Apple -v- Michael Bromwich
  • 00:16:00 - Samsung -v- Apple
  • 00:28:28 - Good Holiday Numbers for Apple
  • 00:45:10 - Apple & China Mobile
  • 00:46:30 - Apple & the NSA
  • 00:52:06 - Tim cook's On-going equality campaigning
  • 00:57:58 - 'Quick' Stories

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP4-Dec2013.mp3"]

  • Bob Kohn's 5-page cartoon Amicus Brief in the eBooks case
  • Tim Cook's Speech at Auburn University
  • Tim Cook's Letter to all Apple employees

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 5 (Jan. 2014)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Nick Rodriguez from The Mac Gist - @NickRodriguez

This episode starts with a quick rundown of some interesting numbers released in January, followed by a quick rundown of the month's developments in some of the many court cases Apple are involved in. The main stories the show focuses on are Apple's settlement with the FTC over in-app purchase, Apple's release of more specific NSA numbers, the continued improvements to the Mac version of iWork, Apple's 2014 Q1 earnings report, a few related Google stories, and the Mac's 30th birthday. The show finishes with a few quick stories including Apple's acknowledgement of the iOS crashes some users are experiencing, Apples's pledge not to discriminate against the long-term unemployed, and some bad news for Microsoft.

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 6 (Feb. 2014)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Scott Willsey from The Pocket Sized Podcast - @scottaw

Joining Bart this month are Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast, Nick Riley & Scott Willsey of the Pocket Sized Podcast. The show starts with a quick rundown of some interesting numbers released in February, followed by a quick rundown of the month's developments in some of the many court cases Apple are involved in. The main stories the show focuses on are the 'goto fail' bug, Microsoft's new CEO, Samsung's new product releases, an interesting bunch of hires by Apple, and some interesting politics/civics moves by Apple, including pressuring the Arizona governor to veto a bill legalising discrimination, and Tim Cook shooting down a right-wing climate-change-denying think-tank at the share holders meeting. The show finishes with a few quick stories including the pre-launch of CarPlay, Sony getting out of the PC business, and a handful of small bad-news stories for Microsoft.

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 13 (September 2014)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh

The show starts with a quick summary of some developments relating to Apple's many on-going court cases, then the panel get stuck into the month's main stories. First the September Apple event with it's new iPhones, Apple Pay, and Apple watches, then iOS 8, then some changes to iCloud, and finally a discussion of Apple's updated privacy policies and their big media push to differentiate themselves from their competitors when it comes to privacy. The show ends with a quick rundown of a few other notable September news stories.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP13-September2014.mp3"]

Links:

Legal Stories
  • Apple denied re-trial in Apple -v- Samsung 2 - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple & Google appeal Judge Koh’s throwing out of the $324M settlement negotiated by the companies with lawyers for the affected employees in the no-poach case (reminder - judge Koh rules last month that the amount was too low) - arstechnica.com/…
  • Appeals court throws out $368M ruling in Virtex -v- Apple patent case, sends it back to the lower court - arstechnica.com/…
  • so-called ‘patent troll’ ordered to pay Apple & others legal fees when the wireless patents they were suing the companies for were ruled invalid - www.macobserver.com/…
Main Story 1 - September Apple Event
  • One-stop-page with all the important links: www.macobserver.com/…
  • New iPhones
    • iPhone 6 & iPhone 6 Plus (4.7” & 5.5”) - loopinsight.com/…
    • Record sales - 10M in first weekend - om.co/…
    • Initial release did not include China, but will come to China on October 17 - www.macobserver.com/…
    • ifixit tear the new phones apart and find they are surprisingly repairable - arstechnica.com/…
    • DXOMark rate the 6 and 6plus the best smartphone cameras - www.dxomark.com/…
    • Square Trade gives iPhone 6 their highest ever Drop Test score - www.macobserver.com/…
    • The internet goes nuts about bendy iPhones - www.macrumors.com/…
    • Apple releases statement saying they test the phones and there is no problem, say there have only been nine returns - www.loopinsight.com/…
    • Apple show journalists the lab where they torture iPhones - www.theverge.com/…
    • Assuming you didn’t try to bend your iPhone, Apple will replace your bent iPhones - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Consumer Reports weighs in - phones are not too bendy - www.consumerreports.org/…
    • Cult of Mac post a gallery of bent smartphones from a variety of manufacturers - www.cultofmac.com/…
  • Apple Pay - arstechnica.com/…
    • US-only (at first) contact-less payment validated with touch ID to launch in October
    • Reports say Apple will get fees from banks - www.bloomberg.com/…
    • Walmart say they won’t be taking part - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Chase on the other hand send out mailing bragging that they will be supporting it - www.loopinsight.com/…
    • Although Apple Pay use NFC, the NFC chip in the new iPhones will only be for Apple Pay (at least for now) - arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple preview Apple Watch - arstechnica.com/…
    • post-keynote Apple say the battery life is expected to be about a day - arstechnica.com/…
    • XKCD weighs in - xkcd.com/…
Main Story 2 - iOS 8 Released
  • new OS out - www.apple.com/…
  • Third party keyboards become all the rage - www.macobserver.com/…
  • iOS 8 brings some App Store improvements:
    • Family sharing now available - www.macstories.net/…
    • App Bundles now available - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple TV gets and update to bring it in line with iOS 8 features - www.macobserver.com/…
  • After a short delay, health kit apps arrive in the app store - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Note that iOS 8 is a security update, if your phone can’t run it, then it’s time for an upgrade - www.intego.com/…
  • iOS 8 comes with more location privacy options - www.cnet.com/…
  • iOS 8 security updates make law enforcement cranky, or as Gruber put it, law enforcement endorse Apple security - daringfireball.net/…
    • Google announce they’ll follow suit with Android L - daringfireball.net/…
  • iOS 8.0.1 update did not got well - apple quickly followed with 8.0.2 to fix the problem
Main Story 3
  • Apple announce new iCloud plans with more storage for less money, and now up to 1TB - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple refund existing customers the balance for the remainder of their payment period - www.macobserver.com/…
  • iOS and Windows users get to enjoy new iCloud Drive, but Mac users have to wait a little longer - arstechnica.com/…
Main Story 4 - Apple release new privacy policy
  • the new policy - www.apple.com/…
  • Tim Cook pen Jobs-like letter on privacy - www.apple.com/…
  • Tim Cook hammers the privacy point during a Charlie Rose interview (“follow the money”) - www.loopinsight.com/…
Quick Stories
  • Apple finally discontinue the iPod Classic - www.macworld.com/…
  • Apple hires:
    • Apple hires Marcela Aguilar (from GAP) as their new director of global marketing Communications - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple hires famous free-lance designer (and friend of Jony Ive) Marc Newson - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Samsung pull out of EU laptop market (including Chrome books) - www.pcadvisor.co.uk/…
  • Larry Ellison announces his retirement from Oracle - www.businessweek.com/…
  • Microsoft to layoff another 2,100 and axes their silicon valley R&D centre - www.reuters.com/…
  • Amazon cut the Fire Phone by $200 to free on contract - www.macobserver.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 14 (October 2014)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Guy Serle from the My Mac Podcast - @Macparrot
  • Bren Finan - @BrenFinan

The show starts with a quick run-down of some Apple-related numbers released in October, followed by an updated on some of the legal cases Apple is involved in. The four main topics for the show are Apple's October iPod and Mac event, the release of OS X Yosemite, the roll out of Apple Pay, and Tim Cook's coming out letter. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple related stories that made the news in October.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP14-October2014.mp3"]

Links:

Noteworthy Numbers:
  • Apple released their Q4 2014 earnings report this month: www.apple.com/…
    • The raw numbers:
    • Revenue: $42Bn ($37.5Bn YAQ)
    • Profit: $8.5Bn ($7.5Bn YAQ)
    • Gross Margin: 38% (37% YAQ)
    • iPhone Sales: 39M (34M YAQ)
    • iPad Sales: 12M (14M YAQ)
    • Mac Sales: 5.5M - up 21% (4.5M YAQ)
    • It’s another record quarter! - http://www.macobserver.com/tmo/article/apple-posts-a-record-september-quarter-42.1-billion-revenue-8.5-billion-ear
  • Samsung Also Release Earnings:
    • Early in the month Samsung warned earnings would be below expectations - recode.net/…
    • When they released their earnings later in the month, they hit a 3 year low, profits down 61% year on year - www.nytimes.com/…
    • RELATED - A scathing take-down of ‘the church of market share’ - techpinions.com/…
Legal Latest:
  • As weird as it sounds, an anti trust case over iPod DRM will go to trial - arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple win summary judgement against LTE patent claims by WiLAN - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple win GPNE patent case, call company a Patent Troll (they tried to assert their Pager patents were infringed on by iPhones because they allow 2-way communication) - www.macobserver.com/…
Main Stories:
  1. Apple Event
    • iPads
    • iPad Air 2 - Touch ID, thinner, faster - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple quietly introduce Apple SIM - the idea being that you can use the same SIM with multiple carriers (Verison don’t take part) - www.macobserver.com/…
      • AT&T lock Apple SIMs to their network if you connect to it (T-Mobile & Sprint do not) - http://arstechnica.com/apple/2014/10/att-locks-multi-carrier-ipad-sim-t-mobile-and-sprint-leave-it-open/
    • Apple release 5K iMac - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Clever graphic shows original Macintosh screen resolution on new 5K iMac screen - thingsofinterest.com/…
    • Updated Mac Mini - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Mac Mini server goes away - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Developers will get WatchKit SDK in November - www.macobserver.com/…
  2. OS X 10.10 Yosemite is released - arstechnica.com/…
    • This release now allows Apple’s Continuity to work between iOS and OS X
    • Nice article explaining how to enable SMS Relay (letting your Mac or iPad send and receive SMS messages on behalf of your iPhone) - www.macobserver.com/…
    • This release makes iCloud Drive available to Mac users
    • Yosemite was accompanied by updates to iWork - www.macobserver.com/…
    • The WSJ trigger some controversy with some very poor reporting on the new Spotlight
    • A good rebuttal to the original WSJ piece - www.theverge.com/…
    • A good, clear description of what Spotlight does from Security Researcher Rich Mogul - tidbits.com/…
    • Bart’s take in the whole thing - www.bartbusschots.ie/…
    • USEFUL - instructions for making a bootable USB installer for Yosemite - arstechnica.com/…
    • USEFUL - list of Macs that can run Yosemite - www.macobserver.com/…
  3. Apple Pay Launches
    • A nice comprehensive review of Apple Pay - arstechnica.com/…
    • A good description of how Apple Pay (and Google Wallet) work - arstechnica.com/…
    • Just days after launching Apple Pay becomes the leader in contactless payments - daringfireball.net/…
    • An un-expected battle between Apple Pay and CurrentC kicks off:
    • A nice description of CurrentC - techcrunch.com/…
    • Walmart explain why they don’t support Apple Pay - www.businessinsider.com/…
    • A blogger explains that unlike CurrentC, Apple Pay is accessible - stevensblog.org/…
    • CVS & Rite Aid move to kill NFC to prevent Apple Pay being used in their stores. Point to the coming of CurrentC next year - daringfireball.net/…
    • CVS say they “can’t” take Apple Pay - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Not all CurrentC members do the same - Meijer defies the trend - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Anti-trust lawyers express concern that depending on the communications between currentC and its merchants, there could be anti-trust problems for CurrentC - www.loopinsight.com/…
    • Rather embarrassingly, a flaw in the CurrentC API lets hackers steam customer email addresses - arstechnica.com/…
    • Wells Fargo bank enticing customers to use Apple Pay with $10-20 Credits - www.macrumors.com/…
    • RELATED - Apple published an updated iOS Security Guide which contains details on how Apple Pay works - images.apple.com/… (PDF)
  4. Tim Cook Comes Out
    • The Coming out OpEd - www.businessweek.com/…
    • An eloquent explanation of why it matters - www.theverge.com/…
    • RELATED - days before Tim was inducted into the Alabama Academy of Honour, and called for progress on LGBT rights in his acceptance speech - www.macobserver.com/…
Quick Stories:
  • The Techno Watch space continues to hot up:
    • FitBit join the watch fray with Surge watch and fitness tracker - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Microsoft join the fitness tracking game with Fitness Band - www.macobserver.com/…
  • After MUCH drama, Apple and bankrupt Sapphire manufacturer GTAT agree to part ways ‘amicably’ - arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple release online iPhone Activation Lock Status Checker to make it easier to avoid buying stolen iPhones - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Ireland to phase-out “Double Irish” tax loophole used by US multinationals like Apple (will keep corporate tax rate low) - www.nytimes.com/…
  • HP to split into two companies - a business oriented one selling networking equipment, servers, software, and services; and one selling printers and PCs - www.nytimes.com/…
  • Christian Bale has been cast as Jobs in the up-coming Sorkin movie

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 15 (November 2014)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
  • Stefaan Lesage from the Tech45 Podcast (Dutch) - @StefaanLesage

Joining Bart this month are Chick Joiner from Mac Voices, Nick Riley, and Stefaan Lesage from the Tech45 podcast.

The show starts with a quick run-down of some Apple-related numbers released in November, followed by an update on some of the legal cases Apple is involved in. The five main topics for the show are the Masque 'vulnerability', the on-going GTAT saga, developments in the Steve Jobs movie, some Apple Watch updates, and Nokia's return to the mobile device market. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple related stories that made the news in November.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP15-November2014.mp3"]

Links:

Numbers
  • Data from Custora shows that Apple dominated mobile Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales - 77% and 79% respectively (down about 5% from last year, with the balance going to Android) - appleinsider.com/…
Legal
  • Apple ordered to pay $23.6M to MTel for infringing old pager patents - arstechnica.com/…
  • Judge Cote approves Apple’s e-book settlement with the states - arstechnica.com/…
  • RELATED - Apple’s appeal of their ebook conviction goes to court on the 15th of December, Eddie Cue has started a media offensive putting Apple’s side of the case already - fortune.com/…
  • Google settle patent-case brought against them by the Apple-backed Rockstar Consortium - www.macobserver.com/…
  • RELATED - Cisco to pay $188M to settle it’s Rockstar lawsuit - arstechnica.com/…
  • NOTE: The iPod class action suit and Samsung’s appeal of Apples’s victory in their patent trial both started in court early in December, a few days before we recorded this show, but we’ll save those discussions for the December show, when we’ll know more about how the cases are panning out.
Main Stories

  1. Masque - the ‘vulnerability’ that isn’t

    • iOS digital signatures work - apps from untrusted developers trigger a warning which users must accept to run the app, media reports this as a ‘vulnerability’ - Apple was quick to point this out - www.macobserver.com/…
    • The technology at the heart of Masque and WireLurker (see last month’s show) is the same - iOS’s Enterprise Provisioning Profiles. Intel’s Mac Security Blog explains the technology and why there is no vulnerability here - http://www.intego.com/mac-security-blog/masque-attack-ios-vulnerability-or-feature-by-design/
    • The correct take-away from the Masque story is that users should not accept unexpected provisioning profiles, the same as last month with WireLurker

  2. GTAT Saga Continues

    • SEC launch investigation into GTAT trading activities - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Unsealed documents show GTAT painting Apple as a bully negotiator - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Gruber’s pithy summary - daringfireball.net/…
    • Apple tells Mesa (AZ) city officials it plans to re-purpose the GTAT factory, saving some jobs (no details on what they will use it for or how many jobs) - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple writes to GTAT creditors and blames GTAT’s failure to deliver Sapphire on mismanaged production - www.macobserver.com/…
    • GTAT Creditors want to question Apple SVP of Operations Jeff Williams, Apple are not making him available - www.macobserver.com/…

  3. Steve Jobs Movie Drama

    • Christian Bale is not playing Jobs after all - www.telegraph.co.uk/…
    • Universal have taken the movie from Sony (reportedly for $30m) - www.hollywoodreporter.com/…
    • Michael Fassbender is reportedly playing Jobs - www.dailyedge.ie/…
    • Natalie Portman is reported to be in negotiations to play a major part in the film - deadline.com/…

  4. Apple Watch

    • Apple release WatchKit APIs - developers can now start developing for the Apple Watch - developer.apple.com/…
    • Gruber points to some highlights in the Apple Watch HIG - daringfireball.net/…
    • Apple updated their Apple Watch pages with a lot more detail and pictures (but no price or launch date) - www.apple.com/…
    • RELATED - Kairos launch an interesting indiegogo for a smart watch band to make any watch smart - www.macobserver.com/…
    • POSSIBLY RELATED - Apple have followed through on their plans to remove FitBit from Apple stores - www.macobserver.com/…

  5. Nokia Returns

    • Microsoft may have bought Nokia’s mobile devices business, but they didn’t buy the whole company, or it’s brand. Nokia announced it plans to allow other manufacturers license the Nokia brand - http://www.theverge.com/2014/11/17/7233173/nokia-brand-licesnsing-plans
    • Nokia unveiled their N1 tablet - an iPad mini clone that runs Android - http://www.theverge.com/2014/11/18/7239709/nokia-n1-tablet-price-release-date
    • The cloning doesn’t stop at the hardware - dailyexhaust.com/…
Quick Stories
  • Office for iOS goes free-to-use and becomes universal - http://arstechnica.com/apple/2014/11/office-for-ipad-goes-free-to-use-now-supports-the-iphone-too/
  • Apple release too to fix vanishing SMS messages issue when people move from an iPhone to another device - nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
  • Square want to bring Apple Pay to small businesses - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple add UnionPay to Chinese App Store - blogs.wsj.com/…
  • Apple support World AIDS Day 2015 by donating a portion of Black Friday sales, and added a product RED section to the App Store - www.loopinsight.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 16 (December 2014)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Victor Cajiao from the Artechulate Podcast - @victorcajiao
  • Allister Jenks - @zkarj
  • Guy Serle from the My Mac Podcast - @Macparrot

The show starts with a quick update on some stories from November, a run-down of some Apple-related numbers released in December, and an update on some of the legal cases Apple is involved in. The five main topics for the show are the BBC Horizon documentary on Apple's supply chain, Apple & IBM releasing their first apps together, a 14-day trial period for app purchase in the EU, on-going Apple Pay momentum, and the business orld's honouring of Tim Cook. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple related stories that made the news in December.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP16-December2014.mp3"]

Links:

Quick Followups
  • GTAT Developments
    • Apple agrees to less from GTAT to keep bankruptcy proceedings on track - www.macobserver.com/...
    • GTAT wants to pay executives $6M in bonuses despite being in Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple raised $20M for product RED with it's campaigns last month - www.macobserver.com/...
Notable Numbers
  • Having stagnated a while, Apple's dashboard show iOS 8 use on the rise again, now at over 2/3 - arstechnica.com/...
  • Analyst estimates that Android profit is down by half for 2014 - recode.net/...
    • RELATED - Samsung closes London flagship store because of falling sales - www.theverge.com/...
  • According to mobile analytics firm Flurry Analytics, Apple sold a little over half of the smartphones activated world-wide between December 19 and 25 - arstechnica.com/...
  • Business Insider released an interesting infographic showing where Apple makes its money - businessinsider.tumblr.com/...
Legal Latest
  • Apple's appeal of its eBooks price fixing conviction goes to court - two if the three judges SEEM to see things Apple's way during questioning - asking why the DOJ did not investigate Amazon with their market dominance - www.macobserver.com/...
  • The iPod Anti-Trust Case:
    • Judge rules last plaintiff did not buy a qualifying iPod - orders prosecution to find a new plaintiff - www.macobserver.com/...
    • A new plaintiff is found allowing the case to continue - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Jury finds Apple not-guilty in the iPod DRM case (an appeal is promised) - www.theverge.com/...
  • On the basis of a US Supreme Court ruling, a judge has dismissed a lawsuit Apple employees had filed demanding they be paid for the time they spend in forced security checks - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Rockstar Consortium will sell off most of its remaining patents in a move seen as a further de-escalation of the on-going patent war in the mobile sector - www.macobserver.com/...
Main Stories
  • The BBC exposes abuses in Apple's supply chain, Apple Fights Back:
    • BBC releases "Apple's Broken Promises" as part of their Horizon documentary series - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple respond strongly - www.telegraph.co.uk/...
  • The Apple+IBM Partnership yields its first apps - arstechnica.com/...
  • EU App Store customers get free trials by the back door - all purchases (except for gift vouchers) can now be returned within 14 days for a no-questions-asked refund (brings Apple inline with EU directives) - arstechnica.com/...
  • Apple Pay Momentum Continues:
    • More banks and retails sign up to Apple Pay - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Cards with Apple Pay support not represent 90% of US transaction volume - arstechnica.com/...
    • Disney World accepting Apple Pay from December 24th - www.macobserver.com/...
    • An Apple job posting hints at worldwide expansion of Apple Pay - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Rumours/Leaks suggest Apple is in negotiation with UK banks to bring Apple Pay to that country, but at least one bank appears to be reluctant to share the amount of information Apple is looking for - www.macobserver.com/...
    • RELATED - Samsung reported to be working on an Apple Pay competitor - recode.net/...
  • The Business world honours Tim Cook:
    • The FT names Tim Cook person of the year - www.ft.com/...
    • CNN names Tim Cook CEO if the year - www.macobserver.com/...
Quick Stories
  • Apple patch NTP bug in OS X automatically - this is the first time Apple have pushed an update to users systems pro-actively - arstechnica.com/...
  • Apple adds PayPal support to online store - thenextweb.com/...
  • Blackberry releases a 'new' phone - www.bbc.com/...
  • TAG Heuer announces plans for a mechanical smart watch - www.macobserver.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 17 (January 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh

The show starts with a quick correction from last month's show, then moves on to look at some of the many numbers and statistics released in January before moving on to a quick rundown of some Apple-related legal stories. The big stories for the month were Apple's spectacular first quarter, David Cameron's attack on secure messaging apps, the Thunderstrike vulnerability, Microsoft's preview of Windows 10, and some staff changes at Apple. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple related stories that made the news in January.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP17-January2015.mp3"]

Links:

Correction from LTA 16
  • Bart: I confused the BBC current affairs program Panorama with the BBC documentary series Horizon - it was Panorama who did the hit job on Apple, not Horizon. I should have known that because Horizon have created some of my favourite science and maths documentaries!
Notable Numbers
  • Android dominated 2014 with 1.1Bn devices shipped - www.macobserver.com/...
  • two months after release Android Lolipop adoption is so low it doesn't even show in Google's own numbers - www.extremetech.com/...
  • About half of Macs now running Yosemite - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Swift jumps 46 places in RedMonk programming language rankings - www.loopinsight.com/...
  • Apple is the No.2 camera manufacturer on Flickr - between Canon at 1 and Nikon at 3 - petapixel.com/...
  • Mac Growth stomps PC growth again - 18% growth and 7.1% global share - www.macobserver.com/...
Legal Latest
  • Apple, Google & Co, up their offer in the anti-poaching case to $415M - www.macobserver.com/...
  • After 2 years of failed negotiations, Apple and Ericsson go to court over LTE patents - www.macobserver.com/...
  • A judge has dismissed a class action suit claiming Apple knowingly sold MacBook Pros with defective motherboards - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Monster sues Beats over Apple acquisition - www.macobserver.com/...
Main Stories
  1. Apple post record first quarter results - www.apple.com/...
    • Summary:
    • Revenue: $74.6Bn - up from $57.6Bn YAQ (consensus estimate was $63.5Bn)
    • Earnings: $18Bn - up from $13.1Bn YAQ
    • Earnings per share: $3.06 - up from $2.07 YAQ (consensus estimate was $2.60)
    • Gross margins: 39.9%
    • iPhones Sold: 74.5M (analysts expected about 69M)
    • The most profitable quarter for any company ever - http://techcrunch.com/2015/01/27/apple-just-had-the-biggest-quarterly-earnings-of-any-company-ever/
    • Apple have sold their billionth iOS device - http://www.macobserver.com/tmo/article/apple-ios-device-sales-top-1-billion-units
    • Apple changed the categories they report on, giving out less info than before - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple Pay already dominating contactless payments - more than 2 out of three contactless payments in US are Apple Pay. Apple Pay coming to more places, including vending machines soon - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Tim Cook says iWatch will ship in April - www.macobserver.com/...
    • RELATED - Apple takes top luxury gifting spot in China - www.reuters.com/...
    • RELATED - Samsung mobile profits plunge 64.2%, iPhone 6 blamed - appleinsider.com/...
    • RELATED - Apple tied with Samsung for global smartphone units in Q4 2014 - www.macobserver.com/...
  2. David Cameron launches a war on private communication - www.independent.co.uk/...
    • Obama expresses support - blogs.wsj.com/...
    • RELATED - Apple dramatically increases it's lobbying in Washington - www.macobserver.com/...
  3. Thunderstrike - the first know Mac Bootkit
    • researchers announce the uber-rootkit that allows malware to infest a Mac's firmware - nakedsecurity.sophos.com/...
    • Apple patch the bug in OS X 10.10.2 - www.intego.com/...
  4. Microsoft Previews Windows 10 - www.cnet.com/...
    • HOLOGRAMS - arstechnica.com/...
    • focus on Universal Apps to allow better integration between phone and desktop - arstechnica.com/...
    • Windows 10 to be free to Windows 7 & 8.1 users - arstechnica.com/...
    • Good bye IE, hello Project Spartan - arstechnica.com/...
    • Cortana coming to the Desktop - arstechnica.com/...
    • in-home Xbox One streaming - arstechnica.com/...
    • Microsoft to turn Skype into their own version of iMessage - www.theverge.com/...
    • Preview version coming to desktops now, phones in February - arstechnica.com/...
  5. Apple Exec News
    • SEC filing details Apple executive pay - www.imore.com/...
    • Apple hires another former Burberry exec - Chester Chipperfield comes to Apple for 'special projects' - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple hires HP veteran for Corporate Sales - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Mickey Drexler retires from Apple's board - www.macobserver.com/...
Quick Stories
  • Apple buy music analytics firm Semetric - www.macobserver.com/...
  • The Aaron Sorkin Steve Jobs movie is actually happening - filming has stated, and Fassbender will play the lead - www.macobserver.com/...
    • RELATED - filming starts in the garage of Jobs' childhood home - www.cnet.com/...
  • Apple re-vamps free on iTunes - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Blackberry's latest 'hail mary' - bastardise net neutrality - arstechnica.com/...
  • It emerges that the reason there was no finger print scanner in the Nexus 6 is that Apple were smart enough to buy AuthenTec - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Samsung to take on Apple Pay with Samsung Pay - www.macobserver.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 18 (February 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh

The show starts with a quick look at some of the many Apple-related numbers and statistics released in February before moving on to a quick rundown of some Apple-related legal stories. The big stories for the month were the explosion of iCar rumours, the release of Photos (to be discussed in more detail next month), iCloud for all, three major green building projects for Apple, and some interesting Apple hires. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple related stories that made the news in February.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP18-February2015.mp3"]

Links:

Notable Numbers
  • iPhone profit share rises to record level (~89%), while Android dropped to a record low (~11%) - appleinsider.com/...
    • RELATED - Samsung reportedly ready to ditch Japanese Smartphone market due to dwindling sales - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple market valuation reaches $750B - more than 2x the value of any other company - medium.com/...
  • A drop in smartphone thefts in London (-50%), NYC (-25%) & San Fran (-40%) suggests that 'kill switches' in Smartphones are having the desired effect - www.reuters.com/...
  • Email tracking firm reporting that more than half of all emails opened in the UK are opened on an Apple device - www.engagecustomer.com/...
Legal Latest
  • Reporting by the WSJ alleges that Michael Bromwich, the antitrust monitor appointed by Judge Coté in the ebook price-fixing case that Apple is appealing, has committed 'major abuses' against Apple - appleinsider.com/...
  • Ericsson sue Apple after failing to reach agreement on renewing a patent license - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple lose patent case to Smartflash LLC in Texas - Apple will appeal and are calling Smartflash Patent Trolls, Smartflash object to this - www.macobserver.com/... & arstechnica.com/...
Main Stories
  1. iCar - rumours exploded in January that Apple are making a car
    • Business Insider initially reported on a strange Apple-owned car driving around with cameras on it. This reportedly prompted an Apple Employee to email them to say that Tesla employees are jumping ship to work on an Apple project that is too good to pass up and will give Tesla a run for their money - www.businessinsider.com/...
    • The Financial Times of London really started the ball rolling with a report that Apple was working on a car and that the project was being headed by a former Mercedes-Benz exec, who 9to5Mac are naming as Johann Jungwirth - www.macobserver.com/...
    • WSJ report that Apple has a staff of 'several hundred' working on a car under the code-name 'Project Titan' - arstechnica.com/...
    • Bloomberg report that Apple want to start producing the car as soon as 2020 - www.bloomberg.com/...
    • 9to5 Mac run down a list of Apple's car-related-hires - 9to5mac.com/...
    • A123 Systems sues Apple for poaching car battery engineers - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple add cars to their business description in Switzerland - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Recent Apple Hire Mark Newson created a concept car for Ford in 1999 - www.macobserver.com/...
  2. Photos
    • Apple add photos preview to website and release a beta version of the App to developers - www.apple.com/...
    • Apple confirmed that Aperture will be removed from the MAS when Photos is released to the public - www.macrumors.com/...
    • Since the second of March so can the public via the OS X 10.10.3 public beta - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Since the public beta is only just out - we'll save this topic until the March show
    • Apple show-case best of iPhone photography - www.apple.com/...
  3. iCloud for Everyone - Apple take iCloud out of beta and open up a limited service to anyone with an Apple ID - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple's support page for iCloud - support.apple.com/...
  4. More Green Apple Building Projects
    • Apple will inbest $2Bn to convert the failed GTAT sapphire plant into a global 'Command and Control' data centre that will be powered by 100% renderable energy, from a new local solar farm - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple to invest $848M in a new Solar Farm in Monterey County, CA - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple to invest €1.7Bn in new European data centres (one in Athenry in Ireland, and one in Denmark), both will be entirely powered by green energy - www.apple.com/...
  5. Notable Apple Staff Changes:
    • Apple Retail Realestate VP Bob Bridger set to retire - www.macobserver.com/...
    • BBC Radio 1 DJ Zane Lowe joins Apple - www.bbc.co.uk/...
    • Chris Breen leaves Macworld to join Apple - www.macobserver.com/...
Quick Stories
  • Apple dropped from China's government buy list - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple turns to Pinterest for easier app discovery - www.macobserver.com/...
  • iOS9 will reportedly focus mainly on stability and performance (not confirmed by Apple) - arstechnica.com/...
  • Apple launch repair program for 2011 MBPs with GPU problems - arstechnica.com/...
  • Apple will publish first public iOS8 beta in March - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple have announced a media event titled "Spring Forward" on the 9th of March - www.apple.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 19 (March 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh

The show starts with a quick look at some Apple-related numbers and statistics released in March before moving on to a quick rundown of some Apple-related legal stories. The big stories for the month were the Spring Forward Apple Event, and the new Steve Jobs book Becoming Steve Jobs.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP19-March2015.mp3"]

Links:

Noteable Numbers
  • Gartner say Apple beat Samsung in World-Wide Smartphone unit sales in the December Quarter - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Tim Cook announced that Apple have sold 700 million iPhones - www.macobserver.com/...
Legal Latest
  • Judge Lucy Koh gives preliminary approval to the updated $415M settlement in the Apple, Google, Intel & Adobe anti-poaching suit - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Developments in the A123 Employee Poaching law suit filed against Apple last month:
    • 4 March - Court Filings Show Apple is working to reach a settlement with A123 after being sued for hiring their battery engineers last month - www.macobserver.com/...
    • 11 March - Apple file to have the suit dismissed for lack of evidence - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Second US Circuit Court of Appeal sides with Apple and questions the actions of Michael Bromwich, the antitrust monitor imposed on Apple by Judge Denise Coté - www.macobserver.com/...
  • A Jury in Texas clears Apple of infringing on wireless patents owned by Canadian patent licensing firm Conversant Intellectual Property Management - www.reuters.com/... & www.macobserver.com/...
Main Stories
  1. The Spring Forward Apple Event
    1. American Apple TV owners get exclusive new HBO Chanel, and Apple TV gets a price-drop - www.macobserver.com/... & www.macobserver.com/...
      • Apple's exclusivity is not going to be long-lived, Sling TV will get HBO ahead of Game of Thrones too - www.macobserver.com/...
    2. A science tool no one expected - ResearchKit - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Research Kit Added to Apple's Open Source page - developer.apple.com/...
      • Days after the event Thousands have already signed up for Research Kit projects - www.bloomberg.com/...
      • The inside story of how ResearchKit came to be - fusion.net/...
    3. A Mac some expected - an all-new ultra-thin MacBook - www.macobserver.com/...
      • only two ports - a headphone jack, and a USB-C port
      • iPad-esque battery life
      • 12" retina display
      • New Butterfly-mechanism ultra-tin keyboard
      • New haptic track pad
      • available in the three iPhone colours
      • Other Macs also silently updated with spec bumps, and the addition of the Haptic Trackpad to some models - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Hands-on of New MacBook by Ars Technica - arstechnica.com/...
      • A good description of USB-C is - arstechnica.com/...
      • Rich Mogul at TidBITS corrects some of the FUD doing the rounds about USB-C - tidbits.com/...
      • A good analysis of Apple's roll in developing USB-C - 9to5mac.com/...
    4. Three Watches we all Expected
      • No new features announced
      • Apple Watch Pricing ranges from Reasonable to insanely expensive - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Apple Watch Sport - 38mm = $349, 42mm = $399
      • Apple Watch - 38mm = $549, 42mm = $599
      • Apple Watch Edition - $10,000 and up
      • In-store previews from 10 April, release date of 24 April - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Rob Griffiths release a great chart showing all the Apple Watch options and their prices - robservatory.com/...
      • Apple Care for Apple Watch prices have also been announced, ranging from $59 for the Sport, to $999 for the Edition - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Guided Tour videos showing the Apple Watch UI have been added to Apple's site - www.apple.com/...
      • Small print on the Apple Website revealed the Apple Watch is rated IPX7, which means it is water proof to 1m for 30 mins - daringfireball.net/...
      • The Apple Watch battery is replaceable, but not by end-users - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Apple's celebrity beta tester for the Apple Watch, Christy Turlington-Burns says the Apple Watch accurately tracks workouts without an iPhone - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Apple Watch gets FCC approval - www.macobserver.com/...
      • A great behind-the-scenes look at the Apple Watch's development from WIRED - www.wired.com/...
      • A great analysis of Apple's Apple Watch manufacturing videos by a manufacturing expert - atomicdelights.com/...
      • Apple patent a special type of Gold containing ceramics - this is NOT used in the Apple Watch Edition, but is very cool - leancrew.com/... & daringfireball.net/...
  2. Becoming Steve Jobs - a new Steve Jobs Biography by Brent Schlender and Rick Tetzeli is released
    • The book is getting a lot of praise from those who knew Steve IRL - e.g. Eddy Cue say this is the first book to really 'get' Steve - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple release a free podcast of an 'At The Apple Store' event where Jon Gruber interviewed the authors - itunes.apple.com/...
Quick Stories
  • April 1st was Apple's 39th Birthday - Happy Birthday Apple!
  • Mark your Calendar - Apple will release their Q2 earnings on the 27th of April - www.macobserver.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 20 (April 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Allison Sheridan from the NosillaCast Podcast - @podfeet
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz

It was a busy month in Apple news so the show jumps straight into the main stories, starting with some first-hand experiences with the Apple Watch, then moving on to Photos, then the Q2 earnings call, and then quickly finishing up with some Apple Pay news and some news from Microsoft's Build conference.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP20-April2015.mp3"]

Links:

Main Stories
  1. The Apple Watch Hits the Market (online only, and only in some countries)
    • Apple watch sold out in less than 6 hours - www.macrumors.com/...
    • Preordered ESTIMATED to be 2.3million, but very much supply-constrained - appleinsider.com/...
    • A leaked Apple memo states that there will be no in-store Apple Watch sales until after May - www.telegraph.co.uk/...
    • During Apple's Q2 earnings call, Time Cook said the Apple Watch would likely be available in more countries in late June - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple's rollout of the Apple Watch has been unusual, and Apple are coming under some fire for it. In a leaked video to Apple employees, Angela Ahrendts explains Apple's reasoning for the unusual launch - www.macobserver.com/...
    • While developers are allowed to develop for Watch Kit, there are limits on what developers can do.
      • 3rd party watch apps (as in apps that present a watch face) are not permitted - nakedsecurity.sophos.com/...
    • Consumer Reports scratch-test the Apple Watch - sapphire is stronger than glass, but both are very scratch resistant - www.loopinsight.com/...
    • iFixit teardown shows that replacing the Apple Watch battery is easy, but replacing the brains of the device is not - arstechnica.com/...
    • Unconfirmed reports suggest manufacturing problems with the taptic engine are behind Apple watch shipment delays - apparently two factories were supposed to manufacture the components, but those made by one of the factories were found to be unreliable - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Reportedly, the problem was discovered before any watches were shipped to customers - daringfireball.net/...
    • Ship Dates for Apple Watch Sport slip to July - www.macobserver.com/...
    • The sensors on the back of the Apple Watch don't appear to be able to see through tattoos - www.cultofmac.com/...
  2. Photos Is Released - www.macobserver.com/...
  3. Q2 2015 Earnings Call: Apple reports record second quarter results - www.apple.com/...
    • The Numbers:
      • Revenue: $58Bn ($45.6Bn YAQ)
      • Profit: $13.6Bn, or $2.33 per diluted share ($10.2Bn, or $1.66 per diluted share YAQ)
      • Gross Margins: 40.8% (39.3% YAQ)
      • International Sales accounted for 69% of revenue
      • 61.2M iPhones sold (up 40%)
      • 12.6M iPads Sold (down 23%)
      • 4.6M Macs Sold (up 10%)
    • To put all this on context, Kieran Healy from Duke University released a great chart showing Apple Sales numbers since mid-2006 - this long-term view helps to separate the signal from the noise - kieranhealy.org/...
    • Apple increases dividend by 11% (to $0.52 per share) and expands shareholder returns to $200Bn - www.macobserver.com/...
    • During the call Tim Cook said Apple plans to be part of coming big changes in media - www.macobserver.com/...
    • RELATED - Samsung released a new investor forecast projecting a 30% drop in Q1 profits (this is being spun as good news because the rate of decline is shrinking) - appleinsider.com/...
  4. Apple Pay News:
    • Discover coming to Apple Pay this Fall - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Best Buy to accept Apple Pay, despite allegiance to CurrentC/MCX - arstechnica.com/...
  5. Microsoft Build Conference
    • Microsoft to update their developers tools to allow Objective C and Java code to be used when building Windows 10 apps - the idea being to allow iOS an Android apps to be more easily ported to Windows - social.techcrunch.com/...
Quick Stories
  • Apple Staff Changes:
    • Randy Ubillos (of iMovie & Final Cut fame) retired from Apple this month - daringfireball.net/...
    • Steve Dowling promoted to VP Communications (he had been acting since Katie Cotton's retirement) - www.apple.com/...
    • Natalie Kerris leaves Apple PR - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Dolby VP Mike Rockwell has joined Apple - www.macobserver.com/...
  • At least one Russian politician is still not over the Apple U2 giveaway - he wants it investigated as a pro-gay propaganda (you really can't make this shit up) - www.macobserver.com/...
  • A bug un American Airlines software flight bag app results in delayed flights (and a lot of people and media blaming the iPad and/or Apple for bad software written by others) - https://nakedsecurity.sophos.com/2015/04/30/ipad-crash-grounds-dozens-of-american-airlines-flights/
  • Apple & IBM's partnership continues to expand:
    • IBM intros Watch Health Cloud with Apple HealthKit support - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Japan Post team up with Apple and IBM to improve their service for monitoring the elderly by giving them iPads running IBM software. This is part of a paid service the postal service runs to check in on elderly people while they are on their rounds - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Mark your calendar - WWDC 2015 will run June 8 through 12 - www.macobserver.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 21 (May 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Bren Finan - @BrenFinan

The show starts with a quick roundup of some of the court-related Apple news for May 2015, before jumping into the main stores of the month. First, a promotion for Jony Ive, then a roundup of the some of the news around Apple Watch, then the demise of the perennial Apple TV rumour, and finally, the banishment of the much maligned discoveryd, and the return of mDNSResponder.

The show finishes with a quick roundup of some other important Apple-related news that broke in May, including some small tweaks to the Mac line, some more big US retailers moving towards Apple Pay, and Microsoft's announcement of plans to bring Cortana to iOS.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP21-May2015.mp3"]

Links:

Legal Latest
  • OpenTV file a patent suit against Apple and Samsung - unlike most patent cases against Apple, OpenTV actually use their patents, and, have existing licensing deals with companies like Disney, Google & Cisco - www.macobserver.com/...
  • The US Court of Appeals has upheld the ruling that Samsung copied Apple, but has struck down the financial penalties over trade dress that formed part of the billion dollar ruling, reducing what Samsung owes Apple to 'just' $550M - www.macobserver.com/... & arstechnica.com/...
  • The fight between Apple and Ericsson heats up, spreading from the US to the UK, Netherlands & Germany - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple end the employee poaching suit filed against them by battery company A123 with an out of court settlement - www.macobserver.com/...
  • The US Second Court of Appeals rejects Apple's request to remove Antitrust Monitor Bromwich, scolds Apple for not using the proper appeals process, and has some harsh criticisms for Bromwich - www.macobserver.com/... & fortune.com/...
Main Stories
  1. Jony Ive promoted to Chief Design Officer
    • The news was announced in a rather odd way, as part of a Steven Fry piece for the British newspaper The Telegraph - www.telegraph.co.uk/...
    • 9to5Mac get a copy of Tim Cook's email to all staff about the promotion - 9to5mac.com/...
    • For context, Gruber looks at Apple's history of C-level titles - they've had very few - daringfireball.net/..., plus a correction - daringfireball.net/...
  2. Apple Watch Developments
    • Tim Cook says Apple Watches will be in stores by June - 9to5mac.com/...
    • Consumer Reports ranks the Apple Watch as best of the 11 smart watches it tested - 9to5mac.com/...
    • Apple Watch gets it's first update, inducing bug fixes AND security fixes - www.macobserver.com/... & www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple release new Guidelines for developers, and launches official 'made for Apple Watch' program 3rd party band manufacturers - www.macobserver.com/... & 9to5mac.com/...
    • Jeff Williams (SVP of Operations) tells Walt Mossberg on-stage at the Code conference that a native Apple Watch SDK is coming at WWDC - techcrunch.com/...
    • The internet has a collective hissy-fit and tries to turn the fact that the Apple Watch does not have a feature no other watch has into some kind of scandal - there is no activation lock on Appple Watch, but doing a factory reset WILL wipe your data - arstechnica.com/...
    • Researchers point out that if a thief can steal your watch very quickly and get their finger under the sensors in less than 1 second, then Apple Pay will remain active on the watch, so, if your watch gets stolen, it's probably a good idea to disassociate all credit cards using the Apple Watch app on your iPhone - nakedsecurity.sophos.com/...
  3. It's about as official as it's like to get - Apple are not working on a full television
    • Events seem to have been triggered by and open letter to Apple from activist investor Carl Icahn which confidently predicted a TV on the way - www.shareholderssquaretable.com/...
    • Then the WSJ report that Apple were working on a TV, but abandoned the project some time ago - arstechnica.com/...
    • Long-time Apple-TV-Faithful Gene Munster admits he was wrong about the TV - www.cnbc.com/...
  4. Apple throws in the towel on the disastrous discoveryd
    • The underlying reason for many of OS X 10.10 Yosemite's foibles is the introduction of a new networking daemon called discoveryd which replaced the old mDNSResponder daemon. - furbo.org/... (NSFW!)
    • The latest beta of OS X 10.10.4 is dicveryd-free, and mDNSResponder is back - 9to5mac.com/...
Quick Stories
  • Apple Tweaks it's product lineup:
    • Existing 5K iMac price dropped from ¢2,499 to $2,229, and new entry level model added for just $1,999 - www.macobserver.com/...
    • MacBook Pro with retina gets some spec bumps, and a force-touch trackpad - www.macobserver.com/...
  • More good news for Apple Pay (and bad news for CurrentC)
    • HomeDepot drop unofficial Apple Pay support, say they want in officially now - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Target CEO Brian Cornell says he wants Apple Pay in his stores - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple's relationship with IBM continues to grow
    • Apple starts adding Apple Watch support to some enterprise Apps being sold through their partnership with IBM - 9to5mac.com/...
    • IBM employees can now choose a Mac or a PC - 9to5mac.com/...
  • Apple, Google, Yahoo!, Facebook, Twitter, the EFF, security exerts and others write an open letter to President Obama arguing strongly against back doors - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Microsoft Announces that Cortana is coming to iOS & android - www.macobserver.com/...
  • The first trailer for the Aaron Sorkin film 'Jobs' has been released - 9to5mac.com/...

Reminder - WWDC starts on June 8 with a Tim Cook keynote at 10am PST - developer.apple.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 22 (June 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
  • Steve Stanger from the Mac Roundtable Podcast - @tmasteve
  • Victor Cajiao from the Artechulate Podcast - @victorcajiao

The show starts with a quick roundup of some of the court-related Apple news for June 2015, before jumping into the main stores of the month. First, some Home Kit News, then the news from Apple's World Wide Developer Conference, then the 'confederate flag' kerfuffle in the App Store, and finally a collection of privacy-related stories including the EFF's 'who has your back' report.

The show finishes with a quick roundup of some other important Apple-related news that broke in June, including some staffing changes at Apple, a recall of Beats speakers, and a replacement program for 3TB iMac hard drives.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP22-June2015.mp3"]

Links:

Legal Latest
  • Apple loses it's appeal of the eBooks Case - arstechnica.com/...
  • Apple tries to the turn the table on a so-called 'patent troll', asking a federal court to order Unwired Planet to pay Apple's legal fees (USD15m) for the case they lost against Apple - www.macobserver.com/...
  • The European Commission launch investigation into Amazon's eBook distribution arrangements - europa.eu/...
Main Stories
  1. Home Kit
    • Support Docs on Apple's site confirm that Apple TV 3rd ten and newer can act as hubs for HomeKit devices - www.macrumors.com/...
    • HomeKit compatible devices starting to ship from Ecobee, Elgato, iHome, Insteon & Lutron - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Philips Hue will get HomeKit support this fall - www.macobserver.com/...
  2. WWDC
    • Diversity on display
      • on the eve of the keynote, Tim Cook said the lack of diversity in tech is 'our fault' - mashable.com/...
      • the keynote itself saw the most diverse Apple crew
    • OS X 10.11 El Capitan - www.macobserver.com/...
      • All Macs that run Yosemite will run El Capitain, but not all will have metal - www.macobserver.com/...
    • iOS 9
      • If your device can run iOS 8, it can run iOS 9 - arstechnica.com/...
      • multitasking on iPads - www.macobserver.com/...
      • better Siri - www.macobserver.com/...
      • New iCloud Drive app - www.macobserver.com/...
      • App Thinning to improve the experience for users of 8Gb and 16GB devices - arstechnica.com/...
      • To help install OS updates, apps can be temporarily deleted and then automatically re-installed - arstechnica.com/...
      • PINs being bumped to six digits to improve security - arstechnica.com/...
      • Content blocking API added, seems to be aimed more at performance and privacy than ad blocking - www.baldurbjarnason.com/...
      • Android Migration Assistant - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Watch OS 2 - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple Pay - uk.businessinsider.com/...
      • Coming to UK in July - www.macobserver.com/...
      • RELATED - Apple release tech document explaining Apple Pay Verification - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple News
      • A new app for iOS - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Swift goes Open Source - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple Music - www.macobserver.com/...
      • A streaming music Service
      • MUCH confusion over DRM - iMore explain what is actually happening - www.imore.com/...
      • iCloud Music Library confusingly similar to iTunes Match - arstechnica.com/...
      • A radio station
      • How to request songs - www.macobserver.com/...
      • A social network for musicians
      • Before it even went live, there were already anti-trust investigations underway
      • The Attorneys General New York Connecticut are investigating Apple's deal with the labels - www.nytimes.com/...
      • Controversy over Apple Music terms, especially the non-payment of any fees to artists during the free trial
      • Indie labels say Apple Music will put them out of business - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Taylor Swift sends an open letter to Apple - taylorswift.tumblr.com/...
      • Apple back down, artists will be paid the same as they get on Spotify during the free trial - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Apple's response also convinces previously sceptical indy labels to come onboard - www.macobserver.com/...
      • In an interview with Billboard, Eddie Cue says Taylor Swift's letter 'solidified' Apple's thinking - www.billboard.com/...
      • RELATED - Taylor Swift's draconian photography contract comes under fresh criticisms - The Irish Times boycotts photos for her Dublin concert - petapixel.com/...
      • The service went live on June 30
      • Early reviews are OK - www.macobserver.com/...
      • No Sonos support on launch, but coming 'soon' - www.macobserver.com/...
      • New apps:
      • iTunes 12.2 is now out adding Apple Music to Macs & Windows PCs - www.macobserver.com/...
      • iOS 8.4 brings Apple Music to iOS - arstechnica.com/...
      • Useful Apple Music Links:
      • Apple Music: what you need to know - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Apple Music FAQ - www.imore.com/...
      • 14 (More) Apple Music Tips - www.computerworld.com/...
  3. Apple gets caught up in the "confederate flag" controversy
    • Tim Cook Tweets his views on 'symbols and words' that feed racism - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple starts removing apps that use the rebel flag, even in historically accurate contexts like civil war games. Some apps seem to be coming back, but there is a lot of confusion - arstechnica.com/... & www.macobserver.com/... & www.macobserver.com/...
    • RELATED - the so-called 'confederate flag' is not actually the flag of the confederated states of America - www.cgpgrey.com/...
  4. Apple get top marks, again, in this year's annual EFF who has your back report - www.macobserver.com/...
    • RELATED - Tim Cook gave a blistering speech on privacy - Weakening Encryption Harms Good People - social.techcrunch.com/...
    • RELATED - Edward Snowden calls Apple 'pioneering' in privacy, and calls on consumers to support Apple - if protecting privacy is profitable, more companies will do it - www.macobserver.com/... & www.macobserver.com/...
Quick Stories
  • OS X 10.10.4 released
    • discoveryd really is dead! (and with it about 300 bugs in Apple's 'radar' bug tracking system) - daringfireball.net/...
    • TRIM can now be enabled on 3rd party SSDs - arstechnica.com/...
  • Apple Staffing Changes
    • Lisa Jackson's role has been expanded from VP for the environment to VP of environment, policy, and social initiatives - www.washingtonpost.com/...
    • Apple release new staff Bios, and surprisingly, Alan Dye (new VP of UI design) and Richard Howarth (new VP of industrial design) report directly to Tim Cook, and not to Jony Ive - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple recalls Beats Pill XL over fire-safety fears - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple announces replacement program for 3TB HDs in 2012 and 2013 iMacs - arstechnica.com/...
  • Batteries are now eligible for replacement under Apple Care+ when they drop below 80% of original capacity - up from 50% previously - arstechnica.com/...
  • RIP Original iPad Mini - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple released iBooks Author 2.3, adding the ability to create books that can be read on iPhones - www.macobserver.com/...
  • The first real trailer (non-teaser) for the Job movie has been released - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Woz says the dialogue in the jobs movie is fiction, but he loves it anyway - www.bloomberg.com/...
  • Apple's Q3 earnings call has been scheduled for 21 July - www.macobserver.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 23 (July 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Bren Finan - @BrenFinan
  • Victor Cajiao from the Artechulate Podcast - @victorcajiao

The show starts with a look at some interesting Apple-related numbers and statistics released during July before moving on to the legal news and some followups from last month's show (mainly Apple Music related). The three main stories for the month are Apple's 3rd quarter earnings, the new iPod Touch, and a collection of security-related stories. The show finishes with a quick roundup of some other short Apple-related stories that broke in July.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP23-July2015.mp3"]

Links:

Notable Numbers
  • Safari offers better battery life on OS X than any other browser - www.macobserver.com/...
  • WSJ reports that millennials are watching dramatically less TV than older generations - http://blogs.wsj.com/cmo/2015/07/24/this-chart-shows-why-comcast-would-be-interested-in-vice-media-and-buzzfeed/
  • iOS now bigger than Wintel - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple makes 92% of smartphone profits, on less than 20% of smartphone sales - arstechnica.com/...
Legal Latest
  • Authors and book sellers demand US DoJ anti-trust investigation of Amazon - daringfireball.net/...
Followups
  • Apple Music
    • Eddie Cue says Home Sharing might be back - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple releases iTunes 12.2.1 to address the DRM bug some people experienced with Apple Music - www.macobserver.com/...
    • RELATED - an interesting explanation of the problem's cause - www.mcelhearn.com/...
    • iMore explain why most Beats 1 shows can't be podcasts (in a word, licensing) - www.imore.com/...
    • US Senator Al Franken sends an open letter to the FTC asking them to investigate Apple Music - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple Music can't be listened to on traditional iPods (any iPod other than the Touch) - www.imore.com/...
  • Apple Pay Launches in the UK - www.apple.com/...
Main Stories
  1. Apple Q3 Earnings - www.apple.com/...
    • The numbers:
      • Revenue: $49.6Bn (up from $37.4Bn YAQ)
      • Net Profit: $10.7Bn (up from $7.7Bn YAQ)
      • Earnings per Share: $1.85 (up from $1.28 YAQ)
      • iPhone Unit Sales: 47.5m (up 35% from 35.2m YAQ)
      • iPad Unit Sales: 10.9m (down 18% from 13.2m YAQ)
      • Mac Unit Sales: 4.7m (up 9% from 4.4m YAQ)
    • No actual Apple Watch numbers released, but Tim Cook says Apple Watch it doing very well - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Tim Cook still 'bullish' on iPad - www.macobserver.com/...
    • As noted by Gruber, Apple shares of course went down on a record quarter, while the business press didn't bat an eye-lit over MS's $2.1Bn quarterly loss - daringfireball.net/...
  2. A new iPod Touch - www.macobserver.com/...
    • 500% faster CPU, 900% faster graphics - arstechnica.com/...
  3. Apple & Security - a mixed bag
    • iOS 9 & OS X 10.11 el Capitan will switch from Two-Step authentication, to a new fully OS-integrated Two-Factor authentication which Apple say will be more streamlined - http://www.macobserver.com/tmo/article/os-x-el-capitan-beefs-up-security-with-new-two-factor-authentication-system
    • Thunderstrike 2 - rootkit that uses thunderbolt accessories to spread - no physical access needed this time - arstechnica.com/...
    • 0-day exploit in OS X comes under active attack (a worryingly amateurish mistake, patched in 10.11, but not yet back-ported to 10.10) - arstechnica.com/...
Quick Stories
  • OS X el Capitan & iOS 9 public betas released - arstechnica.com/... & arstechnica.com/...
    • For the first time, Apple have disabled App Store reviews from devices running the iOS beta - arstechnica.com/...
  • The White House launched the American Business Act on Climate Pledge, and Apple was one of the first to sign - www.whitehouse.gov/...
  • Apple & other tech companies support LGBT Non-Discrimination Act - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple & Samsung working together on electronic SIM standard - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple hired Doug Betts, a car expert formerly from Fiat Chrysler - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Another trailer for another Jobs movie - Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine - iheartapple2.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 23a - Analysts Explained (Special 1)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Lynda Gousha - @llg4cdg

Joining Bart for this first special show is Lynda Gousha, a listener who knows a heck of a lot more about the financial markets than Bart does! This is the first of what will probably be an on-going but sporadic series of special shows. The idea for the special shows is that they will not be about Apple News, but about something that helps us understand Apple news.

This show is all about the financial markets - who are the players, what drives their actions, what are their goals, and, most importantly, what does all the jargon actually mean?!

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP23a-Special1.mp3"]

Links:

  • Link 1 - what buy-side analysts say about Apple
  • Link 2 - who holds Apple stock
  • Link 3 - who is selling Apple stock
  • Bonus link (not mentioned in show) - stock market history (video series)

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 24 (August 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Dr. Robert Carter from the Tech Doctor Podcast - @robert_carter

The show starts with a quick look at some interesting numbers and a quick review of the month's legal news before getting stuck into the six main stories of the month: Apple's Deal with Cisco, Google's transformation into Alphabet, some developments in mobile payments, some developments in smart watches, Tim Cook's somewhat controversial email to Jim Cramer, and the Galaxy Note 5's flawed stylus. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other shorter stories that made the news in August, including the demise of the Amazon Fire Phone.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP24-August2015.mp3"]

Links:

Notable Numbers
  • iMore survey shows very high levels of usage by Apple Watch owners (93% wear it 5 days a week or more, and 95% for 8 hours a day or more) - www.imore.com/...
Legal Latest
  • The European Commission says Apple's streaming music deals did not violate EU antitrust laws - www.macobserver.com/...
  • US Federal Court of Appeals reject's Samsung's latest appeal - Supreme Court or bust now! - www.mercurynews.com/...
  • Judge Koh slashes the attorney fees in the Apple 7 co. Anti-poaching settlement - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple loses to Samsung in Germany's highest court - www.macobserver.com/...
Main stories
  1. Apple does a deal with Cisco - www.computerworld.com/...
  2. Google becomes Alphabet - googleblog.blogspot.com/...
    • The legal ins-and-outs get tricky though! - daringfireball.net/...
    • Google also move to a new logo - daringfireball.net/...
  3. Mobile Payments Developments:
    • PayAnywhere comes onboard with Apple Pay - www.macobserver.com/...
    • CurrentC backer Rite Aid stops blocking Apple Pay, and gets on board with it - http://9to5mac.com/2015/08/11/rite-aid-apple-pay-currentc-blockade-over/
    • CurrentC's launch plans may be slipping - could be delayed till next year - recode.net/...
    • RELATED(ish) - Apple joins the NFC forum and takes a seat on the board - 9to5mac.com/...
  4. Smartwatch developments:
    • Swatch Pick a fight with Apple
      • CEO calls Apple Watch a 'toy' - www.macobserver.com/...
      • Register a trademark for "one more thing" and 'tick different' - www.patentlyapple.com/...
      • Swatch say 'one more thing' was a reference to Columbo, not Steve Jobs (and tick different then?) - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Android Wear comes to iOS - sort of - arstechnica.com/...
    • Samsung release their Tizen-based Gear S2 smartwatch
      • A nice side-by-side video review against Apple Watch - www.loopinsight.com/...
      • Gruber's take on it - daringfireball.net/...
  5. Tim Cook emails Jim Cramer in an attempt to calm the markets, but, some say he may have broken US SEC rules in so-doing - www.reuters.com/... & www.marketwatch.com/...
  6. Samsung's Galaxy Note 5 comes under serious fire as a fundamental design flaw comes to the fore - if you insert the S-Pen (stylus) the wrong way around, you will feel no resistance or any other hint you should not do this, and then the device will clamp onto the pen in such a way that you have to damage your phone to get it out again. Samsung's response - RTFM! - arstechnica.com/...
    • Leo Laporte demonstrates just how bad this flaw is live on air as he accidentally does it to his own phone - www.loopinsight.com/...
    • some compare this to Antenna Gate, holding your phone wrong didn't do permanent damage to your device! - daringfireball.net/...
Quick Stories
  • Some Staff Changes at Apple
    • Ian Rogers, who was in charge of Apple Music, leaves Apple - www.macobserver.com/...
    • We now know he left for LVMH - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple hires Nick Thompson, a former MS lead audio engineer on HoloLens - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Apple hires Jamie Carlson, a senior engineer, away from Tesla - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple quickly smacks down rumours that it is setting up an MVNO - www.theverge.com/...
  • Amazon extinguishes their Fire phone - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Apple have announced a media event for 9 September - www.apple.com/...
    • All the usual devices will be able to stream the event, but so will Windows 10 users this time - www.macobserver.com/...

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 25 (September 2015)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Allison Sheridan from the NosillaCast Podcast - @podfeet

The show starts with a quick look at some interesting numbers and a quick review of the month's legal news before getting stuck into the six main stories of the month: the XcodeGhost malware, the September keynote, the release of iOS 9, Watch OS 2, & Mac OS X 10.11 El Capitan, and Apple's new human-friendly privacy policy. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other shorter stories that made the news in September.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP25-September2015.mp3"]
Noteable Numbers
  • iOS 9 adoption hits 50% in less than a week - www.macobserver.com/...
  • 451 Research find 87% satisfaction rating for Apple Watch - www.macobserver.com/...
  • Adobe study finds that Apple already dominate the "TV Everywhere" market, with 67% - fortune.com/...
Legal Latest
  • Apple reaches settlement with LA Schools district over failed iPad program - Apple will pay $4.2M to the School district (and Lenovo $2.2M) - arstechnica.com/...
  • US Appeals Court finds that Apple were wrongly denied an injunction against Samsung, the case is returned to the lower court - www.imore.com/...
  • Apple appeals eBook Anti-trust case to US Supreme Court - www.imore.com/...
Main Stories
  1. Xcode Ghost - tidbits.com/...
    • Apple's official XCodeGhost Page - www.apple.com/...
    • Apple begin hosting official Xcode download servers in China - www.macobserver.com/...
    • Now blocked by XProtect on OS X - www.intego.com/...
  2. Keynote - daringfireball.net/...

      • 3D Touch will work with screen protectors - www.imore.com/...
      • despite what the internet says, not actually water proof - www.macrumors.com/...
