    • Tim Cook responds to hurricane Harvey with a letter to all staff explaining how the company is helping victims on Texas, and starts accepting donations for relief to the Red Cross through iTunes - www.buzzfeed.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple urged the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to establish stronger net neutrality protections - www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  2. Apple continues it’s push into education - specifically into teaching programming
    • Apple makes a deal with more than 30 US college systems to teach Swift to over 74,000 students - www.loopinsight.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple add support for Sphero’s new R2-D2 robot to Swift Playgrounds - www.macobserver.com/…
  3. The fight over privacy rights continues
    • A US judge orders that you can be forced to put your finger on a fingerprint reader, but not to enter your password - mashable.com/…
    • Recent betas reveal a new feature in iOS - quintuple-tap the sleep-wake button to temporarily disable TouchID - www.macrumors.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
  4. The push towards Augmented Reality continues
    • Apple release developer best practices for AR - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Google adopts Apple’s strategy, releasing ARCore, an ARKit-like suite of APIs for Android - www.imore.com/… & www.loopinsight.com/…
  5. Fitbit join the Smartwatch market with their Fitbit Ionic - www.imore.com/…
Quick Stories
  • Apple strikes another big corporate deal, this time with Accenture. The companies are partnering to deliver iOS-based business solutions to Accenture’s large client base (no mention of the Mac) - www.imore.com/…
  • Apple continues it’s push for more openness from its machine learning team, publishing three news academic papers by the Siri team to its ML portal - www.loopinsight.com/…
  • Apple announces it will build a new data centre in Waukee, Iowa (USA). The deal nets Apple $200M worth of tax breaks, but the company will create a $100M public investment fund for the city - www.macobserver.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple now accepting WeChat Pay in the App Store in China - www.imore.com/…
  • Apple announces a special event in the Steve Jobs Theatre on September 12 - “Let’s meet at our place” - www.loopinsight.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 49 (September 2017)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Patrick Beja from French Spin - @notpatrick
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak
  • Dr. Robert Carter from the Tech Doctor Podcast - @robert_carter

The show starts with some quick followup before moving on to look at a few staffing changes at Apple that made the news in September. The four main stories for the month were Apple's new hardware, Apple's new software, the controversy around Safari's new privacy features, and the hardware released by Sonos, Amazon, and Google. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some shorter Apple-related stories that made the news in September.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP49-September2017.mp3"]
Followups
  • Imagination Technologies has been sold to a Chinese investment company for £550M (~$750M) - uk.businessinsider.com/…
  • Toshiba has agreed to sell it’s Flash Memory business to the so-called Bain Consortium which includes Apple for $18Bn. A sale had previously been agreed with Toshiba, but that fell through. Toshiba are not happy about how things have panned out, and are trying to get this new deal overturned in court, so this is not quite over yet - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Qualcomm has lost two rulings in it’s on-going battle with Apple - “First, it has failed to force Apple’s manufacturing partners to make royalty payments prior to a determination of what the total disputed royalties should be, and second it lost an effort to stop Apple from pursing antitrust cases against it in other countries” - appleinsider.com/…
  • Apple continue their push into education with The Digital Flagship University, a program with Ohio State University that will give students an iPad Pro with and Apple Pencil and Smart Keyboard and access to a bunch of software - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple have made it easier to find AR apps by adding a dedicated section to the App Store - www.macobserver.com/…
  • The EU continues it’s campaign against US tech companies and small European nations with attractive tax arrangements:
    • EU takes Ireland to court for not claiming Apple tax windfall - www.reuters.com/…
    • Luxembourg ordered to collect and extra €250M ($290M) from Amazon - arstechnica.com/…
Notable Staffing Changes
  • Apple has hired three more former Sony TV execs - former head of current programming Kim Rozenfeld, former vice president of drama development Max Aronson, and former director of creative affairs Ali Woodruff - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Long-time Apple General Counsel Bruce Sewell is to retire later this year, and former Supreme Court Clerk Katherine Adams has been taken on to replace him - www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
Main Stories
  1. New Hardware Annouced & Released
    • 4K Apple TV
      • Apple TV 4K review: Come for the 4K, stay for the HDR - www.imore.com/…
      • arstechnica.com/…
    • Apple Watch Series 3
      • The LTE version of the Apple Watch got off to a bumpy start with a bug that affected a lot of people. Apple addressed it quite quickly with a watchOS update - arstechnica.com/… & tidbits.com/…
      • How to roam with your Apple Watch and use LTE data in a foreign country - www.imore.com/… - “The Apple Watch can’t roam. But if you have the right hardware and are willing to pay, you can set it up in a different country with little difficulty”
      • What’s the difference between Apple Watch Series 0, Series 1, Series 2, and Series 3? - www.imore.com/…
      • Apple Watch Series 3 Cellular vs GPS-only: What’s the difference? - www.imore.com/…
      • What the Apple Watch Series 1, Series 2, and Series 3 can do without an iPhone - www.imore.com/…
      • Apple Watch Series 3 LTE Review: Small, flawed, and mighty - www.imore.com/…
      • What’s new with Apple’s Watch bands? - www.imore.com/…
      • Apple Watch Sport Loop Hands On: A runner’s new best friend - www.imore.com/…
    • iPhone 8 & iPhone 8 Plus
      • One of the stand-out features of the iPhone 8 is definitely it’s very impressive brain:
        • iPhone 8 Is World’s Fastest Phone (It’s Not Even Close) - www.tomsguide.com/…
        • Inside iPhone 8: Apple’s A11 Bionic introduces 5 new custom silicon engines - appleinsider.com/…
        • The inside story of the iPhone X ‘brain,’ the A11 Bionic chip - mashable.com/…
        • Why are Apple’s chips faster than Qualcomm’s? – Gary explains - www.androidauthority.com/…
        • Closer Look at Apple’s Image Chip and Portrait Lighting in New iPhones - www.macobserver.com/…
      • iPhone 8 review: The upgrade many people will be looking for - www.imore.com/…
      • A very small percentage of iPhone 8 Pluses have developed a problem where the battery swells and literally bursts open the casing - so far the problem seems very rare, but it’s one to keep an eye on:
        • iPhone 8 Plus Battery Swelling Problem Crops Up in Taiwan - www.macobserver.com/…
        • Chinese state media report bloated battery in Apple’s iPhone 8 - www.reuters.com/…
        • iPhone 8, ‘swollen batteries’, and what you really need to know - www.imore.com/…
    • iPhone X (not yet released)
      • iPhone X FAQ: Everything you need to know! - www.imore.com/…
      • iPhone X vs. iPhone 8: What’s the difference? - www.imore.com/…
      • The biggest new feature is FaceID (replacing TouchID)
        • Face ID: Everything you need to know! - www.imore.com/…
        • Apple’s Face ID Security White Paper Should Allay Fears - www.macobserver.com/…
        • What you should know about privacy and Apple’s FaceID on iOS 11 - arstechnica.com/…
        • Apple explains how Face ID learns from its mistakes - www.theverge.com/…
        • Apple says Face ID didn’t actually fail during its iPhone X event - arstechnica.com/…
        • What We Know About iPhone X Accessibility Features and Face ID - www.macobserver.com/…
        • iPhone X: Face ID Works with Sunglasses - www.macobserver.com/…
        • Here’s How to Temporarily Disable Face ID - www.macobserver.com/…
        • iPhone X: Hands on with Face ID, Portrait Lighting, and Animoji! - www.imore.com/…
      • How the Home ‘button’ works on iPhone X - www.imore.com/…
      • Hands on with the iPhone X: OLED and HDR outshine the other features - arstechnica.com/…
      • You Can Double-Tap to Obscure the Notch While Playing Video on iPhone X - daringfireball.net/…
    • Wireless Charging, AirPower & Apple Charging Mat
      • AirPower, wireless Qi charging, and Apple: Everything you need to know! - www.imore.com/…
      • Here’s What You Need to Know About the iPhone and Wireless Charging - www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple Watch Support in Apple’s Upcoming AirPower Mat Limited to Series 3 Models - www.macrumors.com/…
      • IKEA shows off wireless charging furniture for iPhone 8, iPhone X - www.imore.com/…
  2. New OSes Released
    • macOS 10.13 High Sierra
      • macOS High Sierra: You’ll Hardly Notice You’ve Upgraded - www.macobserver.com/…
      • What’s new in macOS High Sierra - www.imore.com/…
      • macOS High Sierra: How to Stop Videos from Auto-Playing in Safari - www.macobserver.com/…
      • APFS, Apple’s new file system, is shipped as part of High Sierra, but it’s still a bit rough around the edges:
        • New Apple File System Coming in macOS High Sierra Won’t Work With Fusion Drives - www.macrumors.com/…
        • Apple’s new file system will eventually support Fusion Drive machines - arstechnica.com/…
        • Time Machine and APFS: What You Need to Know - www.macobserver.com/…
        • An APFS FAQ: Partitions, Volumes, and AFPS Containers - www.macobserver.com/…
        • Apple fixes the Disk Utility APFS bug: What you need to know! - www.imore.com/…
      • How to share your iCloud storage with your family - www.imore.com/…
      • macOS High Sierra: How to Enable Type to Siri - www.macobserver.com/…
      • macOS High Sierra: Security and Privacy Features Overview - www.intego.com/…
      • macOS High Sierra drops support for older Final Cut Studio, Logic Studio apps - www.imore.com/…
    • watchOS 4
      • watchOS 4 review: Refinements and smarts paint a bright picture for Apple Watch - www.imore.com/…
      • watchOS 4: How to Enable Elevated Heart Rate Alerts - www.macobserver.com/…
      • Original Apple Watch Doesn’t Support watchOS 4 Heart Rate Features - www.macobserver.com/…
      • Getting Rid of the ‘Now Playing’ Screen on watchOS 4 - www.macobserver.com/…
    • iOS 11
      • iOS 11: Apple’s Big Productivity Upgrade - www.macobserver.com/…
      • While the new Control Center adds a lot of much loved new functionality and customisability, it also comes with some controversy:
        • How to customize Control Center in iOS 11 - www.imore.com/…
        • Use Bluetooth and Wi-Fi in Control Center with iOS 11 - support.apple.com/…
        • Why your iPhone and iPad don’t fully disconnect from Wi-Fi and Bluetooth in iOS 11 - www.imore.com/…
        • Control Center’s New Networking States: On, Off, and In Between - tidbits.com/…
        • iOS 11’s Misleading “Off-ish” Setting for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi is Bad for User Security - www.eff.org/…
      • How to use Instant Notes on iPad Pro with Apple Pencil in iOS 11 - www.imore.com/…
      • How to use Instant Markup in iOS 11 - www.imore.com/…
      • How to use the document scanner on iPhone and iPad - www.imore.com/…
      • How to use Do Not Disturb While Driving in iOS 11 - www.imore.com/…
      • iOS 11: How to Type to Siri - www.macobserver.com/…
      • iOS 11: A Complete Guide to iOS Security and Privacy - www.intego.com/…
      • Which iPhones and iPads will (and won’t) work with iOS 11? - www.imore.com/…
      • How to use the Dock in iOS 11 - www.imore.com/…
      • How to use Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, and other could storage services with the Files app on iPhone and iPad - www.imore.com/…
      • How to use Automatic Setup in iOS 11 - www.imore.com/…
      • How to Use iOS 11 Screen Recording - www.macobserver.com/…
      • How to sync your Health data in iOS 11 (and how it works) - www.imore.com/…
      • What’s new with Accessibility in iOS 11? - www.imore.com/…
      • 3D Touch Multitasking Coming Back in Future iOS 11 Update - www.macobserver.com/…
  3. Apple anger the ad industry by improving privacy in Safari 11
    • Apple’s new tracking protection is “sabotage”, claims ad industry - nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • Apple responds to ad group’s criticism of Safari cookie blocking - www.loopinsight.com/…
    • Preventing cross-site tracking and web cookie sharing - www.loopinsight.com/…
    • Apple isn’t collecting user data in Safari, it’s collecting crappy website trends - www.imore.com/…
  4. Product announcements from Sonos, Amazon & Google
    • Sonos announced their new Sonos One - the big new feature is built-in Alexa - www.macobserver.com/…
    • Amazon - tidbits.com/… & www.imore.com/…
      • New Fire TV - HDR 4K and just $69.99
      • 2nd Gen Amazon Echo - starting price dropped to just $99.99
      • Echo Plus - serves as hub for some home automation products (no HomeKit support), starts at $149.99
      • Echo Spot - a smaller version of the Echo Show starting at $129.99
      • Echo buttons - tiny accessories for playing Echo games, just $20 for a starter pack
      • Echo Connect - ties Amazon Echo into your landline phone
    • Google
      • Two new Google Home devices - the Google Home Mini ($49) and the Google Home Max ($399) - www.blog.google/…
      • The Google Pixel 2 - www.blog.google/…
Quick Stories
  • Apple has updated iTunes to version 12.7, and removed or hidden lot of features to tighten its focus on music - www.macstories.net/…, www.macobserver.com/…, www.loopinsight.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple switches from Bing to Google for Siri web searches in iOS 11 & MacOS 10.13 High Sierra - social.techcrunch.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple bumps up iPad Pro prices, launches 32GB Jet Black iPhone 7 and new Siri Remote - www.imore.com/…
  • Apple update their privacy page - www.imore.com/…
  • iTunes movie rentals, in the US at least, now give you twice as long to finish a movie after you start it - 48 hours - www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple, Fitbit, others work with FDA to pilot digital health software - arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple Q4 2017 Earnings Report Set for November 2 - www.macobserver.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 50 (October 2017)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Mark chappell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @oceanspeed
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
  • Allister Jenks - @zkarj
The show starts with some Apple-related legal stories that made the news in October before moving on to look at some interesting Apple-related statistics and staffing changes. The four main stories for the month are Apple's Q4 earnings call, the release of the iPhone X, the end of Windows Phone, and a bad month for Google. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some shorter Apple-related stories that made the news in October.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP50-October2017.mp3"]
Legal Latest
  • Apple -v- Qualcomm
    • Qualcomm Wants China to Ban iPhones, Claims to Have Invented Force Touch — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Qualcomm sues Apple for giving rival Intel classified information — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple -v- Samsung
    • Judge Koh Grants Samsung New Damages Trial in Apple iPhone Patent Infringement Trial — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple lose to VirnetX’s patent claims for a third time, this time the judge increases the bill for Apple to $440M — arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple sued over ‘Animoji’ trademark, allegedly tried to buy IP rights prior to iPhone X debut — appleinsider.com/…
Notable Numbers
  • Rigorous testing by FutureMark shows what we all knew anyway – iPhones do not get slower over time — www.futuremark.com/…
  • A CNBC poll finds that the average American household has two Apple devices — www.cnbc.com/…
  • Piper Jaffray teen poll shows iPhone & Apple Watch continue to dominate — 9to5mac.com/…
  • Apple Pay at three: 20 markets covering 70% of payments, 4,000 issuers — www.imore.com/… & social.techcrunch.com/…
Notable Staffing Changes
  • Apple Poaches Amazon Video Exec to Head International Development — www.macobserver.com/…
Main Stories
  1. Apple’s Q4 2017 Earnings Call — www.apple.com/…
    • Apple’s Data Summary PDF — www.apple.com/…
    • Transcript: Apple CEO Tim Cook on the company’s 2017 Q4 earnings — www.imore.com/…
    • Jason Snell’s earnings report charts — sixcolors.com/…
    • Highlights from Apple’s Q4 2017 investors call — www.imore.com/…
    • Shares of Apple Up in After Hours as Market Reacts to iPhone, iPad, and Mac Sales — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple CEO Tim Cook Expects Record Breaking December Quarter — www.macobserver.com/…
  2. iPhone X released
    • Apple says iPhone X pre-orders are ‘off the charts’ — www.reuters.com/…
    • The iPhone X is sold out, currently offering delivery 5–6 weeks out — www.loopinsight.com/…
    • iPhone X Selling for More than $3,000 on Ebay — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Face ID FUD — daringfireball.net/…, www.imore.com/… & appleinsider.com/…
    • It’ll Cost up to $549 to Fix Your iPhone X Screen Without AppleCare+ — www.macobserver.com/…
    • iFixit’s iPhone X teardown finds two battery cells and an “unprecedented” logic board — arstechnica.com/… & www.ifixit.com/…
    • ACLU raises privacy concerns over app developer access to facial expressions on iPhone X — 9to5mac.com/…
  3. It’s official – Microsoft are calling it a day on Windows Phone — www.windowscentral.com/…
  4. A bad month for Google
    • Problems with the Home Mini – a hardware problem with a switch forces Google to disable functionality to prevent in-intended spying on owners — www.androidpolice.com/… & uk.businessinsider.com/…
    • Problems with the Pixel 2
      • First, reviewers are not happy with Google’s choice of colour calibration on the screens — www.imore.com/…
      • Then it emerges that the screens on some of the larger model phones suffer burn-in after just a few weeks — daringfireball.net/…, www.macobserver.com/… & www.androidcentral.com/…
      • Google respond by extending the warranty — www.loopinsight.com/…
      • Finally, some Pixels seem to have been accidentally shipped without an OS! — www.androidpolice.com/…
Quick Stories
  • Apple and GE bringing Predix apps to iPhone and iPad — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple Buys Wireless Charging Designer PowerbyProxi — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple CEO Tim Cook: Mac Mini Will Be ‘Important Part’ of Future Product Lineup — www.macrumors.com/…
  • Apple Acknowledges Apple Watch Series 3 Issue Where ‘Edge Stripes’ Appear on Display — www.macrumors.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 51 (November 2017)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Elaine Giles from MacBites Learning - @elainegiles
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak
  • Guy Serle from the My Mac Podcast - @Macparrot
The show starts with some Apple-related legal stories that made the news in November before moving on to look at some interesting Apple-related staffing changes. The four main stories for the month are Apple's taxes, Apple's month of embarrassing OS bugs, how FaceID is working out in the real world, and Apple's continued adventures in the health arena. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some shorter Apple-related stories that made the news in November.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP51-November2017.mp3"]
Legal Latest
  • US Supreme Court rejects Samsung’s appeal of their patent loss to Apple — www.reuters.com/…
  • Apple have filed a counter-suit against Qualcomm, saying they are not infringing Qualcomm’s battery life management patents, but that Qualcomm are instead infringing on 8 of Apple’s batter life management patents — www.macobserver.com/…
Notable Staffing Changes
  • Despite only taking up the role of Head of Diversity and Inclusion in Apple in May, DeDenise Young Smith is leaving Apple for Cornell University. Christie Smith formerly from Delloite will be joining Apple to assume the role — www.macobserver.com/…
Main Stories
  1. Apple’s Taxes in the spotlight again
    • The so-called paradise papers revealed that Apple uses subsidiaries registered in Jersey (one of the Channel Islands that are sorta-kinda but not fully in the UK) to legally minimise their US tax liability on foreign-earned income. This triggered a lot of criticism of Apple — arstechnica.com/…
    • Apple responded with a post on their web page — The facts about Apple’s tax payments — www.apple.com/…
    • Editorial by Bart: The reason Apple made changes in their tax registration is that Ireland changed its tax laws. Before the change companies could effectively be nationless when it comes to tax registration. After the change, every company had to pick some nation to be their home nation for tax purposes, so, Apple was forced to choose one. What the leaked documents show is that Apple asked a legal company for advice on which country to choose. That’s not a scandal, it’s good corporate governance, and responsible fulfilment of Apple’s fiduciary duty to their share holders. No on is claiming Apple did anything illegal here. They also did nothing unusual — companies would leave themselves open to shareholder lawsuits if they voluntarily paid taxes they did no legally owe! The problem is the laws Apple, and all other American multinationals, have to abide by. Companies are not charities, they are money-making machines. They are by their very nature amoral — neither good not evil. Companies optimise profits within the law. It’s law makers that get to decide what is and is not OK for companies to do, and they are failing MISERABLY at doing so. Every elected lawmaker who feigns outrage at Apple is just trying to distract you from their abject failure to do their job!
  2. A month of Embarrassing Bugs for Apple
    • iOS hit with two weird Auto-complete bugs
      • Some people experienced a bug where the letter i was replace with the letter a and a funny symbol. The bug seemed to develop over time, affecting ever more people. Apple released an updated version of iOS to fix the bug — 9to5mac.com/… & support.apple.com/…
      • Later in the month reports have begun to surface that some people are experiencing a bug where it gets auto-corrected to I.T. — www.imore.com/…
    • Much more seriously, macOS was hit with a spectacularly embarrassing security bug where entering no password in a specific circumstance enabled the root account with a blank password
      • Major Authentication Security Flaw Reported in macOS High Sierra [Update] — www.intego.com/…
      • Apple closes that big root hole – “Install this update as soon as possible” — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
      • Apple Says It’s Auditing Development Processes in Wake of Mac Root Access Flaw — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Repair file sharing after Security Update 2017–001 for macOS High Sierra 10.13.1 — support.apple.com/…
      • High Sierra Root Login Bug Was Mentioned on Apple’s Support Forums Two Weeks Ago — daringfireball.net/…
      • High Sierra root login bug was known weeks ago, if not longer. What should have happened? — www.loopinsight.com/…
  3. FaceID gets tested in the real world
    • The limitations of Face ID: What you need to know — www.imore.com/…
    • No, siblings aren’t ‘fooling’ Face ID — they’re training it — www.imore.com/…
    • Face ID hasn’t been hacked: What you need to know — www.imore.com/…
    • Watch a 10-Year-Old Beat Apple’s Face ID on His Mom’s iPhone X | WIRED — www.wired.com/…
    • Face ID Hack Created Again by Vietnamese Team With $200 Mask — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Craig Federighi responds to question about multiple-face support – seems it’s not gonna happen any time soon, if at all — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: Apple release a paper describing how they use deep neural networks for face recognition on their Apple Machine Learning Journal — www.imore.com/…
  4. Apple continues their push into Health
    • A study by health startup Cardiogram & the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) finds that the Apple Watch can detect hypertension with an accuracy of 82%, and sleep apnea with an accuracy of 90% (a previous study by the same group found the Apple Watch can detect abnormal heart rhythms with an accuracy of 97% — social.techcrunch.com/…
    • Apple team up with Stanford University to launch a revolutionary heart rhythm study using the Apple Watch — www.imore.com/…
      • How to Sign Up for Apple and Stanford’s Apple Watch Heart Rhythm Study — www.macobserver.com/…
    • FDA Approves First Apple Watch EKG Band — www.macobserver.com/…
Quick Stories
  • Apple officially delays the HomePod until ‘early 2018’ — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple improves their customer support:
    • Apple Support Comes to YouTube With Official Channel — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple updates Support app with redesigned UI, new Discover section, and search — 9to5mac.com/…
  • Apple extends free repairs of anti-reflective coating on certain MacBooks — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple continues their drive to teach coding to as many people as possible:
    • Apple expand their Everyone Can Code program to 20 more universities around the world — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Opens Registration for Free Hour of Code Classes for Kids — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple scientists publish their first research paper related to automatous cars. The paper is published in the journal arXiv with the title ‘VoxelNet: End-to-End Learning for Point Cloud Based 3D Object Detection’ — www.reuters.com/… & arxiv.org/…
  • Two major Cydia repositories shut down due to the continued decline in iOS jail breaking — www.macrumors.com/…
  • Jennifer Aniston, Reese Witherspoon Morning Show Drama Lands at Apple | Hollywood Reporter — www.hollywoodreporter.com/…
  • Microsoft Edge officially launches on iOS — www.imore.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple - Ep. 52 (December 2017)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Lynda Gousha from the Silicon Valley MUG - @llg4cdg

The show starts with some quick follow-up stories, some Apple-related notable numbers, a few Apple-related legal stories, some staffing changes at Apple, and some Apple acquisitions and investments that made the news in December. The four main stories for the month are the launch of Apple Pay Cash in the US, availability of the iPad Pro, Battery Gate, and the rumoured unified developer platform Marzipan. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some shorter Apple-related stories that made the news in December.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP52-December2017.mp3"]
Followups
  • Amazon follows through on promises to mend their rift with Apple by the end of the year:
    • Amazon Prime arrives on Apple TV in over 100 countries — arstechnica.com/… & www.loopinsight.com/…
    • Amazon Prime Video app breaks Apple TV download record — www.bestappletv.com/…
    • Amazon resume selling Apple TVs (and Google Chromecasts) — www.reuters.com/…
  • Apple continue their education push: Apple and Chicago join forces to bring coding opportunities to city’s students — www.apple.com/…
  • Test shows how good iPhone X’s OLED screen is at preventing burn-in — bgr.com/…
  • Continuing their moves to allow Apple scientists present their work more openly, Apple researchers demoed self-driving car tech at the Neural Information Processing Systems conference — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Despite their investments in India, Apple are forced to hike their prices in the country due to being considered a foreign company — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple have agreed to pay the €13Bn the European Commission says it owes Ireland into an escrow account in the first quarter of 2018 — www.reuters.com/…
Notable Numbers
  • iPhone is Flickr’s most popular camera in 2017 — www.imore.com/…
    • The iPhone newspaper cover mentioned by Gaz: www.bbc.com/…
  • iPhone maintains reign as top tech best-selling product in 2017 — www.usatoday.com/…
Legal Latest
  • Chinese Clothing Brand Sues Apple for App Store Trademark Infringement — www.macobserver.com/…
  • An Italian court has granted a pair of Italian brothers the right to name their clothing company Steve Jobs, and use a J with a leaf on top and a bite taken out of it as their corporate logo — gizmodo.com/…, www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
Apple Acquisitions & Investments
  • Apple acquires Pop Up Archive, the company behind the podcast search engine Audiosear.ch
  • Apple acquires popular music recognition app Shazam — www.buzzfeed.com/…
  • Apple Purchases Developer Tool Firm Buddybuild, Team to Remain in Canada — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple uses it’s $1Bn Advanced Manufacturing Fund to make a $390M investment in Finisar, a US company that makes laser-based sensors used for depth sensing in the iPhone X and proximity sensing in AirPods — www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
HR Happenings
  • Jony Ives moves back to directly managing Apple’s design team — www.bloomberg.com/…
  • Apple hires former Universal producer Michelle Lee — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple hires two business affairs executives for their video division – Philip Matthys from Hulu, and Jennifer Wang Grazier from Legendary Entertainment — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple hires three more Amazon executives — variety.com/…
    • Tara Sorensen, formerly head of Amazon kids programming, joins Apple in a similar role
    • Carina Walker, formerly an international development executive at Amazon will become an international creative executive at Apple
    • Tara Pietri, formerly Amazon business affairs chief will lead Apple’s legal affairs division
  • Google Poaches Top Mobile Chip Designer John Bruno From Apple — www.macrumors.com/…
Main Stories
  1. Apple Pay Cash launches in America on iOS & watchOS
    • Apple Releases iOS 11.2, Launching Apple Pay Cash, Faster Wireless Charging, Notifications Bug Fix — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Pay Cash hits Apple Watches with watchOS 4.2 release — arstechnica.com/…
    • Everything Apple Pay Cash, From Setup to Sending Money — www.macobserver.com/…
    • How to send money with Apple Pay Cash in the Messages app — www.imore.com/…
  2. The iMac Pro goes on sale — arstechnica.com/…
    • First Impressions of the New iMac Pro — daringfireball.net/…
    • iMac Pro Geekbench scores begin to surface for the iMac Pro — www.imore.com/…
    • Surprise! The iMac Pro has Upgradable RAM and SSD — www.macobserver.com/…
    • iMac Pro Teardown — www.ifixit.com/…
  3. Battery Gate (or the latest mindless faux-scandal to set the world atwitter)
    • Apple’s public letter on the topic: A Message to Our Customers about iPhone Batteries and Performance — www.apple.com/…
    • Apple’s $29 iPhone Battery Replacement Doesn’t Require a Device Check — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple’s $29 battery replacement program: what you need to know — www.imore.com/…
    • iFixit Drops DIY iPhone Battery Replacement Kits to $29, Matching Apple’s Apology Price — www.macobserver.com/…
    • No, your iPad isn’t affected by #iPhoneSlow. Here’s why! — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple is Slowing Down Your Old iPhone, but There’s a Good Reason — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple deliberately slows old iPhones! A story of good reasons and dumb, dumb messaging — www.imore.com/…
    • hashtag iPhoneSlow What the analysts and experts have to say — www.imore.com/…
    • Battery Scientist Joins Debate on iPhone Throttling — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Is Being Slandered For What Chemistry Cannot Fix — seekingalpha.com/…
    • Samsung, HTC, LG comment on hashtag iPhoneSlow despite awkward histories of cheating on benchmarks — www.imore.com/…
    • Unsurprisingly, the lawsuits soon began to fly:
      • Apple Being Sued for ‘Purposefully Slowing Down Older iPhone Models’ — www.macrumors.com/…
      • Days after iPhone battery fiasco, lawsuits against Apple begin to mount — arstechnica.com/…
      • One iPhone slowdown lawsuit is seeking a wild $999 billion — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple Now Facing 8 Lawsuits Over iPhone Battery Slowdown Fix — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Here’s How to Monitor Your iPhone Battery Health from your phone or Mac — www.macobserver.com/…
  4. Apple reportedly working on new unified framework for Mac & iOS development code-named Marzipan
    • Apple could announce universal iOS/macOS apps as soon as WWDC 2018 — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Has Plans for Unified Mac, iPhone, and iPad Apps — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Marzipan — daringfireball.net/…
Quick Stories
  • GymKit now available in the US — arstechnica.com/… & www.imore.com/…
  • Apple’s TV app arrives in three more countries – the UK, France & Germany — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple updates its iOS App Store Functionality and Guidelines:
    • Apple Allows App Store Preorders — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple eases up on template-based apps — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple cracks down on loot boxes in update to App Store review guidelines — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple to Waive iOS Developer Fee for Governments and NonProfits — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple Maps brings indoor maps to 30 additional airports — www.imore.com/…
  • Save the date:
    • Apple Q1 2018 Earnings Call Set for February 1 — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Annual Shareholder Meeting Set for February 13 2018 — www.macobserver.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 53 (January 2018)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Dermot Daly from Tapadoo - @dermdaly
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Lynda Gousha from the Silicon Valley MUG - @llg4cdg

The show starts with some quick follow-up stories, some Apple-related notable numbers, one Apple-related legal stories, and some staffing changes at Apple that made the news in January. The five main stories for the month are the launch of the HomePod, Apple's repatriation of billions of dollars to the US, Apple's Q1 2018 results, the on-going war on privacy, and Apple's preview of up-coming changes to macOSServer and iOS. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some shorter Apple-related stories that made the news in January.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP53-January2018.mp3"]
Followup — ‘Battery-gate’
  • A future update to iOS will give customers more information about the health of their battery, and allow them to turn advanced power management on and off so they can have unexpected shutdowns if they really think that’s a good idea — www.imore.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
  • Law suits continue to mount up — www.imore.com/…
  • Governments around the world take interest:
    • French prosecutor launches probe into Apple planned obsolescence: judicial source — www.reuters.com/…
    • US Senator John Thune, chairman of the Senate’s Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee sent a letter to Apple with questions about the affair — arstechnica.com/…
    • Apple under investigation by DOJ, SEC for disclosures of its iPhone slow-down update — arstechnica.com/…
    • Chinese Consumer Group Also Wants Answers on Throttlegate — www.macobserver.com/…
    • South Korean group files complaint against Apple CEO over iPhone slowdown — www.reuters.com/…
Notable Numbers
  • According to data analytics firm Sensor Tower, 2017 as a great year for both Google & Apple’s app stores — total mobile app store sales (including in-app purchasing) are estimated to have been $60Bn for 2017 (up 35%), with $44Bn spent buying apps. Apple’s store remains about twice as big as Google’s.
    • For context: The iOS Economy — www.asymco.com/…
    • Related: Apple released some record-setting App Store numbers — over 2017 developers earned $26Bn (30% increase over 2016), and App Store sales for new years day were $300M — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Related: App Annie have released their Q4 2017 App Store report – the most striking two charts show that Google has a massive lead in downloads, and Apple, in sales — www.appannie.com/…
  • Six Colors release their annual Apple Report Card — sixcolors.com/…
  • The latest global smartphone shipment estimates from Strategy Analytics show the market as a whole dropping by 9% in Q4 2017, but Apple remaining basically flat, and surpassing Samsung in units shipped — www.strategyanalytics.com/…
Legal Latest
  • The European Commission have fined Qualcomm €997M (~$1¼Bn) for anti-trust violations because it paid Apple to exclusively use its chips from 2011 to 2016 — www.imore.com/…
Notable Staffing Changes
  • Some detective work by TechCrunch finds that Apple have poached somewhere between a third and a half of the staff from Silicon Valley Data Science, a silicon valley data science startup — techcrunch.com/…
  • Apple have hired Kashif Zafar away form Amazon where he was senior VP of Audible — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Related: Apple is reportedly working on big changes to their eBook offerings, with a new version of the iBooks app in the works that will simply be called Books — arstechnica.com/…
Main Stories
  1. A few months later than promised, Apple’s HomePod launches
    • Pre-orders from 26 Jan, available from 9 Feb — arstechnica.com/…
    • The HomePod is initially shipping without some promised features, but they’ll be released later in 2018. The missing features are related to on-going delays in getting AirPlay 2 released — www.macobserver.com/…
    • What can’t the HomePod do at launch? — www.imore.com/…
    • How HomePod works with Siri — www.imore.com/…
    • These are the Music Services Siri Supports on HomePod — www.macobserver.com/…
    • iPhone Home App Manages HomePod Software Updates — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Related: New bundle drops the Sonos One back to its lowest price — www.imore.com/…
    • Reviews:
      • One Hour With Apple’s New HomePod — www.refinery29.com/…
      • HomePod vs. Amazon Echo vs. Google Home Max vs. Sonos One: Speaker showdown — www.imore.com/…
  2. Apple Plans to pay $38Bn in US Taxes to bring overseas cash home in the wake of President Trump’s large corporate tax cut — arstechnica.com/…
    • Apple to Give Employees $2,500 Bonus in Restricted Stock, Will Also Double Charity Contributions — www.macobserver.com/…
    • For context: The Apple Cash FAQ — www.asymco.com/…
    • Related:
      • Apple promise to invest $350Bn in the US economy over the next 5 years — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple Plans to Build Another New Campus — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple Expands Advanced Manufacturing Fund to $5 Billion — www.macobserver.com/…
      • A great explanation of how all this international tax stuff works from Jean-Louis Gassée — mondaynote.com/…
  3. Apple’s 2018 Q1 Results — www.apple.com/…
    • Transcript: Apple CEO Tim Cook on the company’s 2018 Q1 earnings — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Reports Record Revenues of $88.3 Billion, Record EPS of $3.89 – iPhone X Top Selling Model — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Services Hit 240 Million Paid Subscriptions — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple’s Record Quarter Includes Mixed Results, But iPhone X Performance Will Wow Wall Street — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Watch, AirPods drive Wearables rev 70%, outpacing size, growth of Amazon ads, Google Cloud, Alphabet Other Bets — appleinsider.com/…
    • Apple’s results over the past few years in pictures — sixcolors.com/…
  4. The on-going war on privacy
    • The US Government’s relationship with encryption, and with Apple, remains problematic:
      • FBI Director Renews Calls for Magical Encryption Bypass, Doesn’t Believe Experts Who Call It Impossible — www.macobserver.com/…
      • FBI director says ‘unbreakable encryption is a public safety issue’ — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
      • FBI security expert: Apple are “jerks” about unlocking encrypted phones — arstechnica.com/…
      • The whole FBI are not hostile to Apple though — FBI’s San Francisco Chief: We Heart Apple, They Train Our Cops — www.forbes.com/…
      • House votes for six more years of warrantless surveillance — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • To comply with a new Chinese law, Apple has been forced to had over operation of its Chinese iCloud data to a state-owned Chinese company, which will host the data in China — arstechnica.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple continues to work to protect our security and privacy
      • Apple released an updated version of their iOS Security Guide — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple to Add a Privacy Icon to iOS to Stop iCloud Phishing — www.macobserver.com/…
      • The ad industry is complaining loudly that Safari’s new privacy features are costing them ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ in lost revenue — www.theguardian.com/…
  5. Apple previews future software releases
    • In an article entitled ‘Prepare for changes to macOS Server’ Apple effectively announce the end of macOS Server, deprecating just about every service offered (“macOS Server is changing to focus more on management of computers, devices, and storage on your network”) — support.apple.com/…
      • Apple to Deprecate Many macOS Server Services - TidBITS — tidbits.com/…
      • Apple Seemingly Kills macOS Server, Deprecates Many Essential Services — www.macobserver.com/…
    • iOS 11.3 preview — tidbits.com/…
      • What you need to know about Health Records in iOS 11.3 — www.imore.com/…
Quick Stories
  • Reports continue to come out sugesting Apple’s nascent video group are working very hard indeed:
    • Apple Orders ‘See’, Epic Drama Series From Steven Knight & Francis Lawrence — deadline.com/…
    • Kristen Wiig Will Star in Comedy Series for Apple, Reese Witherspoon to Executive Produce — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Just Committed to a Straight-to-Series Order by Damien Chazelle — www.macobserver.com/…
  • In response to an open letter from a group of investors ahead of Apple’s annual shareholders meeting, Apple have announced they will be improving their parental controls features — arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple’s Everyone Can Code Initiative Spreading to Europe — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Related: Apple have released Swift Playgrounds 2 — developer.apple.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • WhatsApp on CarPlay: The First Third Party Messaging App — www.macobserver.com/…
  • YouTube TV App Now Available on Apple TV — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Siri Podcast News Feature Rolling Out to iOS 11.2.2 Users — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple becomes Malala Fund’s first Laureate partner, helps increase support for girls’ education — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple Named Fortune’s Most Admired Company 11 Years Running — www.macobserver.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 54 (February 2018)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak

The show starts with a quick follow-up on Throttle Gate before moving on to the three main stories of the month, the arrival of HomePods in people's homes, Apple's moves to source their Cobalt directly from mines, and the on-going war on privacy. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some shorter Apple-related stories that made the news in February.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP54-February2018.mp3"]
Followup
  • Throttle Gate Developments
    • The release of iOS 11.3 beta 2 gave us our first look at the battery management UI Apple promised to ship in iOS11.3 — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple responds to a letter from US Senator John Thune which asked specific questions about Apple’s battery management features — arstechnica.com/…
      • iPhone 8, iPhone 8S & iPhone X will not need the same kind of throttling because their newer hardware design prevents the kinds of battery spikes that caused the unexpected shutdowns in earlier models
      • Apple is ‘exploring’ giving partial refunds to customers who paid for the full price of a battery replacement before they reduced the price
Main Stories
  1. The HomePod is out, and off to a mixed start
    • The audio quality really does appear to be excellent as we suspected — arstechnica.com/…, www.imore.com/… & www.loopinsight.com/…
    • The HomePod has been found to leave white rings on some surfaces — www.macrumors.com/…
      • Though it’s not alone in that, so does the Sonos One — www.loopinsight.com/…
  2. As competition for Cobalt ramps up, Apple moves to purchase it directly from miners — www.bloomberg.com/…
    • Cobalt is a critical ingredient in Lithium-Ion batteries like those Apple uses in just about all their products
    • One of the reasons for the ramp-up of demand for Cobalt is electric cars — arstechnica.com/…
    • Cobalt mines are notorious for their human rights abuses, and buying direct will make it much easier for Apple to source the element ethically — daringfireball.net/…
  3. Developments in the Privacy War
    • Apple’s relationship with law enforcement continues to be a lot more nuanced than many realise:
      • Apple Helps Authorities Bring Russian Spam Lord to Justice — www.macobserver.com/…
      • NYPD arms Manhattan cops with the newest tool in fighting crime — the iPhone — www.nydailynews.com/…
    • As expected, Apple has moved forward with its plans to move Chinese iCloud data to China to comply with a new Chinese law
      • It’s now emerged that Apple has been forced to move the encryption keys to China too — www.macobserver.com/…
      • As a result of this move, Apple will need to open a second datacenter in China — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Obviously the laws that apply to Apple apply to other companies too, but that fact sometimes gets lost in the media reports. John Gruber highlighted the fact that Microsoft has been forced to do the same for their Azure cloud services — daringfireball.net/…
      • Related Apple have updated their iOS security documentation to note that they now contract some of their cloud hosting to Google — arstechnica.com/…
    • News has broken that Israeli hacking company Cellebrite now claims to be able to crack any iPhone, even the latest models running iOS 11 — www.macobserver.com/… & nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
Quick Stories
  • More news on news of TV shows Apple is reportedly working on:
    • Apple and Ron Howard Developing Series Based on NBA Superstar Kevin Durant’s Early Career — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Renews Carpool Karaoke: The Series for a Second Season — www.macobserver.com/…
    • M. Night Shyamalan to Produce Straight-to-Series Thriller for Apple — variety.com/…
  • Apple Shareholder Meeting Highlights: No Special Dividend, Health Care Opportunity, and No Apple Park Tours — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple’s moves into the business world continue as they partner with Cisco, Aon, and Allianz to deliver corporate cyber security services — Apple Partnering With Other Companies for Cyber Security — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple Launches Repair Program for iPhone 7 “No Service” Issues - TidBITS — tidbits.com/…
  • Apple to introduce changes preventing old PCs from using the iTunes Store — www.imore.com/… & Apple to suspend iTunes Store support for “obsolete” first-gen Apple TV — arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple Launching its Own Primary Health Care Service for Employees — www.macobserver.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 55 (March 2018)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
  • Lynda Gousha from the Silicon Valley MUG - @llg4cdg
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
The show starts with a few notable numbers and one notable staffing change before moving into the three main stories for March — Apple's Education event, updates for all Apple's OSes, and the on-going debate around security and privacy. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some smaller stories that made the news in March.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP55-March2018.mp3"]
Notable Numbers
  • Study Confirms Apple Watch Can Detect Abnormal Heart Rhythm With 97% Accuracy — www.macrumors.com/…
  • Asymco’s Horace Dediu does the maths based on Tim Cook’s statement that there are 1.3Bn active Apple devices from last month’s earnings call to determine that 2 out of every 3 Apple device ever sold is still in use — www.macobserver.com/… & www.asymco.com/…
Apple Personnel Changes
  • Jimmy Iovine is stepping back from a day-to-day role in Apple Music, and transitioning to a ‘consulting role’ in August — www.macrumors.com/… & www.imore.com/…
Main Stories
  1. Apple’s Field Trip Education Event
    • New 9.7" iPad with Pencil support starting at $329 ($299 for education, and schools can also get Apple Pencils for $89) — tidbits.com/…, www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • Apple announced the $49 Logitech Crayon, a stylus with all the feature of the Apple Pencil except pressure sensitivity which works on any pencil-capable iPad without pairing (only possible because of the lack of pressure sensitivity) — www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • Apple announced the $99 Logitech Rugged Combo Case (a kid-proof keyboard case for the new iPad) — www.imore.com/…
    • Free education iCloud accounts now get 200GB of storage (up from just 5GB), and Apple is continuing to improve it’s Apple School Manager cloud app and matching Classroom app (coming to the Mac for the first time) — www.macobserver.com/…
    • iWork apps updated with Pencil support, beta version of new smart annotation feature, and the ability to create iBooks — tidbits.com/…, www.macobserver.com/…, www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • Apple announced Schoolwork, a cloud teaching app, and the matching ClassKit API to allow apps to integrate with it — www.macobserver.com/…, www.macobserver.com/…, www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • Apple announced Everyone can Create curriculum/program for educators — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple + Education Home Page Redesign — www.macobserver.com/…
  2. Apple Update All their OSes — iOS 11.3, Watch OS 4.3, tvOS 11.3 & MacOS 10.13.4
    • iOS 11.3 adds the promised battery health settings page, Health Records feature, and ARKit 1.5 — www.macobserver.com/…, www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • A software update for the HomePod is included in iOS 11.3, it gets pushed to the device via the Home app similarly to how Apple Watch updates get pushed out via the Watch app on iOS
    • WatchOS 4.3 brings the ability to control a HomePod from your wrist — www.macobserver.com/…
    • iCloud Business Chat goes live — www.imore.com/…
    • HomeKit now has support for software-based authentication, removing the need for a dedicated HomeKit chip to make a device HomeKit-compatible — www.imore.com/…
  3. The On-Going Security & Privacy Debate
    • FBI: we don’t want a backdoor; we just want you to break encryption — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • Justice Dept. Revives Push to Mandate a Way to Unlock Phones — www.nytimes.com/… & Push for legal mandate to unlock phones revived by DOJ — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • GrayKey iPhone unlocker poses serious security concerns — blog.malwarebytes.com/…
    • CLOUD Act and Apple: What you need to know — www.imore.com/…
    • The CLOUD Act: A Dangerous Expansion of Police Snooping on Cross-Border Data | Electronic Frontier Foundation — www.eff.org/…
    • Tim Cook Calls for ‘Well-Crafted’ Regulation Protecting Privacy — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Tim Cook says Apple’s customers are not its product, unlike Facebook — arstechnica.com/…
    • Big news about Apple, GDPR, and your privacy — www.imore.com/…
Quick Stories
  • Apple released its latest annual supplier responsibility report — www.imore.com/…, arstechnica.com/… & www.apple.com/…
  • Bloomberg discovered that Apple has a secret plant in Santa Clara that’s working on manufacturing microLED panels — www.macobserver.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple strikes a deal with IBM to provide an integration between their CoreML AI framework, and IBM’s Watson AI services — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple has signed an agreement to buy Texture, ‘the Netflix of magazines’ — www.imore.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple Intros ‘Families’ Webpage with Kid-safe Computing Tips — www.macobserver.com/… & www.apple.com/…
  • Apple submits proposal for accessibility emoji to the Unicode Consortium — www.imore.com/…
  • Space Gray Mac Accessories are now Available for Purchase — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple Competitor Watch:
    • Amazon dips it’s toe into the wearables market with the $79 Amzfit Bip — www.imore.com/…
    • Fitbit OS 2.0 rolling out to Fitbit Ionic with new gestures, Deezer, and more — www.imore.com/…
    • Google tries to take on the iPad with its first ever Chrome OS tablet — www.imore.com/…
    • President Trump blocked Broadcom’s bid to buy Qualcomm on national security grounds — stratechery.com/…
    • Foxconn buys peripheral maker Belkin for $866M — social.techcrunch.com/…
  • Save the date: WWDC 2018 will run June 4th to the 8th in San Jose — www.imore.com/… & developer.apple.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 56 (April 2018)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Kelly Guimont from App Camp for Girls - @verso
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Victor Cajiao - @victorcajiao
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
The show starts with a few notable numbers and hires that made the news in April before moving on to the five main stories — Bloomberg's report that Apple will switch the Mac to their own ARM processors, Apple's continued Environmental push, the end of the line for the AirPort, the Q2 2018 earnings call, and the iMac turning 20. The show finishes with a quick rundown of a few other Apple related stories that made the news in April.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP56-April2018.mp3"]
Notable Numbers
  • Apple Music Tops 40 Million Subscribers, Gets a Vice President — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Related: Apple is Giving Apple Music Trial Subscribers an Extra Free Month — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Related: Spotify beefs up its free tier — social.techcrunch.com/…
  • US Insurance firm EverQuote found that 80% of users of it’s EverDrive app tried iOS’s new DND while Driving feature, and 70% continued to use it — tidbits.com/… & www.everquote.com/…
Notable Comings & Goings
  • Apple has hired John Giannandrea, former chief of search & AI at Google. Tim Cook makes a point of emphasising that John shares Apple’s values, including their commitment to privacy — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple has reportedly hired Jon McCormack away from Amazon where he was Chief Technology Officer of their devices group. He’s also been chief of software operations at HP, VP of software for Kindle at Amazon, and was with Google’s Advanced Technology & Products Group — www.macobserver.com/…
Main Stories
  1. Bloomberg reports that Apple is going to switch to its own processors for Macs — www.bloomberg.com/…
    • Why the next Mac processor transition won’t be like the last two — www.macworld.com/…
    • ARM Mac: Piece of Cake Or Gas Refinery? — mondaynote.com/…
    • The Fifth Age Of Macintosh: What Happens If Apple Dumps Intel? — www.fastcompany.com/…
  2. Apple continues it’s environmental push:
    • Apple reaches it’s goal of 100% renewable energy — www.fastcompany.com/…, www.macobserver.com/… & www.apple.com/…
    • For earth day Apple unveiled Daisy, a new and better robot for recycling iPhones (replacing Liam), and started to make donations when ever Apple products are recycled using their GiveBack program — www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • Green Peace still find a way to criticise Apple — www.macobserver.com/…
  3. It’s official, Apple exits the router business with the discontinuation of their AirPort line — tidbits.com/…
    • Apple provides advice for choosing a router to its support pages — support.apple.com/…
    • How to keep using Time Machine when the AirPort Time Capsule is discontinued — www.imore.com/…
  4. Apple’s Q2 2018 Earnings Call — www.apple.com/…
    • Contrary to what Analysts thought, iPhone X is doing well
      • iPhone X Alone Generated 35% of the Total Handset Industry Profits in Q4 2017 — www.counterpointresearch.com/… (research published two weeks before the earnings call!)
      • Techpinions found 97% customer satisfaction for iPhone X with 85% very satisfied — techpinions.com/… (research released a week before the earnings call)
      • iPhone X was the best-selling iPhone model each and every week over the quarter, and the best selling iPhone model in China — www.imore.com/…
      • Sounds Like It’s Samsung’s Flexible OLED Phones Whose Sales Are Weak — daringfireball.net/…
      • Warren Buffett: Obsessing over iPhone X sales in the near term ‘totally misses the point’ on Apple’s stock — www.loopinsight.com/…
      • Apple Valued at $901 Billion on Record High, Warren Buffet Buys Even More Shares — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Watch now the size of a Fortune 300 company — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Pay will soon be in 24 markets and accounts for 90% of mobile payments — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple announced a $100bn share re-purchase authorisation as well as a 16% increase in the quarterly dividend — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
    • Tim Cook called privacy a ‘fundamental human right’ — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Transcript: Apple CEO Tim Cook on the company’s 2018 Q2 earnings — www.imore.com/…
  5. The iMac Turns 20!
    • 20 years of iMac: A story of relentless design iteration — 9to5mac.com/…
    • 20 Years of the iMac — tidbits.com/…
Quick Stories
  • The new MacPro will not be ready until 2019, and it will be ‘modular’ — tidbits.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • In a Leaked Memo, Apple Warns Employees to Stop Leaking Information — www.bloomberg.com/…
  • Apple reveals special edition Product Red iPhone 8 and 8 Plus smartphones — arstechnica.com/… (there is no Product Red iPhone X, and the Product Red versions of the iPhone 7 & iPhone 7S have been discontinued — www.imore.com/…)
  • Apple have launched a battery replacement program for non-touch-bar 13-inch MacBook Pros — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple Acknowledges Microphone Issue With Some iPhone 7 and 7 Plus Models on iOS 11.3 and Later — www.macrumors.com/…
  • In an interview with the Sydney Morning Herald Tim Cook made it clear iOS and macOS are not merging — www.smh.com.au/…
  • iTunes has finally made it into the Windows store (important for Windows S users who can only run apps from the app store) — arstechnica.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple shutting down Texture’s Windows magazine app after acquisition — www.theverge.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 57 (May 2018)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak
  • Allister Jenks - @zkarj
The show starts with a quick update on the eternal Apple -v- Samsung trial before moving on to the five main stories for the month. First a collection of App Store related stories including government censorship, a developer's union, a whole kerfuffle around the Steam iOS app, and a challenge to Apple's pricing model from Microsoft. Second, the on-going controversy over Apple's so-called Butterfly Keyboards. Third, the release of two long-awaited products, AirPlay 2, and iCloud messages. Fourth, Microsoft's Hub 2. And finally, Google's Duplex 'demo'. The show finishes with a quick rundown of a few other Apple related stories that made the news in May.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP57-May2018.mp3"]

Legal Latest

  • Apple awarded $533.3M (down from ~$1Bn in the original trial) in the re-trial of the never-ending Apple -v- Samsung case (this is probably still not over, Samsung may very well appeal again) — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…

Main Stories

  1. An eventful month for Apple’s App Stores
    • Probably related to GDPR, Apple has started to crack down on apps that share location data with third parties — arstechnica.com/…
      • Apps that are not asking for clear enough consent before sharing location data with a third party are being pulled from the store, with developers told to remove the sharing or ask for clear consent and then re-submit the apps.

      • Apple has also tightened the rules on what third parties can do with the location data after its shared with them:

        Data collected from apps may not be used or shared with third parties for purposes unrelated to improving the user experience or software/hardware performance connected to the app’s functionality, or to serve advertising in compliance with the Apple Developer Program License Agreement

    • Government Censorship
      • Apple was forced to remove apps that use CallKit (facilitates VOIP calling) from their Chinese app store — www.imore.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
      • Russia forced Apple to remove Telegram from their Russian stores, and there seems to have been some collateral damage, with the Telegram developers reporting that they can’t submit app updates for their apps at all ATM — www.imore.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
      • Starting with the next reporting period (from July 2018), Apple will include government app removal requests in their regular transparency reports — www.macobserver.com/…

    • A small number of indie developers have banded together to form The Developers Union, and ask Apple to bring free trials to the store by WWDC 2019, they plan to move on to campaign for other app store changes that will benefit developers — arstechnica.com/…, www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…

    • The Steam Link Controversy
      • Apple initially approved a Steam Link app for iOS — the app is basically screen sharing for gaming, allowing an iOS user to remotely play a game served from a steam-connected device on the same local area network — www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
      • After Valve publicly announced that Steam Link had been approved, Apple changed their mind, and yanked the app — arstechnica.com/…
    • Microsoft put pressure on Apple by lowering their cut on their store (for most, but not all, purchases) — blogs.windows.com/…
      • Games remain at a 70/30% split
      • Consumer apps get an 85/15% split when Microsoft actively sends the customer to the developer through some kind of promotion
      • Otherwise, consumers app get a 95/5% split
  2. Controversy continues to swirl around Apple’s divisive new Butterfly keyboard design
    • The class-action lawsuits have begun to fly — theoutline.com/…
    • AppleInsider conducted an investigation and found that while laptops with the new keyboards are more reliable overall, the one component that’s less reliable than before is the keyboard — appleinsider.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
  3. iOS 11.4 & MacOS 13.5 finally deliver on two long-announced and long-awaited features:
    • Airplay 2
      • Apple’s List of 32 Speakers Besides HomePod that Will Support AirPlay 2 — www.macobserver.com/…
      • How to use AirPlay 2 on iOS: An in-depth analysis — appleinsider.com/…
      • Airplay 2 FAQ: Everything you need to know! — www.imore.com/…
    • iCloud Messages
      • How to sync your text messages to iCloud — www.imore.com/…
      • So How Secure is Messages in iCloud Anyway? — www.macobserver.com/…
  4. Microsoft Previewed their up-coming Surface Hub 2 – a 50" 4K touch screen tablet designed for use within organisations to facilitate team work — blogs.windows.com/…
    • The device also contains a 4K camera.
    • Up to four of the devices can be tiled together to create a single massive work-space.
    • The individual units can be used like very smart flip-charts, and when connected into larger grids they become more like smart whiteboards.
    • Microsoft will be trialling the devices with some select customers this year, and general availability is expected in 2019 (no mention of price, but don’t expect it to be cheap🙂).
  5. Google Previewed a Duplex, an AI agent that can make voice calls on behalf of humans and is designed to interact with humans over the phone like a human would. The preview was in the form of a pre-created video, not a live demo, and there was no live demos given to the media afterwards.
    • It’s not clear how contrived or not the video was:
      • What Google isn’t telling us about its AI demo — www.axios.com/…
      • On Getting to the Bottom of Google Duplex — www.macobserver.com/…
    • The demo raised a lot of legal and privacy concerns:
      • Does Google’s Duplex violate two-party consent laws? — social.techcrunch.com/…
      • Is Google’s Duplex AI helpful or plain creepy? — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
      • The problem isn’t Duplex or AI. It’s Google. — www.imore.com/…
      • Yammering on One More Time Regarding Google’s Duplex Recordings — daringfireball.net/…

Quick Stories

  • The have FBI admitted that they repeatedly over-stated the number of encrypted cellphones they’re trying to break into by a factor of about six, misleading the US Congress and the public — www.imore.com/… & nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
  • Apple continues to expand its Everyone Can Code program by partnering with schools for the blind and deaf across America — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple’s many year on-going commitment to the environment was well illustrated with news that it helped drive and fund Elysis, a partnership between Aluminium giants Alcoa and Rio Tinto to develop a revolutionary new Carbon-free Aluminium smelting process (regular Aluminium smelting releases a lot of CO2), but this new process releases Oxygen instead — www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
  • In related news, Environmental Law Institute (ELI) has awarded Lisa Jackson (Apple’s VP in charge of their environmental initiatives) their 2018 Environmental Achievement Award — www.eli.org/…
  • There have been two developments in Apple’s unexpected shutdown iPhone battery replacement program:
    • Apple have announced that batteries are now available without delay — www.macrumors.com/…
    • Apple have announced that they’ll be issuing refunds to customers who paid the full price for a replacement before the program was announced — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple’s $29 battery replacement program: what you need to know — www.imore.com/…
  • The sale of Toshiba’s memory division has been finalised for $18Bn. The new owner isK.K. Pange a consortium which includes Apple and is lead by Bain Capital — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple have created a new Music Publishing Division within the company, but it’s not clear what they’re going to use it for yet, so stay tuned! — tidbits.com/…
  • Apple have increased their autonomous vehicle fleet in California to 55 vehicles with 83 registered drivers (second largest fleet in the state after GM Cruise with 104 vehicles and head of Waymo and Tesla with 51 and 39 vehicles respectively) — macreports.com/…
  • Apple has confirmed that they’ll be experimenting with drones in North Carolina in an attempt to improve Apple maps. The experiments are part of a program being run in the state to test drone use beyond what’s currently permitted by the standard FAA rules, and Apple stressed that the drones will be used in accordance with its strong pro-privacy stance — 9to5mac.com/…
  • Google announced and demoed Cloud Anchor, a new cross-platform API for sharing an augmented reality (AR) experience that works between devices running Android and iOS, and the first app using the framework is already out (Just a Line, an app that lets users draw lines in a shared AR environment) — www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
Reminder — Apple’s 2018 WWDC Keynote will be Live-streamed on the 4th of June
  • Here’s How to Watch Apple’s WWDC 2018 Keynote Live Stream — www.macobserver.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 58 (June 2018)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Kelly Guimont from App Camp for Girls - @verso
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh
The show starts with a few followup items before moving on to look at some Apple-related legal stories that broke in June, including the end of the epic Apple -v- Samsung case. Next up is a quick look at some new hires at Apple, and then the show moves on to the three main stories. By far the biggest story is WWDC 2018, the second main story is Apple's deals with Opera and Sesame Street, and the final main story is the US Supreme Court's ruling on cellphone location data. The show finishes with a quick rundown of a few smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in June.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP58-June2018.mp3"]
Followup
  • Steam Link
    • Shortly after LTA 57 was recorded Apple updated their developer guidelines to make it more clear what the problem was with Steam Link — it was indeed about the 30% cut — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Steam removed the purchasing feature from the betas of Steam Link for iOS — toucharcade.com/…
    • No further developments, but the expectation is that Steam will be able to develop a version of that app that makes it into the store
  • Apple have launched a replacement service for their controversial butterfly keyboards — www.imore.com/…
  • Sonos announced and AirPlay2 software update coming in July, and a new compact sound bar named Beam — www.cnet.com/…
  • Apple have released the Schoolwork app for teachers announced at March’s education event — tidbits.com/…
Legal Latest
  • Apple -v- Samsung:
    • Earlier in the month the fight was still live with Samsung demanding yet another retrial — www.macobserver.com/…
    • On June 27, Apple & Samsung settled the case. No details have been released — www.imore.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple -v- Qualcomm: Apple have opened a new front in this battle by challenging the validity of four Qualcomm patents with the US Patent & Trademark Office (US PTO) — www.bloomberg.com/…
Apple Staff Comings & Goings
  • Apple Hires Development Exec Layne Eskridge from Netflix — www.macobserver.com/…
  • George Ergatoudis out at Spotify after two years - to join Apple Music — www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/…
  • YouTuber Mark Rober Secretly Develops VR for Self-Driving Cars for Apple (EXCLUSIVE) — variety.com/…
Main Stories
  1. WWDC 2018: watch the keynote — www.apple.com/… & All of Apple’s big announcements from WWDC 2018 — www.imore.com/…
    • Cross-Platform Updates
      • FaceTime Group Chats brings video conferencing for up to 32 people on Mac & iOS, with voice-only support on Apple Watch — www.imore.com/… & www.theverge.com/…
      • Continued focus on security & privacy across all OS updates — arstechnica.com/…, www.imore.com/…, www.intego.com/… & www.intego.com/…
        • Mac & iOS versions of Safari getting more clever privacy protections — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
        • MacOS gets more user-permission prompts for things like microphone access — www.macobserver.com/…
        • The keychain on iOS gets a big revamp, and an API has been added to allow 3rd-party password managers integrate with the OS — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
        • iOS 12 brings USB Restricted Mode, a feature designed to make it harder to crack locked iOS devices — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/… & www.loopinsight.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
        • Apple updated the their developer rules to ban the creation and selling of user contact databases from users address books — arstechnica.com/…
      • Continuity Camera lets you take a photo via your iPhone on your Mac — www.imore.com/…
      • Free trials are sorta-kinda coming to the App Stores — www.macobserver.com/… & bitsplitting.org/…
      • Apple is continuing to develop it’s health-related services:
        • The Health Records API is now open to developers — www.loopinsight.com/…
        • Apple announced Research Kit 2.0 with some new features to improve the user experience and to improve the data that can be gathered — www.macobserver.com/…
      • The small details of iOS 12, macOS Mojave, and more — sixcolors.com/…
      • Platforms State of the Union: Important highlights from the event — www.imore.com/…
    • MacOS 10.14 Mojave — www.apple.com/…
      • Dark Mode — www.imore.com/…
      • Finder improved with desktop stacks, gallery view & Quick Actions in Quickview — www.imore.com/…
      • Major App Store revamp, both in terms of UI and in terms of sandbox improvements to facilitate more power apps . Big-name apps announced as coming or returning including Microsoft Office365, Transmit & BBEdit — www.idownloadblog.com/…, www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
      • Significant improvements to screenshots and desktop recording — www.imore.com/…
      • Home app comes to Mojave — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple previewed technology they are working on to make it easier to port iOS apps to the Mac. Are using it to bring some of their own iOS apps to Mojave — www.wired.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
      • Mojave supports many old Macs, but not every Mac that runs High Sierra will run Mojave — www.macobserver.com/…
      • iOS 12: Five Secret Features Apple NEVER announced! - YouTube — www.youtube.com/…
      • macOS Mojave: A Roundup of All the Little Things — www.macstories.net/…
      • macOS Mojave: A visual tour of Dark Mode and other major features — arstechnica.com
      • Hands-on with macOS 10.14 Mojave — www.loopinsight.com/…
      • macOS Mojave FAQ: Everything you need to know! — www.imore.com/…
    • iOS 12 — www.apple.com/…
      • Big focus on efficiency, particularly on older devices. All devices that run iOS 11 will run iOS 12 — arstechnica.com/…
      • Screen Time lets users monitor their phone & tablet usage and set limits and controls. Integrated with parental controls for families — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…
        • Tim Cook reveals that he was surprised by how much time he spent on his Phone — tidbits.com/…
      • Siri Shortcuts brings the power of Workflow into the core OS and allows users to define and name custom actions — www.macstories.net/… & www.imore.com/…
        • Siri Shortcuts: How Apple is keeping your data private and secure — www.imore.com/…
      • Notifications & Do Not Disturb get important improvements (grouping of notifications, in-notification control of notification settings, and Do Not Disturb for X time and more) — www.imore.com/…
      • ARKit 2 bring significant improvements — arstechnica.com/…
        • New built-in Measure app illustrates some of the power — www.imore.com/…
        • Niantic shows off a stunning AR demo that lets Pikachu hide behind real-world objects — www.loopinsight.com/…
      • Memoji lets users create their own Animoji — www.imore.com/…
        • Unlike Samsung’s AR Emoji, Memoji are gender neutral — www.refinery29.com/…
      • iBooks becomes Apple Books — www.imore.com/…
      • Live Listening lets you use your iPhone as a remote mic for AirPods (not announce at keynote, but included in iOS 12 betas)
      • 100 new iOS 12 features/changes — www.loopinsight.com/…
      • iOS 12 FAQ: Everything you need to know! — www.imore.com/…
    • WatchOS 5
      • Support for original Apple Watch dropped — www.imore.com/…
      • Auto-detection of workout start and finish — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Walkie Talkie feature added — www.imore.com/… & www.loopinsight.com/…
      • watchOS 5: Everything you need to know! — www.imore.com/…
    • tvOS: very little announced other than support for Dolby Atmos on on 4K AppleTVs — arstechnica.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • CarPlay: very little announced other than support for 3rd-party navigation apps — techcrunch.com/…
    • These are the WWDC 2018 Apple Design Award Winners! — www.imore.com/…
