    • President Trump hints he’s “thinking about” excluding Apple from tariffs — www.imore.com/…
    • Trump impressed by Apple CEO Tim Cook, calls Apple a “great American company” — www.imore.com/…
    • ‘Tim Cook Calls Donald Trump Directly,’ President Reveals — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Foxconn could pivot iPhone production to India even amidst tough challenges — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Apple won’t charge us for any cost increases caused by U.S.-China trade war — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: iOS 13’s beta split is down to Trump’s threatened tariffs, not missed features — medium.com/…
  4. The Siri Grading Kerfuffle Comes to a Satisfactory End — the grading will be re-enabled, but it will be opt-in, and performed by Apple employees, not contractors. Apple also issued an apology:
    • Apple’s article addressing Siri privacy: Improving Siri’s privacy protections — www.apple.com/…
    • Apple apologizes for Siri recording controversy, says program is returning in fall with major changes — www.imore.com/…
    • You have to disable Siri to prevent Apple from retaining transcripts — www.imore.com/…
    • Irish Contractors Listened to 1,000 Siri Recordings Per Shift, Alleges Ex-Employee — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple were not alone in using humans to grade their voice assistants’ performance:
      • Facebook got humans to listen in on some Messenger voice chats — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
      • Humans may have been listening to you via your Xbox — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
      • Microsoft won’t shift on AI recordings policy — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • The Irish Data Protection Commissioner is investigating whether the Siri Grading breached the GDPR — www.irishexaminer.com/…
    • Apple is being sued over the Siri recording fiasco — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: Why Can’t Users Teach Siri about Its Mistakes? — tidbits.com/…
    • Related: Siri Answers 83% of Questions Correctly in Test, Beating Alexa But Trailing Google Assistant — www.macrumors.com/…
    • Related: Apple testing smarter Siri web answers for Spotlight search queries — 9to5mac.com/…

Notable Numbers

  • The smart speaker market continues to grow, but Amazon remains dominant, and the Home Pod’s 5% share is not growing — www.macrumors.com/…
    • Related: Apple’s HomePod is going on sale in Japan on August 23rd — www.imore.com/…
  • iPhone market share dips in Europe as competitors gain ground with mid-range devices — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: iPhone users are upgrading more slowly than ever, says report — www.imore.com/…
  • The Apple Watch continues to dominate wearables with 5.7 million units shipped in Q2 2019 — www.imore.com/… & Apple Watch continues to dominate wearables in North America — www.imore.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has hired Dr. Andrew Trister away form Apple’s Health team — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Microsoft Hires Former Siri Boss Bill Stasior — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple hires 33 more test drives for it’s autonomous car fleet in CA — www.imore.com/…

Main Stories

  1. A Mixed Month for the Security of Apple Products
    • Apple released security updates that contained a regression bug, re-introducing a vulnerability that had been previously patched. This enabled a jailbreak of the most up-to-date iPhone for the first time in many years. Apple quickly issued fresh updates to re-patch the vulnerability!
      • Public jailbreak released after Apple mistakenly reverses vulnerability — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple Issues Emergency Updates for All Its Operating Systems — tidbits.com/…
    • Google’s Project Zero found and critical iOS bug that was being used to silently hack iPhones that simply visited a website back in February, and Apple patched it within 6 days.
      • Mysterious iOS Attack Changes Everything We Know About iPhone HackingMenuSearchFacebookTwitterEmailFacebookTwitterEmailTwitterTwitterFacebookTwitterPinterestYoutubeInstagram — www.wired.com/…
      • Google uncovers collection of malicious sites that secretly hacked iPhones for years — www.imore.com/…
      • Sophisticated iPhone hacking went unnoticed for over two years — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • Apple announced significant upgrades to their security programs:
      • Apple to supply security researchers with special iPhones — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple vastly expands security bounty program: higher payouts, ‘dev’ devices, Mac support — 9to5mac.com/…
      • Apple’s new $1 million bug bounty program: What you need to know — www.imore.com/…
  2. Apple’s Complex Relationship with Indie Repairs:
    • iOS has started showing a warning when it detects that an iPhone’s battery has not been installed by an authorised repairer, and disabling the battery health preference pane on such devices. Note that the phone is not disabled and the battery continues to function as normal:
      • Apple disabling battery health monitoring following third party repairs — www.imore.com/…
      • Is Apple Locking iPhone Batteries to Discourage Repair? — www.imore.com/…
      • Here’s Apple’s statement on the iPhone ‘battery lock’ controversy — www.imore.com/…
      • Opinion: Your right to repair stops where Apple’s liability begins — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple have launched a new Independent Repair Providers program to allow third parties perform out-of-warranty repairs with genuine Apple parts, genuine Apple tools, and using the same manuals Apple’s Authorised Repair Providers use (US-only for now, but expected to expand soon):
      • Apple’s new program makes indies right for iPhone repair — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple gives third-party repair shops more access to authorized parts — arstechnica.com
      • Apple Offers Genuine iPhone Parts and Tools to Independent Repair Shops — tidbits.com/…
  3. Apple’s CEO Tim Cook joins 180 other CEOs to sign an open letter committing Apple to a new vision of corporate responsibly spearheaded by the Business Roundtable:
    • The commitments the CEOs signed their names to: Statement on the Purpose of a Corporation — opportunity.businessroundtable.org/…

Quick Stories

  • A number of airlines have banned some or all 15" MacBooks from checked and/or carry-on baggage:
    • 🇺🇸 In keeping with its policy of not allowing devices with recalled batteries on flights, the FAA has banned 15" MacBooks eligible for a voluntary battery recall that have not had their battery replaced from all flights in the US — www.imore.com/…
    • Virgin Australia bans all MacBooks from checked luggage over battery concerns — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple’s 15-inch MacBook Pro banned from checked luggage on Qantas flights due to fire risk — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple partners with RESOLVE to responsibly source gold for its products — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple’s Press Release: Searching for gold with habitat restoration in mind — www.apple.com/…
  • Apple and Eli Lilly are studying whether data from iPhones and Apple Watches can detect signs of dementia — www.cnbc.com/…
  • Apple Music News:
    • Apple Music Launches Apple Digital Masters, New Initiative Combining Its Hi-Res ‘Mastered’ Collection — www.billboard.com/…
    • Apple Music launches new ‘Shazam Discovery’ playlist to highlight emerging artists — www.imore.com/…
    • Amazon Alexa brings Apple Music support to even more countries — www.imore.com/…
    • Porsche is building Apple Music right into its Taycan EV sports car — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple have opened up an early access program (open to Apple employees only) for their up-coming gaming subscription:
    • Apple running early access program for Apple Arcade, here’s what it looks like — 9to5mac.com/…
    • Early gameplay preview of Apple Arcade shows how the new service will work — www.imore.com/…
    • 🎦 Hands on with six Apple Arcade games — www.loopinsight.com/…
  • Apple brings contactless student IDs on iPhone and Apple Watch to more universities — www.apple.com/…
  • 🇩🇰 🇫🇮 🇳🇴 🇸🇪 Danske Bank customers in Denmark, Finland, Norway & Sweden get Apple Pay — www.macobserver.com/…
  • 🇺🇸 Apple Adds Allscripts to Health Records — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Mozilla Inspires the New WebKit Tracking Prevention Policy — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple’s policy: WebKit Tracking Prevention Policy — webkit.org/…
  • Apple has launched AR art walking tours in in six major cities around the world (Hong Kong, London, New York, Paris, San Francisco & Tokyo) — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Transforms Central Park Into an Augmented Reality Gallery — www.nytimes.com/…
  • 🇮🇳 India liberalizes foreign investment rules in a win for Apple — techcrunch.com/…
  • Apple iPhone 11 event announced for September 10 — www.imore.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 73 (September 2019)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh

The show starts with a look at some followups to previous stories including the Project Zero bug and tariffs on the Mac Pro. Next is a quick look at some quick Apple HR and acquisition news. The four main stories are the so-called Checkm8 un-patchable jailbreak, developments in Apple services (specifically Apple TV+ & Apple Arcade), new Apple OSes (mostly iOS), and new Apple hardware. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple-related stories that made the news in September.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP73-September2019.mp3"]

Followup

  1. The Project Zero iPhone Vulnerabilities & Exploits
    • We now know the vulnerabilities detailed by Google’s project zero were used by the Chinese Government to target the Uyghur Muslim community — techcrunch.com/…, daringfireball.net/… & tidbits.com/…
    • We can also now place the attacks in a larger context where other bugs in other OSes were also used by the Chinese government to target the Uyghurs — www.imore.com/…, gizmodo.com/…, www.forbes.com/… & nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • Apple released a message about the hacks. They disputed Google’s original 2-year timeline, and their use of the phrase “mass exploitation”, saying instead that the attacks were targeted at the Uyghurs and lasted for about 2 months. Apple also said they were already aware of the bugs and working on patches when they were contacted by Project Zero — www.apple.com/…
    • Project Zero have been criticised for not sharing information around the use of the vulnerabilities in a responsible way — vector.libsyn.com/…
  2. Apple’s European court case against the EU Commission’s €13Bn ‘tax’ bill in Ireland got under way (it’s expected to last months and to be appealed to the ECJ, which could take years):
    • A great summary of how things stood before the case opened: Explainer: Apple’s €13bn tax appeal has huge implications — www.irishtimes.com/…
    • Apple says $14 billion EU tax order ‘defies reality and common sense’ — www.reuters.com/…
    • Apple CFO Luca Maestri will lead appeal against the European Commission’s $14 billion order — www.imore.com/…
    • EU Tax Bill ‘Defies Reality and Common Sense,’ Says Apple — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Claims EU Does Not Understand Its Business — www.macobserver.com/…
  3. Government Investigations of Apple continue:
    • 🇺🇸 House Judiciary Committee Investigating Apple Regarding ‘Competition in Digital Markets’ (PDF) — daringfireball.net/…
    • 🇺🇸 Congress wants Facebook, Google, Apple, and Amazon emails as probe heats up — arstechnica.com
    • 🇺🇸 U.S. Congress asks Spotify to provide details on Apple’s alleged anticompetitive practices — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: The NYT reported that Apple changed its app store algorithm so it favours Apple’s own apps less. Apple say the algorithm was not giving them an unfair advantage, but instead that they’re handicapped their own apps for the good of the ecosystem — www.nytimes.com/…
    • Related: Not to be out-done, the Washington Post featured a story attacking Apple for copying good ideas from apps in the app store: About That Washington Post Story on Apple Copying Features From Top Apps in the App Store — daringfireball.net/…
  4. The Mac Pro and the US/China Tariff War:
    • Apple were granted 10 of the 15 tariff exemptions they applied for for the new Mac Pro — www.imore.com/…
    • Redesigned Mac Pro will be made in the US — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple denied tariff relief on five Mac Pro components — www.imore.com/… & Apple to Pay 25% Tariff on Chinese-Made Mac Pro Components — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple is investing $1 billion in India in efforts to move production outside of China — www.imore.com/…
  5. Apple Card:
    • Walgreens joins Apple Card’s rewards program to offer 3% Daily Cash on purchases — techcrunch.com/…
    • T-Mobile is the Only Wireless Provider to Offer 3% Daily Cash on Apple Card — www.t-mobile.com/…
    • Apple Card now accepted through Apple’s Trade In Program — www.imore.com/…
  6. Galaxy Fold:
    • Samsung is canceling all Galaxy Fold preorders so it can ‘rethink the entire customer experience’ — www.theverge.com/…
    • The Galaxy Fold is now available for purchase in the US — techcrunch.com/…
    • Review: Samsung’s Galaxy Fold is finally here. Handle with care — www.washingtonpost.com/…
    • Related: Microsoft announced their own folding phone, but it won’t ship until late 2020 — thenextweb.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • Starbucks picks up Apple VP Isabel Ge Mahe to go — www.imore.com/…
  • Disney CEO Bob Iger resigns from Apple board as competition between the two companies nears — www.imore.com/…
  • Steve Dowling, Apple’s VP of Communications is leaving. Phill Schiller will take over his responsibilities until he’s replaced — www.vox.com/…
  • Apple Hires AstraZeneca Chief Information Officer David Smoley — www.bloomberg.com/…
  • Apple confirms buyout of UK effects firm iKinema — www.imore.com/…

Main Stories

  1. The Checkm8 iOS vulnerability
    • Summary:
      • An un-patchable vulnerability has been found in the bootrom in Apple SOCs from the A5 up to and including the A11, this means all iPhones from the 1Phone 4S up to an including the iPhone X are vulnerable.
      • The exploit requires the phone to be tethered to a computer via the lightning port to work, so cannot be exploited remotely
      • Exploits are not permanent, so do not survive a reboot
      • The vulnerability does not in any way affect the secure enclave, so it cannot be used to break into a locked device
      • The vulnerability does enable an un-patchable tethered jail break
    • Checkm8, the iPhone 4s to iPhone X bootrom exploit, explained — www.imore.com/…
    • New Checkm8 jailbreak released for all iOS devices running A5 to A11 chips — www.zdnet.com/…
    • Developer of Checkm8 explains why iDevice jailbreak exploit is a game changer — arstechnica.com
    • Checkm8 jailbreak and AltStore put cracks in Apple’s walled garden — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
  2. New Services
    • Apple TV+ will launch on 1 November in 100 countries and will cost $4.99 per month for a family:
      • Apple’s TV+: Everything you need to know! — www.imore.com/…
      • You’ll get Apple TV+ for 1 year free with the purchase of an iPhone, iPad, iPod touch, or Apple TV, but only once — www.imore.com/…
      • Oprah’s Book Club Coming to Apple TV+ and Apple Books — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple TV+: What’s New, Release Dates, Actors, and More — www.imore.com/…
      • Related: Disney bundle with Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN+ is just $12.99 — www.imore.com/… & D23 members get 33% off a three-year subscription to Disney+ (yes, even the free membership) — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Arcade:
      • Apple Arcade launched at $4.99 per month for the whole family — arstechnica.com
      • Apple has almost 100 developer studios making games for Apple Arcade — www.imore.com/…
      • Some Apple Arcade titles will be available on console, too — www.imore.com/…
      • All Apple Arcade Games available now (and what’s coming soon) — www.imore.com/…
      • Opinion: Early review suggests Apple Arcade struggling with 4K — www.imore.com/…
      • Related: Google introduces Play Pass in Response to Apple Arcade — www.macobserver.com/…
  3. New OSes — arstechnica.com/…
    • As well as releasing new OSes for modern devices, Apple also provided security patches for some older OSes so older devices that can’t upgrade can still be protected:
      • Apple issues iOS 13.1.1 and security updates for every OS, even iOS 12 — www.intego.com/…
      • Apple releases watchOS 5.3.2 for Apple Watch Series 1 and Series 2 — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple is releasing macOS Catalina in October — techcrunch.com/…
    • iOS 13 (quick-rolling bug fix and security updates — first 13.0, then 13.1, then 13.1.1, then 13.1.2) — arstechnica.com/…
      • Adds new Bluetooth permission prompt to combat user tracking. Already catching out apps like Facebook:
        • Facebook says location data in iOS 13, Android 10 may be confusing — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
        • Facebook: Remember how we promised we weren’t tracking your location? Psych! Can’t believe you fell for that — www.theregister.co.uk/…
        • The new iPhone software update is already catching apps like Facebook being shady — www.businessinsider.com/…
      • There are of course legitimate reasons for apps to request Bluetooth access: Here’s why so many apps are asking to use Bluetooth on iOS 13 — www.theverge.com/…
    • How to use text editing gestures on iPhone — www.imore.com/…
    • How to use external hard drives with your iPhone or iPad in iOS 13 and iPadOS 13 — www.imore.com/…
    • How to keep your iPhone personal hotspot always on in iOS 13 — www.imore.com/…
    • Spotify Getting Siri Support in iOS 13 — www.macobserver.com/…
    • There is a matching version of iPad OS for each iOS:
      • How to use a mouse or trackpad with your iPhone or iPad — www.imore.com/…
    • tvOS 13 brings Apple Arcade and nascent multi-account support
      • Opinion: tvOS 13: The MacStories Review - MacStories — www.macstories.net/…
  4. New Hardware
    • iPad:
      • iPad updated to 10.2" screen and starts at $329 — www.imore.com/…
        • iPad 7 Teardown Show Little Change — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple make its 1TB iPad Pro models much more appealing by slashing price by $200 — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Watch:
      • Apple Watch Series 5 gets Always-On Display and starts at $399. Re-gains ceramic option and gains titanium option — tidbits.com/… & arstechnica.com/…
      • Series 4 discontinued, but Series 3 retained and price dropped to $199
      • Apple Watch Series 5 teardown reveals it’s basically a Series 4 — www.imore.com/… & Teardown of 40mm Apple Watch Series 5 uncovers new battery design — www.imore.com/…
      • The Apple Watch Series 5 titanium model is 13% lighter than stainless steel model — www.imore.com/…
      • The Apple Watch’s noise detection feature is surprisingly very accurate — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple introduces new stylish two-tone Sport Loop bands — www.imore.com/…
      • What is an LTPO display? — www.pcworld.idg.com.au/…
      • Related: 7 out of 10 Apple Watch customers are first time buyers, not upgraders — 9to5mac.com/…
      • Opinion: Apple Watch Series 5 review roundup: The always-on display is a winner — www.imore.com/…
    • iPhones — arstechnica.com
      • 3 new iPhones:
        • iPhone 11, basically updated iPhone XR with dual camera, starting at $699
        • iPhone 11 Pro, successor to the iPhone XS, with triple camera, starting at $999
        • iPhone 11 Pro Max, successor to iPhone XS Max, also with triple camera, starting at $1099
      • Three older models retained with price drops:
        • iPhone XR to $599
        • iPhone 8 Plus to $549
        • iPhone 8 to $449
      • Tear-downs:
        • iFixit performs teardown of iPhone 11, here’s what’s inside — www.imore.com/…
        • iFixit Teardown of iPhone 11 Pro — www.macobserver.com/…
        • iFixit’s iPhone 11 Pro Max teardown finds higher-capacity battery, 4GB of RAM — arstechnica.com & iPhone 11 Pro Max Teardown — www.ifixit.com/…
      • Stress tests show that while not indestructible, the iPhones 11 are very rugged indeed:
        • iPhone 11 Pro survives grueling stress test with flying colors — www.imore.com/…
        • iPhone 11 and 11 Pro drop test: We couldn’t crack these phones, but we broke the camera — www.cnet.com/…
        • iPhone 11 drop tests prove even the toughest glass in a smartphone can break — www.imore.com/…
        • iPhone 11 bend test shows it’s built like a tank — www.imore.com/…
      • The iPhone 11 Pro has the best display on a smartphone, says DisplayMate — www.imore.com/…
        • Related: iPhone 11 will alert you when a non-genuine Apple display is installed — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple’s iPhone 11 Pro axes 3D Touch in favor of Haptic Touch — www.imore.com/… & Haptic Touch: The Ultimate Guide — www.imore.com/…
      • Here are the iPhone 11 and iPhone 11 Pro Camera Features — www.macobserver.com/…
      • I tested Night mode on iPhone 11 Pro in the worst possible lighting conditions and this is how it turned out — www.imore.com/… & Night Mode Showdown: iPhone 11 vs. Pixel 3 vs. Galaxy Note 10 vs. P30 Pro — www.imore.com/…
      • Why does the new iPhone 11 Pro have 3 cameras? — techcrunch.com/…
      • Multiple camera simultaneous recording coming to iPhone XS and iPhone XR, not just iPhone 11 — 9to5mac.com/…
      • An Exclusive Look Inside Apple’s A13 Bionic Chip — www.wired.com/…
      • The U1 chip in the iPhone 11 is the beginning of an Ultra Wideband revolution — sixcolors.com/…
      • iPhone 11 and iPhone 11 Pro Taptic Engines are made from 100% recycled Rare Earth Elements — www.imore.com/…
      • iPhone 11 Pro Max is the new king of Consumer Reports’ smartphone rankings — www.imore.com/…
      • Despite a lot of speculation that there was, it now seems there is no secret bilateral Qi charging hardware in the iPhones 11 — www.imore.com/…
      • According to analysts, the iPhones 11 are selling well:
        • iPhone 11 Pro and iPhone 11 Pro Max account for majority of preorders, says analyst — www.imore.com/…
        • Analyst says iPhone 11 demand is stronger than expected, possibly thanks to colors — www.imore.com/…
        • More analysts agreeing with Kuo, report strong iPhone 11 and iPhone 11 Pro demand — www.imore.com/…
        • New iPhone production reportedly increasing by up to 10% — www.imore.com/…
        • Analyst says iPhone 11 demand is stronger than expected, possibly thanks to colors — www.imore.com/…
        • iPhone launch massively popular in India — www.imore.com/…
      • Opinion: iPhone 11 review roundup: The iPhone most people should buy — www.imore.com/…
      • Opinion: iPhone 11 Pro review roundup: Amazing camera, mind-blowing battery life — www.imore.com/…
      • Opinion: Your new iPhone 11 doesn’t have 5G, but you shouldn’t care — www.cnet.com/…

Quick Stories

  • PSA: HomePod Supports Live Radio Requests, But Even UK Users Can’t Stream Most BBC Stations — www.macrumors.com/…
  • Apple News+ Now Available in Australia, UK — www.macobserver.com/…
  • New Repair Programs:
    • Apple begins a screen replacement program for aluminium Apple Watch Series 2 and Series 3 — www.imore.com/…
    • Some iPhone 6S units aren’t turning on, so Apple launched a repair program — arstechnica.com
  • Apple launches Apple Music web player for everyone — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple continuing its health push with the launch of three new studies into hearing, heart health, and menstrual cycles & reproduction — arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple Care Improvements:
    • Apple adds AppleCare+ to AirPods and Beats headphones — www.imore.com/…
    • AppleCare+ is now available as a monthly subscription for some devices — www.imore.com/…
    • Is Your AppleCare+ Expiring? You Can Now Renew It — tidbits.com/…
  • Apple introduces billing grace period for App Store subscriptions — www.imore.com/… & Apple’s Billing Grace Period Should Give You Peace of Mind — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple’s Social Responsibility Efforts:
    • Apple-backed China Clean Energy Fund has invested in three wind farms — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple teams up with Conservation International to save African grasslands — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple picks up a UN Climate Action Award — www.imore.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Apple’s Tim Cook and Deirdre O’Brien Urge Supreme Court to Protect Dreamers by Upholding DACA — www.macrumors.com/… & Apple CEO Tim Cook and VP Deirdre O’Brien offer support for DACA — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple schedules fiscal Q4 2019 earnings release for October 30th — 9to5mac.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 74 (October 2019)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak
  • Lynda Gousha from the Silicon Valley MUG - @llg4cdg

The show starts with a look at some followups to previous stories followed by some notable numbers, one quick legal star and two small Apple HR stories. The five main stories are Apple's China problem, Apple's flood of buggy software released and patches, Apple's new headphones, the launch of Apple TV+, and Apple's Q4 2019 earnings call. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple-related stories that made the news in October.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP74-October2019.mp3"]

Followup

  • Spotify has been updated with Siri support on iOS 13, CarPlay support, and an Apple TV app — www.macrumors.com/…
  • iPhone XR production has begun in India with iPhone 11 next up — www.imore.com/…
  • The US–China trade war rumbles on:
    • US-China trade talks cause for optimism as new tariffs may be “delayed” — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple asks for Tariff Exemptions on iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods — www.macobserver.com/…

Notable Numbers

  • Piper Jaffrey’s annual “Taking stock with Teens” report on US teens attitudes to tech has found that 83% own an iPhone (marginally up from 82% last year), and 86% want their next phone to be an iPhone — www.imore.com/…
  • The latest numbers from Sensor Tower show app revenue increased by almost a quarter to $21.9b in 2019 Q3 — www.imore.com/…
  • One-third of Apple Store customers now using Apple Trade In — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple Pay roasts Starbucks to become number one mobile payment system in US — www.imore.com/…

Legal Latest

  • Apple’s long-running fight against patent claims by the University of Wisconsin finally comes to an end with then US Supreme Court refusing to hear an appeal against Apple’s victory in the US Federal Circuit Court of Appeals in Washington — www.imore.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • Apple hires Columbia University Cardiologist in health push — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple gains five new VPs, including an early iPhone executive — www.imore.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Apple’s China Problem
    • Apple initially rejected HKmap.live, an app that mapped police & protestor locations in Hong Kong, then approved it, then removed it again:
      • Chinese state media condemns Apple decision to allow “poisonous” Hong Kong maps app in scathing attack — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple removes app that tracks Hong Kong police and protestors — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
      • Apple bans Hong Kong mapping app citing contravention of “guidelines and local laws” — www.imore.com/…
      • Tim Cook wrote a company-wide memo explaining Apple’s decision to remove the app:
        • Leaked memo shows Tim Cook agrees with Apple’s decision to remove Hong Kong mapping app — www.imore.com/…
        • Tim Cook Defends Removal of Hong Kong Protest App in Email to Apple Employees — www.macobserver.com/…
        • Related Opinion: Tim Cook’s Company-Wide Memo on HKmap.live Doesn’t Add Up — daringfireball.net/…
      • Hong Kong lawmaker says Apple should “uphold its commitment to free expression” — www.imore.com/…
      • 7 Bipartisan Lawmakers Urge Apple to Reinstate Hong Kong Protestor App — www.macobserver.com/…
      • AOC and Ted Cruz wade into Apple’s China censorship debate — www.imore.com/…
    • There’s a brief kerfuffle as some wrongly assume Apple have started sending browsing data to Chinese firm Tencent:
      • Here’s Apple’s statement on Safari Fraudulent Website Warning and Tencent — www.imore.com/…
      • Code Reveals Tencent Only Gets Your Data if Your Device’s Region is Set to China — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple has removed the Quartz news app from the Chinese App Store at the request of the Chinese government — www.imore.com/…
    • Tim Cook named chairman at China’s Tsinghua University’s School of Economics and Management — www.imore.com/…
    • Report suggests Apple told TV+ content creators not to paint China in a bad light — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion & Analysis:
      • 8 numbers that explain why Apple is kowtowing to China — www.wired.co.uk/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 75 (November 2019)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak
  • Nick Riley - @spligosh

The show starts with a look at some followups to stories from previous months before jumping into some notable numbers released in November. Next is a single legal story and three HR stories. The five main stories are an alleged gender bias in AppleCard credit limits, the removal of Vaping apps from the App Store, Apple's Russian woes, the new 16" MacBook Pros, and Apple's complicated relationship with US President Donald Trump. The show finishes with a quick rundown of some other Apple-related stories that made the news in November.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP75-November2019.mp3"]

Followups

  • Apple’s purchase of Intel’s mobile chip business has completed — www.imore.com/…
    • Intel says it sold its modem business to Apple at a ‘multi-billion dollar loss’ because Qualcomm ‘strangled competition’ — www.businessinsider.com/…
    • Related: Apple says it remains committed to fair, reasonable, and non-discriminatory licensing of SEPs — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: Apple and Intel file antitrust lawsuit against patent troll — www.imore.com/…
  • As expected, Checkra1n ,the first jailbreak based on the checkm8 iOS boot loader bug has been released — arstechnica.com/…
  • Indian government says Apple is expanding its operations in the country — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: The iPhone was the top-selling premium smartphone in India in Q3 2019 — www.imore.com/…
  • According to reporting from Mark Gurman at Bloomberg, Apple have changed their development process for iOS 14 in an attempt to stop a recurrence of the very bumpy iOS 13 roll-out discussed in last month’s show — www.bloomberg.com/…
    • Related: iOS 13.2.2 Stops Killing Background Apps — tidbits.com/…
    • Related: Apple releases iOS and iPadOS 13.2.3 — arstechnica.com
    • Related: Apple to fix macOS email encryption bug in future software update — www.imore.com/…
  • The EU Competition Commissioner Margrethe Vestager has said many concerns have been raised with the commission regarding ApplePay — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple’s investment in a revolutionary new Aluminium smelting process starts to pay off: Apple has just bought its first ever batch of carbon-free aluminum — www.imore.com/…

Notable Numbers

  • Positive AppleWatch Numbers:
    • Apple Watch shipped 6.8 million units in Q3 2019, up 51% from last year — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Gets Closer to 50% Share of Smartwatch Sales — www.macobserver.com/…
    • 35% of iPhone users have a smartwatch, compared to just 16% of Android users — www.imore.com/…
  • Good news for Apple from the enterprise market:
    • Every company in the Fortune 500 uses Apple products… it’s not hard to see why — www.imore.com/…
    • IBM: Employees using Macs 22% more likely to exceed expectations compared to those using Windows — www.imore.com/…

Legal Latest

  • Apple -v- VirnetX takes another turn as the US Court of Appeals has vacated the damages awarded to VirnetX by a jury and sent it back to the lower court Texas to decide whether to re-calculate the damages or to hold a damages-only trial — www.imore.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • Kim Rozenfeld Steps Down As Apple Head Of Current Programming & Unscripted, Segues To First-Look Deal — deadline.com/…
  • Apple hires pro-Trump lobbyist Jeffrey Miller in its latest attempt to avoid trade tariffs — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple hires National Geographic’s former director of podcasts as it pushes towards original content — www.imore.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Aledged gender-bias in AppleCard credit limits
    • The New York Department of Financial Services have opened an investigation into Goldman Sachs following Tweets alleging gender bias in how AppleCard credit limits are set — www.imore.com/…, NY regulators investigating Apple Card after viral complaint of sexism — arstechnica.com & www.macobserver.com/…
    • Goldman Sachs will re-evaluate Apple Card credit limits after gender bias accusation — www.imore.com/…
    • Elizabeth Warren says that if Goldman Sachs can’t explain its Apple Card algorithm, it shouldn’t use it — www.imore.com/…
    • Senators Elizabeth Warren and Sherod Brown press for examination into Apple Card gender bias claims — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: AppleCard does continue to mature and improve:
      • Apple Card Beginning to Show Up on Credit Reports — www.macrumors.com/…
      • Nike Joins the 3% Cash Back Club for Apple Card — www.macobserver.com/…
  2. Apple has removed all Vaping apps from their App Store and updated their terms to exclude any new vaping apps
    • After CDC Report Apple Removes 181 Vaping Apps — www.macobserver.com/…
    • PAX hopes Apple will reconsider its decision to ban vaping apps from its App Store — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: L’Affaire Vaperware — daringfireball.net/…
  3. Russian Woes:
    • Apple Obeys Russian Demand to Change Crimea in Apple Maps — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple responds to Crimea outcry, says it will take “a deeper look” — www.imore.com/…
      • Related: Facebook made to ‘correct’ user’s post as Singapore flexes fake-news muscle — nakedsecurity.sophos.com/…
    • Putin signs law making Russian apps mandatory on smartphones, computers — www.reuters.com/…
      • Apple: new Russian phone sales legislation is ‘equivalent to jailbreaking’ — www.imore.com/…
      • Apple Threatens To Pull Out Of Russia Market Come 2020 — www.ibtimes.com/…
  4. Apple have released new 16" MacBook Pros — arstechnica.com/… & www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Removes 15-inch MacBook Pro for Sale — www.macobserver.com/…
    • The troublesome Butterfly Keyboard has been replaced by a re-designed scissor-switch keyboard based on the popular Magic Keyboard. The change has been mostly positively received — www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…

      • Apple’s Phil Schiller on reinventing the new MacBook Pro keyboard — www.cnet.com/…
      • Opinion: People won’t stop complaining about the MacBook Pro keyboard and it’s for a good reason — www.imore.com/…
    • Tech Specs:
      • A Look at the 16-Inch MacBook Pro’s Tech Specs — www.macobserver.com/…
      • MacBook Pro 2019: Specs compared — www.imore.com/…
      • 16-inch MacBook Pro benchmarks show marked improvement over 15-inch model — www.imore.com/…

    • Related: Apple confirms Mac Pro, Pro Display XDR will arrive in December — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: Apple fails to end MacBook ‘butterfly’ keyboard class action — www.reuters.com/…
  5. Trump & Apple — it’s complicated!

    • President Trump claims he ‘opened’ Apple’s 6-year-old Mac Pro plant in Texas yesterday — www.imore.com/…
    • Tim Cook Appears Alongside Trump in Re-Election Campaign Ad Shot in Mac Pro Plant in Austin — daringfireball.net/…
    • Apple CEO Tim Cook vows to fight for DACA until his ‘toes point up’ — www.imore.com/…
    • Tim Cook Urges United States to remain a member of the Paris Agreement — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: How Apple’s Tim Cook Mastered Donald Trump — www.forbes.com/…
    • Opinion: China, Russia, Trump, and Apple - Explained — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: Trump Gives U.S. Business the Ukraine Treatment — www.nytimes.com/…

Quick Stories

    • X-ray teardown shows just how smart the iPhone 11 Smart Battery Case is — www.imore.com/…

  • Apple Awards:

  • AppleWatch’s use in medical research continues:

  • Apple breaks ground on new campus in Austin, Texas — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple Rebuilds Privacy Site With ‘Everyday Apps Designed For Your Privacy’ — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple Pay Express is now live for TfL rides in London — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: How to Turn on Apple Pay Express Transit Mode in iOS 13 — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple to give $1 to (RED) for Apple Store purchases made with Apple Pay — www.imore.com/…

  • You can now buy Sony’s Dualshock 4 controller from Apple.com — www.imore.com/…

  • Sony updates some 2018 and 2019 TVs to support AirPlay 2 and HomeKit — www.imore.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 76 (December 2019)

  • Nick Riley - @spligosh

The show starts with a few followup stories, some notable numbers, a few legal stories, and some HR and acquisitions news. The five main stories are the new MacPro and XDR displays, the Connected Home over IP project, Apples continuing evolution on security, a re-kindling of the encryption debate in the US, and TIME magazine including three Apple devices in their top 10 gadgets of the decade.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

  • Apple’s Challenges with Authoritarian Regimes Continued in December:
    • European Parliament members ask Apple to reverse its decision on Crimea — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple TV+ could be banned in Russia if it grows too popular — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple removed chat app ToTok over concerns it was being used by the government of the UAE to spy on citizens — www.imore.com/…
      • ToTok co-founder pleads with Apple and Google to reinstate its app — www.imore.com/…

Notable Numbers

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 77 (January 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak

The show starts with a few followup stories, one notable number, a few legal stories, one acquisitions, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content. The four main stories are round 2 of the Apple -v- US DOJ back-door battle, iCloud encryption, Apple's Q1 2020 earnings, and two trade wars & a virus. The show ends with a quick rundown of some smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in January.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP77-January2020.mp3"]

Followup

  • Apple begins to sell Sonos as the speaker company accuses Google and Amazon of patent theft — www.imore.com/…
  • Rejoice! Apple Card customers can now export monthly transactions — www.imore.com/…
  • Adobe’s Creative Cloud now supports ‘Sign In with Apple’ — www.imore.com/…
  • iOS 13.3.1 has been released and contains the promised toggle to disable all location tracking, even for control of the U1 chip — arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple News launches ‘special coverage’ of the 2020 presidential election — www.imore.com/…
  • The Apple TV app is now available on 2019 LG Smart TVs — www.imore.com/…

Notable Numbers

  • 🇺🇸 Smartwatches and fitness trackers are now worn by 1 in every 5 Americans — www.imore.com/…

Legal Latest

  • 🇺🇸 Apple -v- Gerard Williams (Nuvia founder): Willians failed to have Apple’s suit dismissed in the Santa Clara County Superior Court — www.imore.com/…
    • Williams claimed Apple’s action against him was illegal because of CA’s ban on non-complete clauses. The judge disagreed:

      “[the law doesn’t permit an employee] to plan and prepare to create a competitive enterprise prior to termination if the employee does so on their employer’s time and with the employer’s resources.”

    • Williams also claimed Apple invaded his privacy by reading SMS messages on his Phone sent on his work phone. Since the phone in question was owned by Apple, the judge also disagree with this.
    • Apple’s lawsuit against former chip lead could have implications for startups — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple lawsuit tests if an employee can plan rival startup while on payroll — www.reuters.com/…
  • 🇺🇸 Apple -v- WiLan: On re-trial, the damages Apple must pay WiLan have been reduced from $145M to $85M — www.imore.com/…
  • 🇺🇸 CalTech -v- Apple & Broadcom: Apple and Broadcom ordered to pay over $1 billion for patent infringement — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: Apple and Broadcom chip deals now worth a casual $15 billion — www.imore.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • Apple Acquires AI Company Xnor.ai for Image Recognition Tools — www.macobserver.com/…

  2. 🇺🇸 Did Apple Kill End-to-End iCloud Encryption at the FBI’s Request?

  3. Apple’s 2020 Q1 Earnings Call (new record for Q1) — www.apple.com/…
    • Apple Reports Record Q1 Revenue of \$91.8 Billion and Record Q1 EPS of \$4.99 — www.macobserver.com/…

    • Apple’s wearables revenue overtakes Mac for the first time ever — www.imore.com/…
    • iPhone 11 was the best seller each and every week of the holiday quarter — www.imore.com/…
    • 📊 Analysis: Jason Snell’s superb charts: Apple reports a record $91.8 billion holiday quarter — sixcolors.com/…
    • Opinion:
      • Regular panelist Lynda Gousha’s Analysis:
        1. Quarter was fantastic - the only two minor quibbles were that the Services revenues weren’t higher - in terms of % growth, and growth in Japan was down, due to some ’regulatory changes’.
        2. Forecast was good
        3. Stock has been performing exceptionally well - up until the corona virus hit.
        4. Corona virus could be a really big deal, maybe more from governments' (both US & China) responses than from the virus itself. (I’m gleaning my thoughts from listening to Doctors & economists’ comments on Bloomberg Surveillance podcast). Dangers to Apple include people not going out to stores due to not going out, &, more serious - in some ways - supply chain issues. Apple does almost always have suppliers in more than one location in order not to be damaged too badly by issues like this, but given that so much assembly is done in China….. Hard to tell. Longer term - say 2 years, this won’t be a big deal, but in the interim, it will be.
        5. Apple itself, a long with some long term institutional investors, are likely to take this as an opportunity to buy the stock.
        6. A friend is putting together a spreadsheet showing number of shares outstanding over the years. Since Apple’s buyback program began, it looks like about 1/3 of the shares outstanding at that time have been repurchased. This, of course, impacts the EPS number of which financial types are so fond. Hard to tell if they take note of that, though the financial analysts we speak of so often, & on whom Ken reports so much damn well should be taking note of it. Of course the top line number, revenue, is not impacted.
        7. On the conference call itself, there were lots of new analysts, and some ‘old familiar’ ones missing. Most amusing of the articles I had a chance to look at, was this one, by Jason Snell. I agree w/his take, FWIW.
      • Things Apple Didn’t Want to Talk About in its Q1 Earnings Report — www.macobserver.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 78 (February 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Nick Riley from the Essential Apple Podcast - @spligosh
  • Lynda Gousha from the Silicon Valley MUG - @llg4cdg

The show starts with a few followup stories, two notable numbers, a few legal stories, a few Apple staffing changes, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content. The four main stories are the Corona virus, a kerfuffle setoff by some creating maths from AV vendor Malware Bytes, some over-hyped reporting on AFib detection with Apple Watch, and a collection of stories around HomeKit. The show ends with a quick rundown of some smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in February.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP78-February2020.mp3"]

Followup

  • The push to break encryption continues:

  • 🇺🇸 The US government’s scrutiny of Apple and the other major tech companies continues: The FTC is looking into the acquisitions made by Apple, Google, and more — www.imore.com/… & Feds launch a probe into Big Tech’s smallest acquisitions — arstechnica.com/…
  • Apple Card transactions can now be exported in OFX — www.imore.com/…
  • Fitbit rolls out blood oxygen monitoring to more users — www.imore.com/…

  • Google has paid Android developers about half of what Apple has — www.theverge.com/…
  • Apple Watch reportedly sold more units than every Swiss watchmaker combined — www.imore.com/…

  • Apple forced to pay its CA Apple Store employees overtime for the compulsory bag searches the company has been imposing — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple loses its attempt to force a VirnetX patent rehearing — www.imore.com/… & Apple will have to pay VirnetX $440 million after a decision not to hear its appeal — www.imore.com/…
  • Gerard Williams, the former Apple exec who is being sued by Apple for starting a rival chip company on Apple’s time and with Apple’s resources as well as for poaching Apple employees is now suing Apple for poaching his employees — www.imore.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Corona Virus Chaos

    • Foxconn has turned to the ‘SARS hero’ in its ongoing battle with coronavirus — www.imore.com/…
  2. AV vendor Malware Bytes made waves with an evocatively titled report claiming there are more malware threats against the Mac than against Windows PCs:
    • Malwarebytes: Malware threats per endpoint on Mac double that of Windows — www.imore.com/…
    • Research: Macs Saw Almost Twice as Much Malware as Windows PCs in 2019 — www.tomshardware.com/…
    • Malware threats on Macs outpace Windows for first time ever — www.loopinsight.com/…
    • Related Opinion: The State of Scamware on the Mac — daringfireball.net/…
  3. New reporting on Apple Watch made for a very dramatic headline, but it’s a stretch. A 2019 study has found that 84% of Apple Watch’s AFib detections prove to be accurate. Paperwork submitted by Apple to the US FDA states that the watch does not reliably detect AFib when pulse rates are abnormally low or high (<50pbm & >120BPM). A 2015 paper studying people who recently developed AFib found that their average pulse was 109, and one third of them had a pulse over 120, putting them outside the Apple Watch’s reliable detection window.
    • Apple Watch may miss AFib in as many as 59% of cases despite the fancy sensors — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: Should consumers be wary of Apple’s heartbeat monitoring app? — www.loopinsight.com/…

  • Throttle-gate cases continue to be resolved in courts around the world:

Notable Numbers

  • Android flagship phones depreciate nearly twice as fast as iPhones — www.imore.com/…

Legal Latest

  • 🇫🇷 Apple is fined €1.1Bn for anti-trust violations in France. The French competition state that Apple entered into agreements with their two biggest French wholesalers that they would not compete with each other, and would not under-cut Apple’s own prices. The two whole salers Tech Data and Ingram Micro were also fined, but much less than Apple, just €76M & €63M respectively — www.imore.com/…, arstechnica.com/… & venturebeat.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

Main Stories

  1. Forced Uyghur Labour
    • A report from the Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI) has found evidence that a number of Chinese companies in Apple’s supply chain are or have used forced labour from Uyghur Muslims:

  2. New and Updated Hardware
    • New 13" Retina Macbook Airs:
      • New Magic Keyboard, base storage increased to 256GB, better performance, and a starting price of $999 ($899 for students)
      • Apple announces new MacBook Air with new Magic Keyboard — www.imore.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 80 (April 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Chuck Joiner from MacVoices - @chuckjoiner
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak
  • Nick Riley from the Essential Apple Podcast - @spligosh

The show starts with a few followup stories (including the virus-shaped elephant in every room these days), two quick legal story, a few Apple staffing changes and acquisitions, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content. The four main stories are Apple & Google's COVID API, Apple's Q2 2020 Earnings, the Magic Keyboard for iPad, and the new iPhone SE. The show ends with a quick rundown of some smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in April.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP80-April2020.mp3"]

Followup

  • COVID–19 Developments:
    • Note: we’ll discus Apple & Google’s Contact Tracing/Exposure Notification API in the main stories
    • 🇺🇸 Apple Stores and offices in the US will not reopen until May amid coronavirus pandemic — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple will battle COVID–19 by designing and making millions of medical face shields — arstechnica.com/… & Apple shares face shield design and assembly instructions on support site — www.imore.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Apple’s COVID–19 app updated with state-specific info and self care tips — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Tweaks Maps to Prominently Feature Hospitals, Food Delivery, More — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple announces $50 million Royalty Advance Fund for independent labels — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple adds 3% Daily Cash to physical Apple Card at Walgreens drive-thru — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple donates $10 million to ‘One World: Together at Home’ benefit event — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple is now redirecting (PRODUCT)RED purchases to COVID‑19 relief fund — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple is hiring 1,000 interns this summer despite the coronavirus pandemic — www.imore.com/…
    • Foxconn enforcing strict measures to keep iPhone manufacturing on track — www.imore.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Apple Partners With Stanford to Create Another COVID–19 App — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple is making some Apple TV+ series available for free for a limited time — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple creates iPad-based at-home learning program for kids enduring COVID–19 lockdowns — appleinsider.com/…
    • Apple Launches ‘Today at Home’ Segments With Creative Pros — www.macobserver.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Apple, Verizon, T-Mobile CEOs all named to U.S. economic revival groups — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple will reopen its Seoul store on Saturday (18 April), the first outside of China — www.imore.com/…
    • Tim Cook remains optimistic about Apple’s future in company-wide meeting — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple partners with Rogers to bring 21,000 iPads to students in Ontario — www.imore.com/…

    • 🇺🇸 Apple hosed an entirely on-line live session to teach developers about accessibility, it was probably a trial run for online-only WWDC — Apple holding live developer accessibility session on April 23 — www.imore.com/… & Apple’s online accessibility event might have given us clues to how WWDC will go down — www.imore.com/…
    • ‘Big Night In’: Tim Cook Announces Apple Support For BBC Coronavirus Fundraising Efforts — www.macobserver.com/…

    • Tim Cook delivers virtual commencement address to Ohio State University — www.imore.com/…
      • 🎦 Watch the video (it’s really good IMO) — www.youtube.com/…
  • More on last month’s new iPad Pros & iPad OS Update:

Legal Latest

  • Apple lawyer fired for insider trading says charges are unconstitutional — www.imore.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • Apple Acquires Irish AI Startup ‘Voysis’ — www.macobserver.com/…

Apple Original Content Update

  • British comedy ‘Trying’ arrives on Apple TV+ — www.imore.com/…
  • ‘Desperate Housewives’ producer Annie Weisman signs two-year Apple TV+ deal — www.imore.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Apple & Google join forces to develop a privacy-preserving iOS & Android API public health agencies can use to create apps to help track COVID–19 and warn people they may have been exposed — tidbits.com/…, arstechnica.com/…
    • This API will be used by many different apps in many different jurisdictions. The exact operation of the apps will vary, and it will be up to each public health authority to decide how they will deal with the verification of positive tests before publishing the relevant anonymous keys to warn people — www.imore.com/…
    • The API is being developed quickly, and has already been made available to select developers in the most recent beta version of iOS — www.imore.com/…
    • It’s now up to individual countries to decide what they want to do:
      • 🇺🇸 The CDC’s guidance on contact tracing apps align with Apple and Google — www.imore.com/…
        • Related: U.S. Senators propose COVID–19 data privacy bill — www.imore.com/…
      • 🇩🇪 Germany reverses course, supports Apple/Google’s contact tracing approach — www.imore.com/…
      • 🇫🇷 France is not going Apple’s way and wants Apple to give it exceptions to iOS security, which Apple does not appear to be doing — France claims Apple’s privacy policy is blocking its contact tracing app — www.imore.com/…
      • 🇬🇧 The UK has rejected Apple and Google’s contact tracing program — www.imore.com/… & The NHS says despite not following Apple and Google, its contact tracing app will work — www.imore.com/…
      • 🇨🇦 Contact tracing stirs debate in Canada — www.imore.com/…
      • 🇮🇪 Irish government confirms it will use de-centralized contact tracing model — www.imore.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Apple sends letter to senators in response to privacy concerns about its coronavirus app — www.imore.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Related: Regarding the Washington Post’s Poll on Americans’ Willingness to Use Smartphone Apps for Exposure Notification — daringfireball.net/…
    • Related: Cellebrite Pitches its iPhone Hacking Tools as COVID–19 Surveillance Solution — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Good Explainers:
      • Contact tracing: A guide to one possible pandemic solution — www.imore.com/…
      • 🎧 RESET: Contact Tracing, Explained — overcast.fm/…
  2. Apple’s Q2 2020 Earnings Call — www.apple.com/…

    • Lynda Gousha’s thoughts:

      Here’s a couple of things I thought interesting: 1. One of the analysts commented on Apple’s contributions to the effort Apple has put in to fighting COVID 19. That’s unusual, in my experience, they usually limit themselves to financial commentary, and/or questions. 2. As you know, the market hates uncertainty, and all we have these days is uncertainty, with Apple being no different in that respect to any other company. Economists, and other financial types will make guesses, but most folks admit they really don’t know how long it’s going to take to recover from this situation from a health perspective, let alone economically. 3. That said, Apple, because of its cash position, and perhaps because of the services business (and maybe wearables - due to health aspects of watch), is in a lot better shape than most other companies. Barring something totally extreme & unpredicted Apple will weather this storm just fine, and the stock is likely to do better than most others. 4. FWIW, analysts did not expect Apple to do stock buybacks in this environment - perhaps because it can be politically frowned on these days, and also because holding onto cash might be especially prudent now. The fact that Apple did announce stock buybacks, though, is interpreted as management’s and the BOD’s confidence in the company’s ability to come thru the current situation just fine. Also, FWIW, years ago I remember Steve saying, in other very difficult circumstances, something to the effect of, “We will continue to invest through these difficulties”, meaning, continue to develop excellent research & development, and produce excellent products. (I don’t remember if that was the dot com bust in 2001 or so, or the 2008 fiasco.) But, what’s important is that that part of the company culture has not changed. Investors can expect the same excellent performance from the stock.

      I don’t have much to say about the numbers - they were better than expected, but the market will & has moved onto the future. The fact that Apple did not provide guidance’ for the next quarter is a negative, but hardly unusual in these circumstances. The market almost always prices stocks on what they expect to be the case 6 months to a year in the future, so the results for this past quarter are not considered important. And, of course, nothing is certain right now.

    • Apple Q2 2020 results: $58B revenue, but no guidance — sixcolors.com/…

  3. Apple’s Magic Keyboard for iPad ships — www.imore.com/…

  4. Apple have Launched an all new iPhone SE with the brains of an iPhone 11 in the body of an iPhone 8 — www.imore.com/… & www.macobserver.com/…

    • The new iPhone SE has 3GB of RAM and an 1821 mAH battery — www.imore.com/…
    • The cheapest iPhone has a more powerful processor than the most expensive Android phone — www.loopinsight.com/…

      • 🎦 Marques Brownlee Reviews the New iPhone SE — daringfireball.net/…

Quick Stories

  • New HomeKit accessories and bike mount kit land on Apple Store website — www.imore.com/…

The show starts with a few followup stories (including the virus-shaped elephant in every room these days), one notable number, a few quick legal stories, a few Apple staffing changes and acquisitions, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content.       • It has been reported that the phones were unlocked used brute-force passcode guessing hardware.
      • The head of the FBI & the Attorney General used the news as an opportunity to attack Apple for not cooperating with the government, not unlocking the phones, and for making them secure in the first place (though they seem to have gone out of their way never to say ‘secure’ and to instead imply encryption is only about privacy).

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 82 (June 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Charles Edge from the Mac Admins Podcast - @cedge318
  • Scott Willsey from the BubbleSort Podcast - @scottaw

The show starts with a few followup stories (including the virus-shaped elephant in every room these days), one notable number, a few Apple staffing changes and acquisitions, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content. The four main stories are a turbulent month for the App Store, looming anti-trust on both sides of the pond, the Mac's move to Apple Silicon, and this year's OS updates. The show ends with a quick rundown of some smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in June.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP82-June2020.mp3"]

Followup

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 83 (July 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Lynda Gousha from the Silicon Valley MUG - @llg4cdg
  • Gazmaz from the My Mac Podcast - @gazmaz

The show starts with a few followup stories (including the virus-shaped elephant in every room these days), one acquisition, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content. The five main stories are Apple's Q3 earnings, Apple's plan to be carbon neutral by 2030, the ECJ tax judgement in favour of Apple and Ireland, antitrust pressure on Apple, and Apple TV+ at the Emmys. The show ends with a quick rundown of some smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in July.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

Main Stories

  1. Apple’s Q3 2020 Earnings — www.apple.com/…

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 84 (August 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Adam Christianson from The Mac Cast - @maccast
  • Simon Parnell from the Essential Apple Podcast - @serenak

The show starts with a few followup stories (including the virus-shaped elephant in every room these days), a few legal stories, some acquisitions, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content. The four main stories are Phill Schiller's transition to Apple Fellow, update iMacs, Microsoft's Surface Duo, and Apple's App Store problems (there's much more going on than just the Epic saga!). The show ends with a quick rundown of some smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in August.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="http://www.mymac.com/podcast/lta/LetsTalkApple-EP84-August2020.mp3"]

Followup

  • COVID Updates:
    • ExposureNotification/Contact Tracing Apps Continue to Roll Out:
      • Apple & Google have announced the next phase of their API — OS-level support that does not require an app. They’ve named this new option for governments Exposure Notifications Express. OS-level support is coming to Android later in September, but it’s already available on iOS with the release of iOS 13.7 — www.macobserver.com/… & tidbits.com/…
      • 🇺🇸 US States finally start rolling out apps. Apps are out or on the way for the following states: Virginia, North Dakota, Wyoming, Alabama & Pennsylvania — www.imore.com/…, www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
      • 🇬🇧 Coronavirus: England’s contact-tracing app gets green light for trial — www.bbc.com/…
      • 🇦🇺 Australia’s Covidsafe app only working 27% of the time on some iPhones — www.imore.com/…
    • Stores Continue to Open & Close Around the World:
      • 🇨🇳 Today at Apple Sessions Restart in Mainland China — www.macobserver.com/…
      • 🇺🇸 Apple Sainte-Catherine closes abruptly, prompting speculation about employee COVID–19 case — www.imore.com/…
      • 🇪🇸 Apple stores reclosing in Madrid following COVID–19 surge — www.imore.com/…
      • 🇺🇸 Some U.S. Apple stores that were closed due to COVID–19 will now reopen — www.imore.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Apple Card payment deferment extends up to six months — www.imore.com/…
  • As promised when Apple bought them, Dark Sky has killed it’s Android app — arstechnica.com/…
  • 🇮🇳 New iPhone SE handsets sold in India are now made there as well — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple’s announced stock split has happened, and it drove the stock up to new record levels: Apple Worth $2.2 Trillion as Stock Hits Record High Following Stock Split — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple’s value passes entire FTSE 100 — www.imore.com/…
    • Even after a bad day (along with the entire tech sector) on 3 Sep the stock still closed with a market cap above the $2T threshold (last month Apple became the first publicly traded company to cross a market cap of $2T) — 9to5mac.com/… & www.cnbc.com/…
  • 🇺🇸 🇨🇳 A new front has opened in the US-China trade war — Social Media, and it could very negatively affect Apple’s iPhone sales in China:
    • Trump signs executive orders banning transactions with Chinese owners of TikTok, WeChat — www.imore.com/…
    • Trump administration faces lawsuit over WeChat ban — www.imore.com/…
    • Trump administration seeks dismissal of lawsuit against executive order regulating social media — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple, Ford, and Walmart lobbying against WeChat ban — www.imore.com/…
    • 95% of China iPhone users would leave Apple if WeChat was banned — www.imore.com/…
    • Chinese Foreign Ministry: No reason to keep iPhones if WeChat is banned — www.imore.com/…
    • Trump on concerns WeChat ban could hurt iPhone sales: ‘Whatever’ — www.imore.com/…
    • The Trump administration is rethinking its ban of WeChat — www.imore.com/…
    • Related Analysis: WeChat is one of the only ways to communicate with family and loved ones who live in China — now there’s plans on taking that away — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: A WeChat ban could be fatal for Apple and the iPhone in China — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: Kuo: iPhone’s loss of WeChat could cause a worldwide shipment fall of 30% — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: WeChat threat is Cook’s greatest Trump challenge yet — 9to5mac.com/…

Legal Latest

  • 🇺🇸 Judge tells Apple it took too long to try to recoup the $454 million it paid VirnetX over patents — www.imore.com/…
  • 🇺🇸 Apple settles Powerbeats 2 lawsuit for nearly $10M over defect — www.imore.com/…
  • 🇺🇸 Apple Must Pay $506 million over use of PanOptis LTE patents — www.imore.com/…
  • 🇺🇸 Apple Store employees have won their appeal against a lower court’s ruling that Apple did not owe them for time spent having their bags searched before leaving work. Presumably that means Apple owes a lot of back-pay, but that’s not explicitly stated in the article — appleinsider.com/…

Apple Acquisitions

  • Apple reportedly picked up Israeli AR and camera firm Camerai on the quiet — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple has reportedly acquired virtual reality startup company Spaces — www.imore.com/…

Apple Original Content Update

  • Apple renames Beats 1, adds two more radio stations to Apple Music — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple TV+ Deals:
    • Apple inks first-look deal with Leonardo DiCaprio’s production company — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple TV+ lands new drama from Robert Downey Jr.’s production company — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple signs first-look TV+ deal with Martin Scorsese — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple TV+ picks up a new animated ‘Harriet the Spy’ TV show — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Wins Bid for Spy Romance Film With Idris Elba, Simon Kinberg — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Apple Orders ‘My Kind of Country’ Competition Series — www.macobserver.com/…
    • New Apple documentary charts artists’ AR collaboration with Apple stores — www.imore.com/…
    • Keira Knightley to Star in ‘The Essex Serpent’ for Apple TV+ — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Three Nature Documentaries Coming to Apple TV+ Fall 2020 — www.macobserver.com/…
    • “Mariah Carey’s Magical Christmas Special” to premiere on Apple TV+ — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple TV+ picks up ‘Five Days At Memorial,’ a show about Hurricane Katrina — www.imore.com/…
  • Apple TV+ Releases:
    • ‘Ted Lasso’ and ‘Boys State’ arrive on Apple TV+ — www.imore.com/…
      • Related: Ted Lasso Renewed for Season Two on Apple TV+ — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Related: ‘Boys State – Then & Now’ asks how the Apple TV+ documentary’s stars feel they’ve changed since it was filmed — www.imore.com/…
    • Official Trailer for Apple TV+ Series ‘Tehran’ Arrives, Show Available September 25 — www.macobserver.com/…
    • ‘On The Rocks’ will hit theaters before premiering on Apple TV+ — www.imore.com/…
  • Productions starting to resume after COVID halt:
    • Production resumes on season two of Apple’s space drama ‘For All Mankind’ — www.imore.com/…
    • Apple Original Series ‘Invasion’ Resumes Filming After Pause — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Related:
    • American Airlines adds free inflight Apple TV+ streaming — thepointsguy.com/…
    • The Apple TV app is rolling out to some LG TVs from 2018 — www.imore.com/…
      • Customers furious after LG U-turns on AirPlay 2 and HomeKit support for pre–2019 TVs — www.imore.com/…
    • 🇺🇸 Apple Offers CBS All Access and Showtime Bundle for Apple TV+ Subscribers — tidbits.com/…
    • 🇬🇧 EE Offers iPhone Users Apple Music, TV+, Arcade ‘Full Works’ Bundle — www.macobserver.com/…
    • 🇨🇦 Rogers offering six months free Apple Music with select Infinite plans — www.imore.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Phil Schiller is transitioning to Apple Fellow from SVP for Worldwide Marketing but retaining the lead on the App Store and Apple events. Greg Joswiak is replacing Phil as SVP for Worldwide Marketing:
    • As Phil Schiller Becomes Apple Fellow, Greg Joswiak Becomes VP — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Greg Joswiak is taking over Worldwide Marketing from Phil Schiller — www.imore.com/…
    • Related: An introduction to every Apple Fellow in company history — www.cultofmac.com/…
  2. Apple updated their iMac Line:
    • Apple’s iMac line just got overhauled, with the 27-inch getting the biggest changes — arstechnica.com/…
    • Apple announces new iMac with 10th gen Intel Processors, new webcam — www.imore.com/…
    • 27-inch iMac Receives Significant Update, Other iMacs Get a Nod — tidbits.com/…
    • Apple gives iMac Pro lineup a stealth update with a more speedy base model — www.imore.com/…
    • Storage in new Macs is soldered to the logic board. Except when it isn’t. — www.imore.com/…
    • What Apple’s Nano-Texture is, and what it brings to Apple’s new 27-inch iMac — appleinsider.com/…
    • This is how to (very carefully) clean that fancy new nano-texture iMac — www.imore.com/…
    • First 2020 iMac benchmarks hit the web showing a handy speed boost — www.imore.com/…
    • Third-Party RAM for 27-inch iMac Still Far More Affordable Than Apple’s Checkout Upgrade Options — www.macrumors.com/…
    • Analysis: iMac 5K 2020 vs. iMac 5K 2019: What’s the difference and should you upgrade? — www.imore.com/…
    • Opinion: One New iMac is Fabulous. The Other, Not so Much — www.macobserver.com/…
  3. Microsoft Announced the Surface Duo a different take on the foldable — two screens running Android:
    • Microsoft’s Surface Duo arrives on September 10th for $1,399 — www.theverge.com/…
    • Microsoft’s blog post announcing the device — blogs.windows.com/…
    • 🎦 The product announcement — youtu.be/…
  4. Apple’s App Store Problem
    • What Happened:
      • Microsoft announced that it’s eagerly awaited cloud gaming service xCloud will launch on Android on the 15th of September, but says nothing about iOS. The tech press fill in the blanks and call Apple out for their app store policies. Apple responded saying every game needs to be submitted for individual review. Microsoft then responded publicly, saying Apple’s stance is unworkable leaving ‘no path’ to xCloud on iOS — www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
      • Facebook launched Facebook gaming for iOS, but because if App Store rules, the app doesn’t actually allow users to play any games, merely to watch others play — www.imore.com/…
        • Related: Mark Zuckerberg fires major shots at Apple during company meeting — www.imore.com/…
      • Facebook complains that Apple won’t let it facilitate fee-less paid events (Facebook wants to give all the money to the event organisers) — www.imore.com/…
      • The Epic Saga Begins:
        • Epic released an update for Fortnight for iOS & Android that included code that reached back to their servers so they could change the app’s functionality after it had passed Apple & Google’s review process to add in their own payment method, breaching Apple & Google’s rules. Both companies responded by removing the game from their stores. Epic then filed a lawsuit it had prepared in advance, and released a bunch of ads it had ready and waiting — arstechnica.com/…, www.macobserver.com/…, www.theverge.com/…, www.macobserver.com/… & www.imore.com/…
        • Epic’s case was quickly re-assigned to judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers who’s already overseeing two smaller anti-trust case against Apple — www.imore.com/…
        • Apple invokes the clause in its developer agreement that allows it terminate the agreement in case of rule violation, warning Epic that it will revoke all its developer accounts, hence killing app its apps, and, removing access to Apple’s development tools from developers working on Epic’s Unreal Engine, a software library they sell to game developers — arstechnica.com/… & www.theverge.com/…
        • Epic files for a restraining order requesting the court both force Apple to put Fortnite back in the store as-is, and preventing Apple terminating its developer accounts. Apple files a response saying the emergency Epic is requesting relief from is entirely self-inflicted, and entirely within its own power to resolve — www.macobserver.com/… & techcrunch.com/…
        • Apple release emails showing Epic asked for a special deal — www.imore.com/…
        • Microsoft filed documents in the injunction case in support of protecting the Unreal Engine (but not in support of restoring Fortnite) — arstechnica.com/…
        • The judge in the restraining order case partially sides with Apple, and partially with Epic. Apple argued that Epic created the emergency around the removal of Fornight, and can resolve it without any assistance by simply submitted a version of the app that doesn’t break the rules. The judge agreed, and denied Epic’s request to force Apple to add Fortnight back to the store. However, the judge also found that since the Unreal Engine is produced by a subsidiary company, Apple should not block that company from continuing to develop the engine — www.imore.com/… & www.imore.com/…
        • Apple promoted PUBG, a Fortnite competitor that’s been around longer than Fortnite itself, in its app store editorial content — www.imore.com/…
          • Related: 🇮🇳 Apple & Google removed PUBG from their Indian app stores to comply with the Indian government’s ban on Chinese apps — www.imore.com/…
        • Apple terminated one of Epic’s developer accounts (the one it used to publish its games, not the one it used to develop the Unreal Engine) — www.imore.com/…
        • Epic released its big update, but not in iOS or the Mac, and it wrote a letter to customers blaming Apple — www.imore.com/…
      • While the Epic saga was unfolding Apple briefly blocked Wordpress from updating its app until it started to support in-app purchases for its subscriptions. This was a mistake, and Apple reversed its position and apologised to Wordpress — arstechnica.com/…
      • Also while the Epic saga was unfolding, Facebook let it be known that it was blocked by both Apple & Google from describing the 30% revenue cut the companies take in the description of one of their apps — www.reuters.com/… & www.imore.com/…
      • While all this was going on Apple’s app store continued to attract anti-trust attention around the world
        • 🇪🇺 The European Commission let it be known that it’s ‘aware’ of Microsoft & Facebook’s issues with Apple — www.imore.com/…
        • 🇷🇺 Russian watchdog rules Apple’s App Store is anticompetitive — www.imore.com/…
        • 🇺🇸 Congressman aims to end tech’s ‘deeply disturbing’ antitrust behaviour — www.imore.com/…
        • 🇰🇷 Korea confirms investigation into Apple and Google’s 30% cut — www.imore.com/…
        • 🇷🇺 Russian lawmaker introduces bill to cap Apple’s App Store fees at 20% — www.imore.com/…
        • 🇩🇪 Germany considering App Store inquiry, watching Epic Games case ‘very closely’ — www.imore.com/…
        • 🇯🇵 As Japanese developers complain about their problems with the app store, Japanese regulators are also taking an interest — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple implemented the improvements to the app review process it promised at WWDC, allowing developers to challenge the guidelines as well as Apple’s decisions — arstechnica.com/… & www.imore.com/…
      • Apple released a statement claiming the iOS app economy has created 300,000 jobs since 2019 — www.imore.com/…
      • News Publishers Ask Apple for Better App Store Terms — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple announced a new feature to allow developers to create subscription offer codes for their apps — www.imore.com/…

Joining Bart this month are Charlotte Henry & Kelly Guimont from the Mac Observer, and Nick Riley from the Essential Apple Podcast.

The show starts with a few followup stories (including the virus-shaped elephant in every room these days), some hires and acquisitions, and a quick overview of news related to Apple's original content. item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 86 (October 2020)

Panel:

  • Mikah Sargent from the Clockwise Podcast and TWiT Network - @mikahsargent

The show starts with a few followup stories, updates on some Apple-related legal cases, one acquisition, and a quick(ish) overview of news related to Apple's original content. The three main stories are Apple's Q4 2020 earnings call, the on-going anti-trust kerfuffle, and Apple's 'Hi, Speed' event. The show ends with a quick rundown of some smaller Apple-related stories that made the news in October.

item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 87 (November 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:

The show starts with a few followup stories, updates on some Apple-related legal cases, some Apple HR news, and a quick(ish) overview of news related to Apple's content offerings. The three main stories are more App Store Developments, the release of macOS Big Sur, and Apple's new M1 Macs. item.title: Let's Talk Apple — Ep. 88 (December 2020)
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bbusschots
  • Ken Ray from Mac OS Ken - @macosken

The show starts with a the usual followups and updates on long-running stories, including a deeper than normal dive into the regulation question. That's followed by a few quick updates on some Apple-related legal cases, some Apple HR news, and an overview of developments in Apple's various service offerings. The four main stories are Facebook's anti-anti-tracking crusade, Apple's new AirPods Max, the launch of Fitness+, and the arrival of ProRAW.
