item.title: LTA 144: August 2025
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bartb.ie

August is the so-called 'silly season', and it shows, with just two main stories, but lots more detail than usual in the other regular segments. Starting as usual with feedback and followups the most notable developments are in the secret UK encryption case and the Apple-Epic saga, there are some more regulatory problems for Apple, just one legal story, then the usual HR news before checking in on Apple's services and original content where there is a very notable price change to discuss. The two main stories are Tim Cook's 'Made in America' charm offensive, and Apple's US blood oxygen workaround. As usual the show finish with a few smaller stories that made the month's news.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="https://media.lets-talk.ie/lta/lta144.mp3"]

Updates & Followup

Quick updates to long-running stories the show continues to track, and to stories covered in recent shows.

  • The UK's super-secret case against Apple got significantly more confusing in August:

    • Reminder: under the UK's so-called snooper's charter the government can secretly order technological changes and it is a crime for the recipients of the recipients of such orders to admit they received them. The only think we know for absolute certain is that Apple removed it's Advanced Data Protection feature from UK users because it as not longer able to offer it.
    • The last we had heard about the story was reporting from the FT in London that the UK government was trying to find a face-saving way to back out of the whole thing.
    • The first development in late August was a Tweet from the US Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard saying UK had dropped their attempt to get at the data of US residents, but there was no official confirmation from the UK government, or from Apple, and ADP remains unavailable in the UK — appleinsider.com/…
    • The media initially took this one short and vague Tweet as proof the whole things was over, but just a week later the FT returned with another bombshell of a story — they have seen Apple's submissions for a secret court hearing on the whole thing and it is set for early 2026. Not just that, but the British governments demands are reported to go far beyond just a back door in ADP — appleinsider.com/…
    • So, we end the month like we started it, none the wiser as to how all this will play out
    • Probably Related: FTC draws hard line on foreign-driven censorship & data demands for Big Tech — appleinsider.com/…

  • August was a relatively quiet month in the Apple -v- Epic saga:

    • An Australian court has ruled that Apple & Google's app stores are anti-competitive, but there are no details yet of what exactly that will mean — appleinsider.com/…

    • Nothing substantial happened in the US case, just some ground work preparing for what ever remaining court dates there will be:

      • Two industry groups have filed Amicus briefs in Apple's appeal of injunction forcing them to open up the US app store stating the judge went too far when when she ruled that simply putting a lawyer's name on a document did not automatically make is privileged (and citing this was a common tactic to attempt to avoid accountability) — appleinsider.com/…
      • The storied venture capital firm Y Combinator has also filed an Amicus brief, though this one defending Epic — appleinsider.com/…
      • The American Antitrust Institute think-tank has also filed an Amicus brief, also against Apple so in favour of Epic — appleinsider.com/…
      • Apple ended the month by filing a brief with the appeals court claiming the entire injunction is unconstitutional — appleinsider.com/…

  • August was a relatively quiet month in Trump Tariff news:

    • Appeals court shoots down 'reciprocal' tariffs, will still hit iPhone 17 launch — appleinsider.com/… (ruling does not come into force until 14 October to give time for an appeal to be filed)
    • Another TACO: Over 150% China tariff rate delayed by 90 days, 30% still in effect for iPhone season — appleinsider.com/…

  • Some more details have emerged about how Japan's new Mobile Software Competition Act (MSCA) will affect Apple, as well as the App Store changes discussed last month, they will also have to offer an EU-like browser ballot — www.cultofmac.com/…

  • August was a good month for Apple in India:

    • Present Trump doubled the tariffs on India (25% → 50%) as punishment for buying Russian oil, but Apple is exempt — www.macobserver.com/…
    • Five Apple factories in India will build iPhone 17 for the US — www.cultofmac.com/… (as per a Bloomberg report)
    • Apple's new store expands official support & sales to a third location in India — appleinsider.com/… (Apple Hebbal in Bengaluru)
    • Apple has broken its India annual sales record, and more growth is coming — appleinsider.com/… (Bloomberg reporting based on an unnamed person familiar with the figures)

Regulatory Rundown

  • When the UK passed it's Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act (DMCC) that trigged an investigation into Apple and Google by the country's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) to determine if those companies have Strategic Market Status, who have now found that Apple & Google do indeed have that status, bringing them under tighter regulations similar to Gatekeeper status under the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) — www.macobserver.com/…

    • Apple threatens UK with delayed features if EU DMA-like regulations introduced — appleinsider.com/…

  • Google Allowed to Keep Chrome and Continue Paying Apple $20 Billion for Search Placement — tidbits.com/…

    • My take: Technically there is a change since the ruling says Google can't demand their search engine be exclusive in their contracts with browsers, but they can keep paying to be the default and for every referral, so browsers are incentivised to make Google the default anyway to maximise revenue, so no real change, at least not unless and until another search engine offers better rates.

  • German Court Blocks Apple’s Carbon Neutral Claims for Apple Watch — www.macobserver.com/… (purely on a technicality regarding a specific off-set, not on any broad principle)

  • Apple App Store Faces Formal Antitrust Investigation in Colombia — www.macobserver.com/…

  • France's unnecessary iPhone 12 RF patch is spreading across Europe — appleinsider.com/…

Legal Latest

  • Elon Musk baselessly suing Apple for Grok's position on the App Store — appleinsider.com/…

    • The best description of the legal arguments being made — www.macobserver.com/…

    • Elon Musk's antitrust claims refuted by Apple citing curation for safe discovery — appleinsider.com/…

    • Opinion: Musk is wrong and has only influence on his side in a childish App Store spat — appleinsider.com/…

    • Opinion: Elon Musk sues Apple and OpenAI, revealing his panic over OpenAI dominance — arstechnica.com/…

      At this point appearing to be genuinely panicked about OpenAI's insurmountable lead in the chatbot market, Musk has specifically alleged that an agreement integrating ChatGPT into the iOS violated antitrust and unfair competition laws. Allegedly, the conspiracy is designed to protect Apple's smartphone monopoly and block out AI rivals to lock in OpenAI's dominance in the chatbot market.

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • AI remains the focus of Apple's HR news:

    • Apple starts hiring AI engineers for a new Answers, Knowledge and Information team — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple Loses Sixth AI Leader to Meta’s Superintelligence Push — www.macobserver.com/… (Frank Chu who oversaw AI infrastructure, training & search)

    • Four more employees depart Apple, join other AI efforts — appleinsider.com/…

      • Most notably: Apple’s Robotics Research Head Joins Meta’s Reality Labs — www.macobserver.com/… (Jian Zhang)

    • Related: Apple machine learning privacy workshop talks help promote AI security — appleinsider.com/…

    • Related: Xcode 26 beta 7 adds GPT-5 & Claude account support — appleinsider.com/…

  • Apple TV+ senior executive Chris Parnell poached by Paramount — appleinsider.com/… (was a senior creative executive working on original content)

  • Apple denies its Fitness chief is bullying his team as an employee sues — appleinsider.com/…

  • Apple Sues Ex-Employee for Stealing Apple Watch Secrets for Oppo — www.macobserver.com/…

Apple Services & Original Content Highlights

  • Apple TV+:

    • Apple have increased the monthly cost of a stand-alone AppleTV+ subscription by 30% ( $9.99 → $12.99), the first price-rise in two years — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • The change is not for everyone, but for "new customers in the U.S. and select international markets as of today" — tvline.com/…

      • Note that the annual price remains the same, as Gruber reports, this strongly encourages annual sign-ups over monthly ones — daringfireball.net/…

        The usual rule-of-thumb for subscriptions of any sort seems to be to charge 10× the monthly rate for an annual subscription. That’s exactly where the TV+ month/annual prices were before today. Now, the annual subscription price isn’t just a little bit cheaper than 12× the monthly price ($156), but a lot cheaper.

      • Also note Apple One has also not changed price, so is now an even better offering — www.cultofmac.com/…

    • 'F1: the Movie' is now available to rent or buy — appleinsider.com/… (next release will be streaming on Apple TV+)

    • 'Ted Lasso' now flies the friendly skies on United's in-flight entertainment system — appleinsider.com/… (along with Severance, Shrinking, Slow Horses & Silo)

    • Apple TV+ show 'Trying' will be free on the BBC soon — appleinsider.com/… (first Apple show to get syndicated this way, nice way to keep monetising the growing back-catalogue)

  • **Apple Music:

    • Apple Music migration tool will finally help U.S. Spotify users switch — appleinsider.com/… ( was only available in Australia & New Zealand)

      An Apple Support document update spotted by MacRumors says the migration tool is now available in the UK, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, and Mexico, as well as Australia, New Zealand, and the United States.

    • Apple partners with TuneIn to stream radio stations to 75 million users — www.cultofmac.com/…

  • Apple Arcade adds fun new content, including NFL Retro Bowl ’26, Jeopardy! Daily, and an exciting update to Hello Kitty Island Adventure — Apple PR

  • Apple Maps now helps cyclists navigate Hong Kong and Taiwan streets — appleinsider.com/…

  • Apple Wallet ID Support Expands to Montana — www.macobserver.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Apple really focused on it's made in American push in August:

    • Apple started the month with a big PR event in the White House announcing an additional $100Bn investment in US manufacturing — www.macstories.net/…

      • $500Bn → $600Bn over the next 4 years

      • Additional investments are into Apple's American Manufacturing Program which covers 10 US-based manufacturers (Amkor, Applied Materials, Broadcom, Coherent, Corning, GlobalFoundries, GlobalWafers America AKA GWA, Samsung, Texas Instruments AKA TI)

      • The first investment to be detailed is in Corning, which will now make the glass for US-bound iPhone and Apple Watch screens — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • During the event President Trump announced a plan to announce a 100% tariff on semiconductor imports, but said companies like Apple who invest in the US would be exempt — appleinsider.com/…

        • TSMC, Apple's biggest chip provider confirmed they understood themselves to be exempt — www.macobserver.com/…
        • By the end of the month it was still a threatened tariff not an actual one — appleinsider.com/…

      • Tim Cook expertly buttered up President Trump by presenting him with a huge gaudy gold and glass trophy (an engraved Corning Gorilla Glass disk set in a gold base made from 24K Utah gold) — appleinsider.com/…

      • The trophy, and the private conversations the whole spectacle enabled seem to have worked, at least for now, Tim Cook has succeeded in getting President Trump understand that iPhone final assembly can't just be moved to the US, and that it's better for Apple to source high-value components from US manufacturers instead — appleinsider.com/…

        "He makes many of the components here, and we've been talking about it, and the whole thing is set up at other places, and it's been there for a long time, so in terms of cost and all [on Apple's difficulties bringing final assembly to the United States]. But I think we may incentivize him enough that one day he'll be bringing that — but he brings most of the stuff — look, he's not making this kind of an investment anywhere else in the world, not even close." — Trump at the White House event where he was presented with his glass and gold trophy

      • Tip of the Hat for the best Headline: Trump wanted a US-made iPhone. Apple gave him a gold statue. — arstechnica.com/…

      • Opinion: Gold, Frankincense, and Silicon — daringfireball.net/… (I agree with Gruber's take)

        Faulting Cook for playing ball and kissing Trump’s ring (among other things) is like faulting a local business for paying into a protection racket — one in which the cops are complicit, and the whole scam exists at the behest of a crooked mayor. Moral rectitude can feel good, but not so much when the cops are burning your store to the ground. There is no authority to appeal to for help when the highest office in the country is running the protection racket. … US manufacturing, on the other hand, is a point of genuine alignment between Trump’s desires and Apple’s interests and ethics

    • Apple Partners with Samsung to Launch New US Based Chip Technology — www.macobserver.com/… (likely camera sensors, but no details announced)

    • Apple chips to be made at newly opened Texas Instruments plant — appleinsider.com/…

    • The good-will and buttering-up continued right to the end of the month with Tim Cook attending a White House dinner where both he and Trump spoke — appleinsider.com/…

      "I want to thank you for setting the tone such that we could make a major investment in the United States and have some key manufacturing advanced manufacturing here. … I think that says a lot about your focus and your leadership and your focus on innovation, I also want to thank you for helping American companies around the world. This is a very key, key thing. … We're all, we are all different in some ways, but we all believe in the power of technology to improve people's lives, and that is the thing that binds us all together." — Tim Cook

  2. Apple Watch getting blood oxygen sensor back after 18 month absence — appleinsider.com/… ( Apple PR)

    • Apple found a loop-hole! Masimo's patent covers devices that have the sensors, display, and processing on the device, so Apple is only using the sensor on US Apple watches now, and sending the raw readings to the paired iPhone for both processing and display (within the Health app) — daringfireball.net/…

    • Masimo responds by suing US Customs & Border Patrol (CBP) — www.macobserver.com/… & appleinsider.com/…

      TMO: The lawsuit, filed in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, claims CBP violated the Administrative Procedure Act and due process protections when it issued an internal advice ruling on August 1. According to Masimo, the agency overturned its own January decision without notifying the company or allowing it to respond. Apple Insider's description of Masimo's Argumment: The CBP crossed a line by effectively making a ruling in the patent dispute, instead of leaving it to the ITC, Massimo believes. Furthermore, the CBP didn't give Massimo an opportunity to participate in discussions.

      • An insightful analysis from John Gruber: daringfireball.net/…

        The CBP’s investigation centered around whether the Masimo patents were “limiting” — which seems to mean a device that does all these things: the sensors, the computation of results, and the display of results. Masimo argued that the patents weren’t limiting, and apparently made no argument for how the import ban on Apple Watches should stand if the patents were found by CBP to be limiting. The CBP asked the International Trade Commission — the outfit that instituted the import ban — whether they considered the Masimo patents to be limiting, and the ITC responded yes, they did, that that was the entire basis of the import ban.

    • CPB have filed a motion to dismiss the Masimo case against them — www.macobserver.com/…

      The government maintains that Masimo must first take its objections to the International Trade Commission. If the ITC rules against Masimo, the company can appeal to the Federal Circuit. Customs said Masimo cannot sidestep this process by filing directly in district court.

Quick Stories

  • Apple’s $2.5B Housing Plan Shows More Progress Than Meta, Google — www.macobserver.com/…

    Six years after the three companies announced large-scale commitments, Apple has spent more than $1.6 billion of its $2.5 billion plan, funding the creation or preservation of over 10,000 affordable housing units, offering financial help to at-risk residents, and supporting first-time homebuyers.

  • Apple brings its Self Service Repair program to Canada — appleinsider.com/… (now 34 countries & 25 languages)

  • Beats Solo 4 launches special Ruby Red JENNIE edition — appleinsider.com/…

  • Apple's September event will be held at 13:00 EST on the 9th of September and is titled Awe Dropping — arstechnica.com/…

    • How to find the Easter egg in the new Apple event logo — www.cultofmac.com/…

Legend

Note: When the textual description of a link is part of the link it is the title of the page being linked to, when the text describing a link is not part of the link it is a description written by Bart.

item.title: LTA 145: September 2025
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bartb.ie

The show starts with a quick update on the UK iCloud saga, a handful of regulatory and legal stories, a little HR and acquisition news, and rundown of the notable Apple services and original content news before digging into the three main stories. The first main story is a short look at some Trump-related developments in the US before getting stuck into the the twin big stories, the new hardware from the 'Awe Dropping' event, this year's big new OS releases.The show finishes with the usual rundown of a few other quick Apple-related stories that made the news in September.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="https://media.lets-talk.ie/lta/lta145.mp3"]

 

Updates & Followup

Quick updates to long-running stories the show continues to track, and to stories covered in recent shows.

  • More reporting from the Financial Times confirms my fears that the UK super-secret iCloud backdoor drama is not over: cyberinsider.com/…

    “According to sources familiar with the matter, the latest Technical Capability Notice (TCN) issued under the Investigatory Powers Act (IPA) asks Apple to break encryption solely for UK citizens’ data stored in iCloud.”

Regulatory Rundown

  • EU investigates Apple, Google, and Microsoft over handling of online scams — arstechnica.com/… (Are these companies meeting their Digital Services Act obligations to add effective protections?)

  • Apple has filed an official response to the European Commission's request for feedback on the Digital Markets Act — Apple PR

    "Under the DMA, the European Commission’s interpretation of the rules is constantly changing. And that makes it nearly impossible for companies to know how to comply.” … “The DMA’s rules only apply to Apple, even though Samsung is the smartphone market leader in Europe, and Chinese companies are growing fast … the DMA singles Apple out while leaving our competitors free to continue as they always have.” … “Over time, it’s become clear that the DMA isn’t helping markets. It’s making it harder to do business in Europe.” … “it’s become clear that the DMA is leading to a worse experience for Apple users in the EU. It’s exposing them to new risks, and disrupting the simple, seamless way their Apple products work together. And as new technologies come out, our European users’ Apple products will only fall further behind.” — Apple

    • Apple says more features would be delayed in EU under DMA — www.macobserver.com/…

    • EU Digital Markets Act benefits only other big tech companies and hurts customers, says Apple — appleinsider.com/…

    • EU Says Apple Must Comply with DMA Rules — www.macobserver.com/…

    • Opinion:

      • Dan Moran: Apple posts thoughts on the DMA — sixcolors.com/… (excellent article, can't disagree)

      • John Gruber: Apple on the Digital Markets Act — daringfireball.net/…

        "If Apple just shipped all EU iPhones with Android instead of iOS, all of their DMA problems would go away … How in the world would that increase competition?"

Legal Latest

  • Apple & Amazon iPhone & Mac price fixing lawsuit dismissed — appleinsider.com/…
  • Apple Says Musk’s xAI Case Built on “Speculation” — www.macobserver.com/… & OpenAI mocks Musk’s math in suit over iPhone/ChatGPT integration — arstechnica.com/…

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • Irish chip firm IC Mask Design acquired by Apple — appleinsider.com/… (Only made public thanks to DMA transparency requirements!)
  • Former Siri Head Robby Walker to Exit Apple After AI Setbacks — www.macobserver.com/…
  • Apple Faces Federal Lawsuit for Alleged Religious Discrimination — www.macobserver.com/… (long-time Apple Genius converted to Judaism, did not get appropriate accommodations, and was fired)
  • NLRB withdraws claims about Tim Cook's email violating workers' rights — appleinsider.com/… (National Labour Relations Board)

Apple Services & Original Content Highlights

  • Apple TV+:

    • Another good year for Apple at the Emmys:

      • Apple TV+’s Severance and The Studio nab record 15 Creative Arts Emmy Awards — www.cultofmac.com/…
      • 'Severance' and 'The Studio' earn Apple TV+ a record-breaking 22 Emmys — appleinsider.com/…
      • Apple’s Outstanding Comedy The Studio sweeps as the most-winning freshman comedy in Emmy history, and global hit Severance leads as most-winning drama at the 77th Primetime Emmy Awards — Apple PR

    • Apple TV+ secures 10-episode follow-up to BBC's 'Gavin and Stacey' — appleinsider.com/…

    • Seven new Apple Immersive films let Apple Vision Pro users explore sports, music, and culture — appleinsider.com/…

      • Related: CANAL+ Releases Immersive Documentary MotoGP: Tour De Force — www.macstories.net/…

    • The Peanuts gang will have a home at Apple until 2030 — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • Related: How to watch "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" for free in 2025 — appleinsider.com/…

  • Apple Music:

    • Apple Music Expands Transfer Tool to Almost Every Country — www.macobserver.com/… ( All but China, Myanmar & Russia)
    • Apple Music for Android gains some iOS 26 upgrades — appleinsider.com/…

  • 'NBA 2K26 Arcade Edition' arrives on Apple Arcade this October — appleinsider.com/… ( Apple PR)

  • Apple News+ added The Washington at no extra cost — www.macobserver.com/… (Probably US-only, but not sure)

  • Apple Pay & Apple Wallet:

    • Apple Pay Adds Affirm and Klarna for In-Store Purchases — www.macobserver.com/… (in the US & UK)
    • Tap to Pay on iPhone comes to yet more European countries — appleinsider.com/… (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Monaco & Norway)
    • Apple Wallet’s Car Key is about to reach 13 more automakers — www.macobserver.com/… (Acura, Cadillac, Chery, Chevrolet, GMC, Hongqi, Lucid, Porsche, Rivian, Smart, Tata, Voyah & WEY)
    • [Digital driver’s license access grows, with North Dakota joining 10 other states — www.cultofmac.com/…](https://www.cultofmac.com/news/north-dakota-drivers-license

  • Apple Health: Apple Expands Sleep Apnea Notifications to South Korea — www.macobserver.com/…

  • Apple Sports app adds widgets and expands to 8 new countries — www.cultofmac.com/… (All in Europe)

    • Apple Sports is now available in Ireland — Apple PR

  • Apple Invites adds calendar syncing and video playback — appleinsider.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Trumplandia Update

    • It's not clear how badly Trump's 100% tariffs on films will hit Apple TV+ — appleinsider.com/… (it's not even clear what is going to actually happen!)

    • Apple removes ICEBlock, won’t allow apps that report locations of ICE agents — arstechnica.com/… (Apple's US app store is now like their app stores in other authoritarian countries)

      • Opinion:

        • Complying With ‘Demand’ From Trump Administration, Apple Removes ICEBlock From App Store — daringfireball.net/…

          "No one, not even Bondi, is claiming any aspect of ICEBlock is illegal. Thus it’s not merely inappropriate but outrageous — and yet another among dozens of other causes for alarm regarding Trump 2.0’s decidedly authoritarian turn — for the DOJ to 'demand' Apple do anything about it. But demand they did, and comply did Apple." — John Gruber

        • Apple’s ICEblock capitulation is business as usual — sixcolors.com/…

          “Do not expect corporations to be your proxy in the fight against authoritarianism. They are, simply put, not designed for it. They are machines designed to return profit to shareholders and that means they fundamentally rely on a stability that you’re not going to get from making waves. You will always be disappointed.” — Dan Moren

    • Related: Apple CEO Tim Cook attended UK state dinner with President Trump — appleinsider.com/…

  2. Apple's Awe Dropping event

    • Apple’s September 2025 Event: Replay Today’s Keynote — www.macstories.net/…

      • 2-Minute Apple September Event 2025 Recap: All the Big Announcements — www.macobserver.com/…

    • Apple's September 2025 Event: All the Small Things (Bento Box Version) — www.macstories.net/…

    • What Apple Chose to Highlight — their press releases, in order:

      • Introducing AirPods Pro 3, the ultimate audio experience — Apple PR
      • Apple debuts Apple Watch Series 11, featuring groundbreaking health insights — Apple PR
      • Apple unveils iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max, the most powerful and advanced Pro models ever — Apple PR
      • Apple debuts iPhone 17 — Apple PR
      • Introducing iPhone Air, a powerful new iPhone with a breakthrough design — Apple PR
      • Apple announces Final Cut Camera 2.0 — Apple PR
      • Apple introduces Apple Watch SE 3 — Apple PR
      • Introducing Apple Watch Ultra 3 — Apple PR
      • Later in the Month: The next generation of iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods Pro arrives in Apple Store locations worldwide — Apple PR

    • Apple's September 2025 Event: By the Numbers — www.macstories.net/…

    • New AirPods Pro 3:

      • AirPods Pro 3 arrive with heart rate sensing, and best-ever ANC — appleinsider.com/…

      • AirPods Pro 3 Can Run 8-10 Hours on a Single Charge — www.macobserver.com/…

      • Hands on: AirPods Pro 3 Live Translation and heart rate monitoring are compelling — appleinsider.com/…

        • Live Translation will also work with AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 — appleinsider.com/…
        • Apple blocks Live Translation in the EU over DMA concerns — www.macobserver.com/…

      • Apple drops USB-C cable from AirPods Pro 3 packaging — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • AirPods Pro 3 review roundup: A ‘no-brainer upgrade’ — www.cultofmac.com/…

    • New Apple Watches:

      • Most new Apple Watches get Hypertension Alerts (not SE 3)

        • Apple expects to notify 1 million people that they have hypertension in a year — appleinsider.com/…
        • Some older Apple Watch models will get hypertension notifications — appleinsider.com/… (Series 9, Series 10 & Ultra 2)
        • Apple's description of the feature — support.apple.com/…
        • FDA Clears Apple Watch for Hypertension Notifications — www.macobserver.com/… & Canada Approves Apple Watch Hypertension Alerts — www.macobserver.com/…

      • New Apple watches get Sleep Scores

        • How Sleep Score works on Apple Watch with watchOS 26 — appleinsider.com/…
        • What Older Apple Watches are Compatible with the New Sleep Score? — www.macobserver.com/… (All Ultras, Series 6+ & SE 2)

      • Apple Watch Series 11 hides hypertension monitoring & better battery in a familiar shell — appleinsider.com/…

        • Apple Expands Apple Watch 11 With Bold Color Palette — www.macobserver.com/…
        • Apple Watch Series 11 review roundup: Battery life is the biggest benefit — appleinsider.com/…

      • Apple Watch Ultra 3 brings bigger screen, better battery and new health tricks — www.cultofmac.com/…

        • Review: Apple Watch Ultra 3 vs Apple Watch Ultra 2 — Same body, better screen — appleinsider.com/…
        • Apple Watch Ultra 3 review roundup: excellent and much-needed upgrade — appleinsider.com/…

      • Apple Watch SE 3 refreshed with modern design, features, and budget-friendly price — appleinsider.com/…

        • First SE watch with always-on display
        • Review: Apple Watch SE 3 is all the smartwatch you need — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • Related: There are an incredible amount of new Apple Watch bands with new colors and styles — appleinsider.com/…

    • iPhones

      • The A19 chips add hardware to dramatically boost security on all this year's new iPhone models — appleinsider.com/…

        • Full details: Memory Integrity Enforcement: A complete vision for memory safety in Apple devices — security.apple.com/…
        • Related: A19 Pro vs A18 Pro: What Actually Changed — www.macobserver.com/…

      • New iPhones use Apple N1 wireless chip—and we’ll probably start seeing it everywhere — arstechnica.com/…(Apple's own WiFi + bluetooth chip)

      • Related: iPhone Satellite Features Remain Free for Another Year — tidbits.com/…

      • iPhone 17

        • Center Stage camera turns iPhone 17 into super selfie machine — www.cultofmac.com/…

        • Analysis: iPhone 17 Camera: What’s New and Why It Matters — www.macobserver.com/…

          Specs sound nice, but the real win is in everyday use. Photos taken at night look cleaner without the grain that older iPhones struggled with. Motion blur is reduced, so kids, pets, or street scenes come out sharp. Video feels steadier, making it easier to capture moments without extra gear.

        • Reviews:

          • Apple's base iPhone 17 grows up with a better screen & improved cameras — appleinsider.com/…
          • Screen and camera upgrades make iPhone 17 Apple’s best base model ever — www.cultofmac.com/…

        • iPhone 17 review roundup — the best iPhone for almost everyone — appleinsider.com/…

      • iPhone 17 Pro is here with hugely improved cooling & unibody frame — appleinsider.com/…

        • Apple “started from scratch” to design all-new iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max — arstechnica.com/…

        • iPhone 17 Pro Only Comes in Three Colors, With No Black or White Option — www.macobserver.com/… (Comes in bright orange, dark blue, and grey)

        • iPhone 17 Pro Price goes up by $100 but base storage doubles — www.macobserver.com/… & iPhone 17 Pro Max Becomes the First 2TB iPhone — www.macobserver.com/…

        • Ceramic Shield 2 Explained: What’s New? — www.macobserver.com/…

          This second generation is engineered to solve the two biggest real-world complaints about smartphone screens: scratches and glare.

        • Apple Announces Final Cut Camera 2.0 with Support for ProRes RAW and Genlock — www.macstories.net/…

          • Related Analysis: iPhone 17 Pro: All Filmmaker Features Explained — www.macobserver.com/…

        • Why Apple Traded Titanium for Aluminum on iPhone 17 Pro — www.macobserver.com/…

          Here’s the deal: the A19 Pro chip is clearly built for sustained performance, not just flashy peak speeds. To keep that thing humming during a long 4K ProRes shoot or a heavy gaming session, you have to get heat out. And let’s be real, titanium is an insulator. It looks cool, but it traps heat. Aluminum, on the other hand, is fantastic at heat dissipation.

        • iPhone 17 Pro teardown reveals vapor chamber, explains scratches — appleinsider.com/…

          Overall, the iPhone 17 Pro is deemed to be marginally less repairable than the iPhone Air, but it still receives a provisional repairability score of 7 out of 10.

        • Reviews:

          • Two Weeks With the iPhone 17 Pro: The Best of the Best — www.macobserver.com/…
          • iPhone 17 Pro Camera Review: Rule of Three — www.lux.camera/… ) (Excellent long-form review, and cameras look great!)
          • Apple iPhone 17 Pro review: Come for the camera, stay for the battery — arstechnica.com/…
          • iPhone 17 Pro is a powerhouse without functional compromise [Review] — www.cultofmac.com/…

        • iPhone 17 Pro & iPhone 17 Pro Max review roundup — fast, excellent, and orange — appleinsider.com/…

      • iPhone Air Announced: Apple’s Thinnest iPhone Ever With Titanium Build, A19 Pro, and a $999 Starting Price — www.macobserver.com/…

        • Contrary to what many thought, the iPhone Air is incredibly strong — Jerry Rig Everything on youtube.com/…

        • eSim only!

          • Related: Apple C1X modem promises 2x faster speeds and 30% more efficiency — www.cultofmac.com/…
          • iPhone Air delayed in China over eSIM regulations — appleinsider.com/…

        • Apple’s Thinnest iPhone Ever… Is Actually Repairable? iPhone Air Teardown — iFixIt on youtube.com/… (yes, 7/10)

        • How Apple made iPhone Air’s USB-C port ultra-thin (and better) — www.cultofmac.com/… (3D-printed Titanium )

        • MagSafe battery resurrected, gives up to 40 hours of use to iPhone Air — appleinsider.com/…

          • MagSafe Battery for iPhone Air absolutely does not fit properly on anything else — appleinsider.com/…
          • Apple may have slipped the iPhone Air’s battery into its MagSafe pack — www.cultofmac.com/…

        • Analysis:

          • Why you shouldn’t worry about iPhone Air battery life — www.cultofmac.com/…

            • Not based on first-hand experience, but interesting comparisons to older model phones — the Air last 35% longer than 14 & 15, and 17% longer than 14 & 15 pro!

          • Why the iPhone 17 Air Camera Stands Apart from the Pro and Base Models — www.macobserver.com/…

            The Air replaces multiple visible lenses with a unified 48MP Fusion camera that uses sensor-level tricks and heavy image processing to give you flexible framing, reliable low-light shots, and pro-grade video in a thinner chassis.

          • iPhone Air vs 17 Pro: Differences That Matter — www.macobserver.com/…

            The Air is the thinnest iPhone Apple has ever made, designed for people who want lightness and elegance above all. The Pro is bulkier, heavier, and built for power users who care about cameras, battery, and sustained performance.

        • Review: If you touch an iPhone Air, you’ll want to buy it immediately — www.cultofmac.com/…

        • iPhone Air review roundup: Slim but not perfect — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple’s September 2025 Event: All the New Accessories — www.macstories.net/…

      • TechWoven Cases, Bumper Cases, Clear Cases & new colours of Silicone Cases
      • Cross-body strap
      • Beats iPhone 17 Pro Kickstand case

    • Every New Apple Intelligence Feature Announced at Apple’s Awe Dropping Event — www.macobserver.com/… (Mostly small things, peppered throughout the line, and not called out as a single whole)

    • Overall Analysis: Thinking through Apple’s September 9 announcements — sixcolors.com/…

      "This year, Apple is more or less abandoning ProMotion and always-on as iPhone Pro differentiators. That means habitual buyers of the lower-end phones will be getting a really substantial improvement when they next update their phones! … Apple has also chosen not to skimp on its new selfie camera … Similarly, the base iPhone’s ultrawide camera joins its main camera at 48MP … the big camera difference between the [regular and pro] models really is the lack of a third telephoto lens. … Apple doesn’t like to just come out and say, “Welp, prices are higher now.” The company places an inordinate amount of pride into releasing upgraded products at identical price points. But this year, it raised iPhone prices, sort of, kind of. Start with the iPhone Air, which begins at $999, a slot that was previously occupied by the iPhone Pro and a full $100 more expensive than the iPhone Plus, which it’s replacing in the product line. … Then there’s the iPhone 17 Pro, which now starts at $1099, up from the $999 starting price introduced with the iPhone X. Apple has gone to great lengths to point out that the $1099 price is the same as the similarly-configured iPhone 16 Pro model last year, because the iPhone 17 Pro has 256GB of base storage, and the iPhone 16 Pro started at 128GB." — Jason Snell

  3. New versions of Apple’s software platforms are available today — Apple PR

    • OS 26.0.1 Updates Fix Early Bugs — tidbits.com/…

    • Nice one-stop-shop big-picture overview: Apple Brings 200 Documented Changes Across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe — www.macobserver.com/…

    • The improved parental controls announced earlier in the year have gone live with these OS updates — Apple PR & appleinsider.com/…

    • Analysis: the best considered critique of Liquid Glass I've seen: On Liquid Glass — pxlnv.com/… (long read)

    • Spatial widgets add a new dimension to Apple Vision Pro with visionOS 26, available now — appleinsider.com/…

      • Everything new in visionOS 26: Spatial Widgets and 15 more new features — www.cultofmac.com/…

        • The other most significant new feature is better personas

      • Reviews:

        • visionOS 26 review: a necessary evolution in need of new hardware — appleinsider.com/…

          Apple made several quality-of-life upgrades to how visionOS works and presents itself to users … Apple Vision Pro isn't being held back by the M2, but the edge cases are starting to show up.

        • visionOS 26: The MacStories Review — www.macstories.net/…

          visionOS 26 keeps [the] rapid development going with a ton of new features, improvements, and capabilities that make Vision Pro even more powerful and enjoyable to use.

    • tvOS 26 is out now with karaoke mode, redesign, and big sound upgrades — appleinsider.com/…

      • tvOS 26 review: High on polish, light on new features for Apple TV — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple Releases watchOS 26 With Liquid Glass Design and Health Tools — www.macobserver.com/…

      • Everything new in watchOS 26: Workout Buddy and 15 other features — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • watchOS 26: The MacStories Review — www.macstories.net/…

        Liquid Glass on the Apple Watch is fine. It’s not adding anything useful, nor is it taking anything away … the Smart Stack is gaining even more utility in the form of Smart Stack hints, which appear as small icons at the bottom of your watch face.

    • macOS Tahoe with Liquid Glass, Clipboard History, and more is now available — appleinsider.com/…

      • Excellent overview: Everything new in macOS 26 Tahoe: Supercharged Spotlight and 40+ other features — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • How to Use Clipboard History on macOS Tahoe — www.macobserver.com/…

      • macOS Tahoe is getting a new Repair Assistant for part calibration and pairing — appleinsider.com/…

      • Support for FireWire Removed from macOS 26 Tahoe — tidbits.com/…

      • Reviews:

        • The most detailed review I've seen: macOS 26 Tahoe: The MacStories Review — www.macstories.net/…

        • macOS 26 Tahoe: The Ars Technica review — arstechnica.com/…

        • macOS Tahoe review — a strong update, just not for the reasons you expect — appleinsider.com/…

          Liquid Glass will briefly startle you, but then it's the new features in macOS Tahoe that make this a significant and a significantly useful upgrade … You even very, very soon wonder how you put up with the old macOS, the new one is so much better.

        • macOS 26 Tahoe review: Power under glass — sixcolors.com/…

          macOS 26 Tahoe is two things at once: It’s the broadest and most productivity-focused update for macOS in years, while also taking collateral damage from Apple’s broader design ambitions on its other platforms. If you’re worried about upgrading to macOS 26 Tahoe because of Apple’s 'liquid glass' design, don’t be—it’s mostly a minor reskinning that doesn’t really change how the Mac works … I have found macOS Tahoe to be perfectly usable, and there are moments of beauty separated by long stretches of banality … it sure feels like Apple is building a new vision of how the menu bar works, with old-school Menu Extras joined by individual controls as well as user-created submenus full of controls. … What you should consider, though, are the ways that macOS Tahoe offers new power features for Mac users. The new Spotlight features, including clipboard history, are huge. Shortcuts automations and access to AI models open up all sorts of new possibilities. The new Control Center suggests that Apple has figured out how to embrace menu bar management for the first time.

    • Apple releases iOS 26 with Liquid Glass and more intelligence — appleinsider.com/…

      • Everything new in iOS 26: Liquid Glass and 70+ new features — www.cultofmac.com/…

      • A fun video tour of some of the notable new features form Joanna Stern — WSJ on youtu.be/…

      • How the iPhone Camera App Changed in iOS 26 (and How to Use It) — www.macobserver.com/… & iPhone 16 to Get Bright Photographic Style in iOS 26 Update — www.macobserver.com/…

      • What is the Preview App in iOS 26? How to use — www.macobserver.com/…

      • Inside iOS 26 - How to add free custom ringtones to your iPhone — appleinsider.com/…

      • Boarding Pass Live Activities Arrive in Apple Wallet with iOS 26 — www.macobserver.com/… (looks very useful, but needs airlines to update their apps to use new APIs)

      • New Apple Intelligence features are available today — Apple PR

        • Visual Intelligence Explained: Unlocking the Power of Your Device’s Camera — www.macobserver.com/… (now works on any image, including screenshots)

          • Apple Intelligence now leans on Google for visual search — www.macobserver.com/…

        • How to Enable and Use Call Screening in iOS 26 — www.macobserver.com/…

        • iOS 26 Hold Assist: What It Is and How to Use It — www.macobserver.com/…

        • What is Adaptive Power Mode in iOS 26: Compatibility, Features, and Performance — www.macobserver.com/…

        • Siri just got 5 secret iOS 26 upgrades and they’re actually useful — www.macobserver.com/… (nothing dramatic, but nice little quality-of-life updates)

        • Apple’s Foundation Models framework unlocks new app experiences powered by Apple Intelligence — www.apple.com/… (new APIs, so will take time for apps to leverage this new capability)

      • Apple has finally explained why battery life can be different after an OS update — appleinsider.com/… (the phone has some house-keeping to do, so the first day will be abnormally hard on battery life)

      • Reviews:

        • The most detailed feature-by-feature review I've read: iOS and iPadOS 26: The MacStories Review — www.macstories.net/…

        • iOS 26 review: A practical, yet playful, update — arstechnica.com/… & Reviewing iOS 26 for power users: Reminders, Preview, and more — arstechnica.com/…

        • iOS 26 review: Smart, glassy, but waiting on Siri — appleinsider.com/…

          Siri delays haunt an otherwise excellent upgrade … ['liquid glass' is] an aesthetic that works well, and Apple has certainly worked hard to perfect it. Expect more tweaks in the future as Apple deals with the inevitable complaints, but it's landed in a good position for the operating system's release … Overall, iOS 26 is a great update for most users.

        • iOS 26 Review: Through a glass, liquidly — sixcolors.com/…

          "… worth noting that almost all of the iOS 26 features that Apple demoed during its WWDC keynote this year are available in this initial version … Overall, iOS 26’s quality of life improvements are what are likely to resonate the most" — Dan Moren

    • AirPods under iOS 26: iOS 26 AirPods Update: Every New Feature You Get — www.macobserver.com/…

      • Live Translation (on AirPods Pro 2 & 3 & AirPods 4 with ANC)
      • Better playback control including automatic sleep detection and better control over when audio auto-switches to other devices
      • How to use AirPods as an iPhone camera control — www.cultofmac.com/… (remove shutter, off by default)
      • Some audio quality improvements

    • CarPlay under iOS 26:

      • iOS 26 CarPlay Widgets Explained: How To Use Them — www.macobserver.com/…
      • iOS 26 CarPlay Video Streaming: How It Works and What to Expect — www.macobserver.com/…
      • CarPlay in iOS 26: The MacStories Review — www.macstories.net/…

    • iPadOS 26 arrives with controversial Liquid Glass and Mac-like multitasking — appleinsider.com/… & Apple Launches iPadOS 26 With Major Productivity Upgrades — www.macobserver.com/…

      • iPadOS 26 review: A computer? — sixcolors.com/…

        *“It’s like a weight has been lifted from the soul of the iPad. It remains a very nice device to use in full-screen mode with all the simplicity attendant to that mode. But via a single tap, it can also transform into a multi-window, multitasking device that’s appropriate for the Mac-class hardware underpinning today’s iPads. … Apple’s new windowing system is great, embracing all the things that make the Mac work without forcing it on people who don’t want it. The improvements to Files, support for local recording, and the new background tasks Live Activity help create an iPad that just feels more ready for professional productivity tasks.“ — Jason Snell

Quick Stories

  • Apple refreshes Beats lineup with Powerbeats Fit — www.macobserver.com/… & Compact new Powerbeats Fit earbuds add comfort and durability — www.cultofmac.com/…

    • Beats Powerbeats Fit review: Compact earbuds ideal for workouts — appleinsider.com/…

  • Adobe Brings Premiere Video Editor to iPhone — www.macobserver.com/… (and iPad!)

  • Apple launches new project to protect and restore California redwood forest — Apple PR

  • Apple's fourth quarter 2025 earnings call to take place on October 30 — appleinsider.com/…

item.title: LTA 146: October 2025
item.dc:creator: bbusschots
item.content:encoded:
Panel:

  • Bart Busschots (host) - @bartb.ie

The show starts with a few quick followups on stories from last month before catching up with the month's regulatory, legal, and HR news. That's followed by a quick look at Apple's services news for the month. There are just two main stories, Apple's Q4 2025 earnings, and Apple's M5 hardware refreshes. The show wraps up with a few other quick stories that made the news in October.

You'll find detailed show notes below the fold, and if you enjoy this free show, please consider clicking on the donate button at the top of the left side bar - the show is free for you to listen to, but not for Bart to Produce!

[audio mp3="https://media.lets-talk.ie/lta/lta146.mp3"]

Updates & Followup

Quick updates to long-running stories the show continues to track, and to stories covered in recent shows.

  • The ICEBlock story got a little more icky early in the month:

    • ‘Apple Is Better Than This’: Ex-Apple Exec Condemns ICEBlock Removal — www.macobserver.com/… (Wiley Hodges, 20 year veteran)

    • Apple Banned an App That Simply Archived Videos of ICE Abuses — www.404media.co/…

      "Speaking to 404 Media, the app’s administrator, identified only as Mark, said Eyes Up was designed to promote transparency. 'Our goal is government accountability. We aren’t even doing real-time tracking,' he said. Mark asked to be identified by his first name to avoid potential retaliation. He argued that the decision reflected political discomfort rather than legitimate safety concerns. 'I think the administration is just embarrassed by how many incriminating videos we have,' he added." — from TMO's summary (www.macobserver.com/…)

    • Apple also removed DeICER, a civic-reporting app used to log immigration enforcement activity, and their justification was perverse: "[the app's] purpose is to provide location information about law enforcement officers that can be used to harm such officers individually or as a group" — daringfireball.net/…

      "There’s not one story about any of these apps being used to harm ICE agents. And even if such an attack happened, that wouldn’t imply it’s the purpose of these apps. The purpose of these apps is to protect people — citizens and non-citizens alike — from ICE." — John Gruber

  • Apple & Tim Cook continue to pander to President Trump, but it seems to be paying off

    • Apple amongst US tech giants backing Trump's White House ballroom reno — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple CEO Tim Cook dines with Trump in Tokyo — appleinsider.com/…

      • The event was trying to drum up investments in the US
      • At Tokyo event, Trump says Tim Cook has “done more than the entire group” — www.macobserver.com/… (Less pledged at the event than Apple has pledged to spend itself in the US)

    • Presidents Trump Xi agree to reduce tariffs in exchange for more rare earths — appleinsider.com/… & www.cultofmac.com/…

  • Rollouts continue for Apple's recently released products and features:

    • Apple Watch Hypertension Alerts Roll Out in Canada and Singapore — www.macobserver.com/… (and Bahrain)
    • iPhone and Apple Watch will soon support Emergency SOS via satellite in Mexico — www.cultofmac.com/…
    • Apple’s sleek iPhone Air finally touches down in China — www.cultofmac.com/…

Regulatory Rundown

  • US States continue to roll out age verification laws:

    • Apple sets new Rules for Texas under State’s Age Verification Law — www.macobserver.com/…

      If you create a new Apple account in Texas next year, you’ll have to confirm whether you’re 18 or older. Anyone under 18 must join a Family Sharing group, and parents will need to approve every app download, purchase, and in-app transaction.

      • Note that this law applies to all apps, not just those aimed as adults
      • Apple Warns of Privacy Risks as Texas Age Verification Law Takes Effect — cyberinsider.com/…

    • Apple faces new App Store age-verification rule in California — www.macobserver.com/…

      • Does not have privacy implications because it does not force everyone to send copies of their government IDs to private companies (in the hope they never loose them)
      • Focuses on requiring app store owners to provide parents with the tools they need, and to honour the settings parents set
      • Should be easy for Apple to comply with

  • Apple takes EU to court, calling Digital Markets Act “intrusive and unlawful” — www.macobserver.com/…

    “the DMA requires security and protection for consumers. But the enforcement of this law has seen the EU demanding Apple make changes that unquestionably do undermine or even remove such security” — Good summary from appleinsider.com/…

  • Apple warns it could disable App Tracking Transparency across Europe — www.macobserver.com/…

    • Opinion: EU ad companies are gaining traction claiming forcing actual consent is anti-competitive, this is the perfect example of some in the EU perverting valuable protections into protectionism)
    • Related: Apple met EU officials 76 times while spending $8M on Lobbying — www.macobserver.com/…

  • UK follows EU path, labels Apple and Google as ‘Strategic Market Status’ Firms — www.macobserver.com/… (nothing will happen in the short term)

  • Apple has lost a massive $2Bn class action suit in the UK, the Competition Appeal Tribunal has ruled that Apple's closed ecosystem artificially inflated prices — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple has already announced it's intention to appeal — www.macobserver.com/…

      “A separate hearing next month will set the damages method and consider Apple’s request to appeal.”

    • Opinion: John Gruber — daringfireball.net/…

      Apple has approached all this regulatory conflict from a perspective that they’re right, and the regulators are wrong … But even if Apple is correct about that, at some point, after being handed loss after loss in rulings from courts and regulatory bodies around the globe, shouldn’t they change their strategy and start trying to offer their own concessions, rather than wait for bureaucrat-designed concessions to be forced upon them?

Legal Latest

  • Apple -v- John Prosser: things get interesting!

    • Apple pushes court to rule against Jon Prosser after missed deadline — www.macobserver.com/… (No formal reply to the suit)
    • The court agrees: Apple's leaker lawsuit marches on after Jon Prosser misses deadlines — appleinsider.com/…
    • Jon Prosser says he’s been in ‘active communication’ with Apple over lawsuit — www.theverge.com/… (A short and very vague statement that suggests Apple is not being honest, but doesn't actually contradict Apple's court filings)
    • Apple clarified that Prossser had contacted them, but not replied to the actual suit as required — appleinsider.com/…
    • Apple iOS 26 leaker's court filing rolls Jon Prosser under the bus — appleinsider.com/… (Michael Ramacciotti did file his reply properly, and he's denying he colluded with Prosser)

  • Apple -v- Epic: oral Arguments were held in the federal appeals court in Apple's case seeking the reversal of the recent contempt runing that forced it to allow linkouts for payment in the US — appleinsider.com/…](https://appleinsider.com/articles/25/10/23/judges-seems-sympathetic-to-apple-in-app-store-appeal-hearing)

    The panel of judges didn't immediately rule on the matter. A decision is expected in the coming months, but probably not in 2025.

  • It was a good month from Apple in US courts, as lots of cases agree with the company and reject cases:

    • Apple, Amazon Lawsuit Over iPhone and iPad Prices Dismissed — www.macobserver.com/…

      The case unraveled when Floyd decided to withdraw from the lawsuit. Instead of informing the court, his attorneys told U.S. District Judge Kymberly Evanson that Floyd had become “difficult to reach” while they searched for new plaintiffs. This misrepresentation prompted the judge to revisit earlier rulings.

    • 'Alarming errors' lead to App Store class action decertification — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple fends off part of AirPods Pro defect lawsuit, judge narrows scope — appleinsider.com/…

      Judge Wise dropped the claim that Apple made unfair profits but let the rest of the case move forward.

  • Siri's voice recording scandal lives on in new French probe — appleinsider.com/…

    • French prosecutors have launched a formal investigation
    • This dates back to 2019 before Apple tweaked their policies around human review of Siri interactions

Apple HR & Acquisition News

  • Meta steals top Apple AI exec behind ‘answer engine’ project — www.cultofmac.com/… (Ke Yang)

  • NPR’s Podcasting Lead Leaves for Reported Role at Apple — www.macobserver.com/… (Collin Campbell, was NPR SVP of Podcasting Strategy & Franchise Development)

  • Apple reshapes health, fitness and Apple Watch leadership as Jeff Williams nears retirement — www.cultofmac.com/…

    As part of the rejig, Eddy Cue will oversee the health and fitness team … the watchOS division will come under Craig Federighi, the current head of software engineering.

Apple Services & Original Content Highlights

  • Apple's gaming efforts continue apace:

    • Build dynasties in Football Manager 26 Touch, arriving November 4 on Apple Arcade — Apple PR (November 4th)
    • NBA 2K26 brings breathtaking basketball action to Apple Arcade — www.cultofmac.com/… (I'm picking up a sports theme!)
    • EA resurrects nearly 20-year-old 'MySims' games for Apple Arcade this November — appleinsider.com/…
    • Apple joins advisory board for 'The Game Awards' — appleinsider.com/…

  • Apple TV:

    • Apple TV+ Rebranded to Just Apple TV — tidbits.com/…

      • As well as the new name there is also a more colourful new logo — sixcolors.com/…
      • Opinion: John Gruber — daringfireball.net/… (good insights I agree with)
      • Opinion: Jason Snell suggests re-naming the Apple TV devices to HomePods — sixcolors.com/…

    • 'F1 The Movie' crosses the finish line, hits Apple TV December 12 — appleinsider.com/…

      • Related: Apple Is the Exclusive New Broadcast Partner for Formula 1 in the U.S. — daringfireball.net/…

    • MLS playoff matches free to all Apple TV subscribers — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple TV and Peacock bundle starts at $15/month, available on Oct. 20 — arstechnica.com/…

    • Apple TV Apprenticeships: A Gateway to Production Careers — www.macobserver.com/… (partnership with the UK National Film and Television School AKA the NFTS)

    • Related: A surprisingly frank long-form interview with Eddie Cue: The Town with Matthew Belloni: Apple’s True Intentions in Hollywood — overcast.fm/…

  • West Virginia becomes latest state to allow driver’s licenses in Apple Wallet — www.cultofmac.com/…

Main Stories

  1. Apple's Q4 2025 Earnings — Apple PR

    • Charts: Apple caps off high-flying fiscal year with Q4 record — sixcolors.com/…
    • This is Tim: Complete transcript of Apple’s Q4 2025 financial call — sixcolors.com/…
    • All the records Apple said it broke in Q4 2025 — appleinsider.com/…
    • An excellent short summary with some important context: Apple Reports Strong Q4 2025 Results — daringfireball.net/…
    • Services, Mac, and iPhone Drive Apple’s Q4 2025 Quarterly Revenue Record — tidbits.com/…
    • iPhone revenue falls short of Wall Street expectations, but it doesn't matter — appleinsider.com/… (Wall St. expectations, not actual guidance from Apple or internal targets that have leaked)
    • Apple posts record revenues — and predicts the best is yet to come — www.cultofmac.com/…
    • Hits from tariffs continue, Apple to pay $1.4 billion more in 2025 holiday quarter — appleinsider.com/…
    • Cook: More partnerships coming soon to enhance Apple Intelligence — appleinsider.com/…
    • Apple Intelligence-enhanced Siri is on track for a 2026 debut — appleinsider.com/…

  2. M5 Hardware Refreshes (now shipping — Apple PR)

    1. Apple unleashes M5, the next big leap in AI performance for Apple silicon — Apple PR

      • Apple’s new M5 chip lands with 4× AI GPU boost, faster Neural Engine, and higher memory bandwidth — www.macobserver.com/…
      • Apple’s new M5 Chip Makes Mac Gaming a Reality with Ray Tracing — www.macobserver.com/…

    2. Apple unveils new 14‑inch MacBook Pro powered by the M5 chip, delivering the next big leap in AI for the Mac — Apple PR

      • Apple Quietly Made the Best Laptop Speakers Even Better — www.macobserver.com/…

      • New 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 ships without a charger across Europe — www.macobserver.com/…

        • Analysis: A lot of the reporting on the charger thing is missing important nuance — www.macobserver.com/…

          Legal language does not forbid multiple charging methods on the device itself, which explains why MacBook Pro supports both MagSafe and USB-C. Legal language also does not forbid bundling a charger for free, as long as buyers can pick the version without it. The core requirement is choice at the point of sale, not a penalty for including an adapter.

      • iFixit teardown shows small repair wins in M5 MacBook Pro — www.macobserver.com/…

      • Review Roundup: First reviews call M5 MacBook Pro a beast — but M4 owners can skip this upgrade — www.cultofmac.com/…

    3. Apple introduces the powerful new iPad Pro with the M5 chip — Apple PR

      • New iPad Pro arrives with M5 speed, Wi-Fi 7, and Apple's C1X modem — appleinsider.com/…
      • M5 iPad Pro Display gets 1 Nit Minimum Brightness — www.macobserver.com/…
      • M5 iPad Pro is Apple's most repairable yet, but roadblocks remain — appleinsider.com/…
      • Review roundup: The best tablet gets better — appleinsider.com/…

    4. Apple launches M5 powered Vision Pro with new Dual Knit Band — sixcolors.com/…

      • Apple Vision Pro Dual Knit Band and more accessories hit Apple Store — appleinsider.com/…
      • Tariff Fallout: M5 Apple Vision Pro production moved to Vietnam amid supply chain shift — appleinsider.com/…
      • Review roundup: faster, comfier, still not for everyone — appleinsider.com/…
      • Related: Apple releases new Vision Pro Developer Strap for faster Mac connections — www.macobserver.com/… ("delivers data transfer speeds of up to 20 Gbps when connected to a Mac")

    5. Related: Apple adds a black Magic Keyboard option for the iPad Air — appleinsider.com/…

Quick Stories

  • Apple Clips social video app killed after eight years — appleinsider.com/…

    • Apple's support article for users: Save your Clips videos — support.apple.com/…

  • Beats Solo 4 and Solo Buds both gain Walmart-exclusive color options — appleinsider.com/… ('Drenched Gray')

  • Apple expands renewable energy projects across Europe — Apple PR

    • Some insightful analysis from Apple Insider — appleinsider.com/…

Legend
